post.summary: Remind the customer of a request
post.description: Send a waiting customer request's email again, to the same verified recipient, with the same content. You can remind a request at most once every 24 hours. A reminder changes nothing else: the request keeps its deadline and the case keeps its status. Each reminder is logged on the case as a CUSTOMER_REQUEST event with action `reminded`. The response's `delivery_status` is how this reminder's delivery ended: SENT, SIMULATED (the email was not sent), or UNKNOWN (the email might have been accepted; it is not sent again automatically). `next_reminder_at` is when you can remind this request again. Returns 409 with a `reason` when the customer no longer has the request to answer, and 429 with `retry_at` and a `Retry-After` header when the request was reminded in the last 24 hours. Requires `write:cases`.

parameters.name: organization_id
parameters.description: Organization UUID.

parameters.name: application_id
parameters.description: Application UUID.

parameters.name: case_uuid
parameters.description: Case UUID.

parameters.name: request_uuid
parameters.description: Customer request UUID, from the case's request list.

  -H 'x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY'

200.description: The reminder was recorded and its email sent.

delivery_status.description: How this reminder's delivery ended. SIMULATED: the email was not sent. UNKNOWN: the email might have been accepted; it is not sent again automatically.

next_reminder_at.description: When you can remind this request again: `reminded_at` plus 24 hours.

example: Customer messages require an active case without a pending resolution.

403.description: The caller lacks the required cases permission.

404.description: The request or case is unavailable for this caller.

409.description: The request no longer waits on the customer, so there is nothing to remind them of. `reason` says why: `answered` (the customer responded), `cancelled`, `expired`, `closed` (the case was resolved after the request went out, even if it was reopened since), `not_actionable` (a review-in-progress update asks nothing), `not_delivered` (the first email has not gone out), or `contact_unavailable` (the verified email is no longer available).

example.detail: This request no longer waits on the customer, so there is nothing to remind them of.

429.description: The request was already reminded in the last 24 hours. `retry_at` and the `Retry-After` header say when you can remind it again.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before you can remind this request again.

post.description:
Render the email the person receives when you set a session to `Approved` or `Declined` with `send_email: true`, without changing the session or sending anything. The response shows the subject and HTML exactly as they are sent, the recipient, the sender, the language, and whether confirming the change sends the email at all (`will_be_sent`, `not_sent_reason`).

The recipient is the person's own address: the one they verified in an email verification step of the flow, else the one given in `contact_details` when the session was created. The sender is your application's verified sender domain when white label applies (`sender_kind: customer`), else Didit's sender (`sender_kind: didit`).

To send exactly what you previewed, call [Update Session Status](/sessions-api/update-status) with the same `new_status`, `send_email: true`, `email_address` set to `recipient`, `email_language` set to `language` and `email_preview_token` set to `preview_token`. The receipt expires after 15 minutes. When the recipient, language, session status, sender or email changed since the preview, the update returns `409` before anything changes; preview again and confirm with the new receipt.

Works for User Verification (KYC) and Business Verification (KYB) sessions in `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review`, `Kyc Expired`, `Abandoned` or `Resubmitted` status. The status check runs before body validation. Requires the `write:sessions` privilege; a scoped API key needs write access to decisions. Responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`: treat them as sensitive verification content.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: UUID of the verification session. Accepts both user (KYC) and business (KYB) session IDs.

new_status.description: The decision whose email you want to preview.

email_language.description: Language of the email, the same default as Update Session Status. A language that is not offered falls back to English; `language` in the response says which one is used.

Approved.summary: Preview the Approved email in English

Declined in Spanish.summary: Preview the Declined email in Spanish

200.description: Preview only. The session is unchanged and no email is sent.

Cache-Control.description: Always `no-store`: the preview carries verification content and must not be cached.

recipient.description: The address the email goes to. An empty string when no address is known for the person: then no email can be sent and `preview_token` is empty too. Pass it as `email_address` when you confirm.

recipient_source.description: Where `recipient` comes from. `email_verification`: the address the person verified in an email verification step of the flow. `contact_details`: the address given in `contact_details` when the session was created. An empty string when there is no address.

sender.description: The `From` header the email goes out with.

sender_kind.description: `customer`: the email goes out from your application's verified sender domain (white label). `didit`: it goes out from Didit's own sender.

subject.description: The subject line exactly as it is sent.
subject.example: Your verification has been approved in Example App

html.description: The email's HTML exactly as it is sent, with its logo embedded as a data URL. Render it in a sandboxed frame, never directly in your application DOM.

language.description: The language the email is written in. English (`en`) when the `email_language` you asked for is not offered.

will_be_sent.description: Whether confirming the change with `send_email: true` sends this email. `false` when `not_sent_reason` is set.

not_sent_reason.description: Why confirming would send no email, or `null` when it will be sent. `status_unchanged`: the session already has this status, so the update changes nothing and sends nothing. `notification_emails_disabled`: the session was created without `contact_details.send_notification_emails: true`, so no decision email goes to the address given in `contact_details`. `no_recipient`: no address is known for the person. `sandbox`: a sandbox session whose recipient has not opted into sandbox email delivery, so the send is only simulated.

preview_token.description: Signed receipt for this exact email, valid for 15 minutes. Pass it as `email_preview_token` to [Update Session Status](/sessions-api/update-status). An empty string when there is no recipient.

Will Be Sent.summary: The Approved email goes to the address verified in the flow

WebhookEvent.description: Supported webhook event name. Use these exact strings in `subscribed_events`; unsupported values are rejected.

WebhookSubscribedEvents.description: Event filter for this webhook destination. Didit delivers only webhooks whose event type exactly matches one of these values — there is no wildcard subscription. When sent, the list must contain at least one valid event (an explicit `[]` is rejected with 400); a destination whose list is empty (field omitted at create) receives nothing. On update the list is replaced wholesale, never merged.

request_id.description: Session id of the verification. A `Retry` send returns the same `request_id` as the original send. This id appears in the Business Console, is returned again by a finalized `POST /v3/phone/check/`, and can be passed to `GET /v3/session/{sessionId}/decision/`.

status.description: `Success` — OTP sent to a new verification. `Retry` — OTP re-sent for the pending verification created by a previous send. `Blocked` — the anti-fraud layer refused to send; the verification is immediately finalized as `Declined` and nothing is billed.

reason.description: Why a send was `Blocked` (e.g., `repeated_attempts`, `suspicious`, `spam`). `null` on `Success` and `Retry`.

vendor_data.description: Echo of the `vendor_data` stored on the session (from the first send).

metadata.description: Echo of the `metadata` stored on the session (from the first send).

request_id.description: On `Approved`/`Declined`: the session id of the matched verification — identical to the `request_id` returned by `POST /v3/phone/send/`. On `Failed` and `Expired or Not Found`: a random one-off UUID that cannot be looked up later.

status.description: `Approved` — correct code, no declining risk. `Declined` — terminal: a declining risk matched or the attempt budget (3) was exhausted. `Failed` — wrong code, attempts remaining. `Expired or Not Found` — no pending verification for this number in the last 5 minutes.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the outcome, including the number of attempts remaining after a wrong code.

phone.description: Full phone report. Present (non-null) only on finalized outcomes (`Approved`/`Declined`); `null` on `Failed` and absent on `Expired or Not Found`.

status.description: Final status of the phone verification. Matches the top-level `status` for finalized checks.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the number.

is_virtual.description: `true` when the line type is virtual (`voip`, `isp`, or `vpn`).

verification_method.description: Channel that actually delivered the OTP once delivery is confirmed (e.g., `whatsapp`, `sms`); until then, the requested channel.

verified_at.description: When the correct code was entered. `null` if the verification was never approved.

workflow_label.description: Display name for the workflow (max 50 characters).

is_default.description: Set this workflow as the default for new sessions.

status.description: Controls versioning. Omit to update the current version in place (drafts auto-publish). `published` on an already-published version creates and returns a NEW version. `draft` is only valid while the version is still a draft.

feature.description: Feature to run. Use the uppercase values shown here.

config.description: Feature-specific settings. For `QUESTIONNAIRE`, include `questionnaire_uuid` with the `questionnaire_id` returned by the questionnaire create endpoint. For `OCR`, `methods` selects which ID Verification methods each country may use (document capture, non-doc lookup against a government or other authoritative source, and digital identity wallets); omit it and every country is document capture only. For `SIGNATURE`, see [Electronic Signature settings](/management-api/workflows/feature-configs#electronic-signature): `signature_level` accepts `aes` only for now, and workflow documents and their fields are managed in the console, so through the API send documents and fields per session with `signature_documents_source: "session"`.

label.description: Optional internal label for this workflow node.

ReviewItem.description: One entry in a session's review / activity feed. Status changes carry `previous_status`, `new_status`, `previous_value`, `new_value`, and `changed_fields`; comments carry `comment` and (for Console comments) `mentioned_emails`; the remaining fields are `null` or empty when they do not apply to the activity type.

uuid.description: Unique identifier of this feed entry.

activity_type.description: What kind of activity this entry records. `STATUS_UPDATED` rows come from manual decisions (`PATCH /v3/session/{session_id}/update-status/`) and from entries added via `POST …/reviews/` (which default to this type even when no status is recorded). `COMMENT` rows come from Console reviewers; Console detail-page views are also stored as `COMMENT` rows flagged with `metadata.system_event = "DETAIL_VIEWED"`. The remaining types track data edits, file changes, tags, and AML monitoring activity. STATUS_UPDATED rows are also written by system actors (e.g. AML ongoing monitoring with actor_type SYSTEM, and automatic feature-status updates), not only by the update-status endpoint and manual review posts. `FEATURE_OVERRIDE_PENDING`, `FEATURE_OVERRIDE_APPLIED` and `FEATURE_OVERRIDE_CANCELLED` record an override of one check's status (`PATCH /v3/session/{session_id}/features/{node_id}/update-status/`): requested to wait for the flow to finish, applied, or cancelled. They carry the check's status in `previous_value` / `new_value` (`{"status": ...}`), leave `previous_status` and `new_status` `null`, and name the override in `metadata` (`feature_override_id`, `node_id`, `feature_model`, `forced`, `state`, `cancel_reason`). The entry for the request carries the reviewer's `comment`; an override applied when the flow finishes is recorded with `actor_type` `SYSTEM`.

actor_display.description: Human-readable author label, resolved in order: actor's full name → Console account identifier → local part of `actor_email` → `"API Client"` (for `API_KEY` actors) → `"System"` (for `SYSTEM` actors) → `"Unknown"`. Entries created via `POST …/reviews/` always display `"Unknown"` because that endpoint records no actor attribution.

actor_email.description: Email of the Console user who performed the action. `null` for API-key and system actors.

actor_type.description: Who performed the action: an API key, a Console user, or Didit itself (`SYSTEM`, e.g. AML ongoing monitoring). Entries created via `POST …/reviews/` carry the default `CONSOLE_USER` regardless of the caller.

new_status.description: Session status recorded by this entry (for status updates). `null` for comments and data-change entries.

previous_status.description: Status the session had before the change. Populated on `STATUS_UPDATED` entries written by the update-status endpoint; `null` on entries added via `POST …/reviews/`. Also populated on system-written STATUS_UPDATED rows.

comment.description: Free-text note attached to the entry, or `null`.

mentioned_emails.description: Console users `@email`-mentioned in the comment. Always empty for entries created via this API — mention processing is a Console-only feature.

previous_value.description: Snapshot of the changed data before the action, e.g. `{"status": "In Review"}` on a status change. `null` when nothing was changed.

new_value.description: Snapshot of the changed data after the action, e.g. `{"status": "Approved"}`. `null` when nothing was changed.

changed_fields.description: Names of the fields modified by this activity (e.g. `["status"]`). Empty for comments and for entries added via `POST …/reviews/`.

metadata.description: Extra context for system-generated entries. Console detail-page views carry `{"system_event": "DETAIL_VIEWED", "detail_type": "verification"}` so they can be filtered out of notification logic. `null` for ordinary entries.

created_at.description: When the entry was written, ISO 8601 UTC.

approved_phones.description: Verified phone numbers collected from this user's approved sessions, e.g. `["+14155551234"]`.

features.description: Aggregated per-feature status across all of this user's sessions. Possible keys: `ID_VERIFICATION`, `NFC`, `LIVENESS`, `FACE_MATCH`, `POA`, `QUESTIONNAIRE`, `EMAIL_VERIFICATION`, `PHONE`, `AML`, `IP_ANALYSIS`, `AGE_ESTIMATION`, `DATABASE_VALIDATION`. Possible values: `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review`, `Not Finished`, `Resub Requested`.

features_list.description: Same data as `features`, as an ordered array of `{feature, status}` objects.

last_session_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent session

last_activity_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent activity on this user (session, transaction, status change, data edit, etc.).

UserDetailItem.description: Full user detail. Extends UserListItem with metadata, comments, and updated_at.

metadata.description: Custom metadata JSON you attached to this user. Defaults to `{}`.

tags.description: Tag assignments. NOTE: on detail responses each entry is a tag *link* object (`{uuid, tag: {...}, added_by_email, added_by_name, created_at}`), unlike the flat `{uuid, name, color}` shape used on list responses.

uuid.description: UUID of the tag assignment (not the tag itself).

previous_value.description: Previous field values for PROFILE_UPDATED entries.

new_value.description: New field values for PROFILE_UPDATED entries.

changed_fields.description: Names of the fields changed by a PROFILE_UPDATED entry.

comments.description: Activity log and comments for this user (status changes, profile edits, manual notes).

didit_internal_id.description: Didit's stable internal UUID for this business.

vendor_data.description: Your unique identifier for this business (passed when creating sessions). This can be null when no vendor identifier was supplied.

display_name.description: Custom display name set by you

legal_name.description: Official legal name from registry or manual entry

effective_name.description: Best available name: display_name if set, otherwise legal_name

status.description: Lifecycle status of the business record (NOT a session status). `ACTIVE` is the default, `FLAGGED` marks it for manual attention, `BLOCKED` prevents new sessions for this `vendor_data`.

session_count.description: Total number of verification sessions for this business

features.description: Aggregated per-feature status across all of this business's KYB sessions. Currently the only key is `KYB` (the registry company check status). Possible values: `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review`, `Not Finished`, `Resub Requested`.

features_list.description: Same data as `features`, as an ordered array of `{feature, status}` objects.

last_session_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent session

last_activity_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent activity (status change, session update, etc.)

BusinessDetailItem.description: Full business detail. Extends BusinessListItem with metadata and updated_at.

metadata.description: Custom metadata JSON you attached to this business. Defaults to `{}`.

TransactionDetail.description: Full monitoring record for one transaction, as returned by `GET /v3/transactions/{transaction_id}/` and `POST /v3/transactions/`.

uuid.description: Didit-stable transaction identifier. Use as `{transaction_id}` for follow-up calls.

environment.description: Environment of the application that owns the transaction. A `sandbox` transaction is stored but never evaluated, screened, notified or billed, so its empty `rule_runs` means "not evaluated".

transaction_number.description: Application-scoped sequential transaction number shown in Console (e.g. `4123`).

txn_id.description: The `transaction_id` you supplied at create time (max 128 chars). Unique per application.

txn_date.description: When the transaction occurred (from `transaction_at`; defaults to submission time).

zone_id.description: IANA time zone identifier provided at create time.

transaction_type.description: Top-level category as stored: `finance`, `kyc`, `travelRule`, `userPlatformEvent`, `gamblingBet`, `gamblingLimitChange`, `gamblingBonusChange`, `auditTrailEvent`. Note multi-word values are echoed back in camelCase even when submitted in snake_case.

action_type.description: Sub-type within the category (e.g. `deposit`, `withdrawal`, `transfer`). Defaults to the category when not supplied.

direction.description: Direction relative to the subject. Stored uppercase regardless of the casing submitted (`in`/`out`/`inbound`/`outbound` are accepted on input).

status.description: Current monitoring verdict. Transactions are created `APPROVED`; rules may flip them to `IN_REVIEW`/`DECLINED` synchronously.

source.description: How the record originated: `LIVE` for transactions submitted through the API or SDK, `IMPORTED` for transactions loaded through the console import.

amount.description: Transaction amount as a decimal string with trailing zeros stripped (e.g. `"1500"`, `"0.5"`, `"0.123456789012345678"`). Up to 18 decimal places.

currency.description: Currency code of `amount`. Any ISO 4217 alphabetic code is accepted (e.g. `EUR`, `USD`, `NGN`), as is a crypto asset symbol (e.g. `BTC`). Prefer a currently-circulating code. Not every accepted code has an exchange rate: when none is available for the code (for example the ISO accounting unit `XSU`, or a crypto symbol Didit does not price), automatic conversion fails and `preferred_currency_amount` is returned null unless the request supplied a pre-converted `amount_in_default_currency`.

amount_in_default_currency.description: Pre-converted amount you supplied, as a decimal string with trailing zeros stripped.

preferred_currency_amount.description: `amount` converted to the application's preferred currency, when available.

payment_details.description: Free-text payment reference or memo from the submission.

payment_txn_id.description: External payment system reference (e.g. blockchain transaction hash) from `payment_reference_id`.

score.description: Risk score accumulated by rules (typically 0–100). Higher = riskier.

severity.description: Categorical risk severity set by rules/providers (`UNKNOWN`, `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, `CRITICAL`). `null` until something sets it.

vendor_data.description: Convenience copy of the applicant's `vendor_data`.

metadata.description: Snapshot of the `subject` and `counterparty` payloads as submitted at create time.

props.description: The `custom_properties` you supplied at create time. Each key is addressable in rule conditions as `custom_values.<key>`.

source.description: Whether the tag is a Didit preset or a custom tag.

tags.description: Tags attached to the transaction (manually or by rules).

role.description: Party role. The create endpoint assigns `APPLICANT` (the subject) and `COUNTERPARTY`.

kind.description: `USER`/`BUSINESS` parties link back to a Didit-owned entity via `vendor_data`. `EXTERNAL` parties have no Didit entity behind them.

vendor_data.description: Your internal user/business identifier.

country_code.description: Country code from the submitted `address.country` (typically ISO 3166-1 alpha-3).

dob.description: Date of birth from the submitted `date_of_birth`.

address.description: Address object as submitted. `{}` when omitted.

institution_info.description: Institution details as submitted. `{}` when omitted.

device.description: Normalized device context, including server-side IP enrichment under network_context (geolocation, VPN/data-center flags) when an IP was provided.

persistent_device_id.description: Stable cross-session device identifier (v2 fingerprint schema).

user_agent.description: Browser or app user agent string.

platform.description: Platform identifier (web, ios, android, macos, windows, linux).

os_family.description: Operating system family (e.g. iOS, Android, Windows).

session_id.description: Session identifier (stored in metadata).

network_context.description: Network context with IP address and geo-location.

ip_country_code.description: Geo-resolved country of the IP (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3).

external_party_snapshot.description: Frozen copy of the party data for `EXTERNAL` parties. `null` while the party is linked to a Didit user or business.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 over `type:account_id:issuing_country` — stable identifier to correlate reuse of the same instrument.

account_id.description: Account identifier (IBAN, wallet address, card token, …).

vendor_data.description: Your identifier for the owning user/business.

role.description: How this method was used in the transaction. The create endpoint assigns `SOURCE`/`DESTINATION` from the direction (outbound: subject = SOURCE; inbound: subject = DESTINATION).

payment_methods.description: Payment methods linked to the transaction.

documents.description: Files attached to the transaction from the console. `[]` when none.

file_url.description: Short-lived signed download URL; fetch it when needed rather than storing it.

activities.description: Activity log entries (creation, notes, manual reviews, status changes).

alerts.description: Alerts raised by rules and providers.

rule.description: UUID of the rule that ran.

matched.description: Whether the rule's conditions matched this transaction. A run is recorded only for matched rules, so live evaluations always carry `true`.

is_test.description: True when the rule ran in TEST mode (no effect on status/score).

score_delta.description: Score added by this rule's `add_score` actions.

status_target.description: Status set by a `change_status` action, if any.

action_summary.description: Summary of the actions the rule executed, joined with `; ` (e.g. `score +30; change_status:IN_REVIEW; add_tag:high_risk_country`). Parts: `score +N`, `change_status:<STATUS>`, `add_tag:<name>`, `add_note`, `add_to_list`, `open_case`. `null` when the rule executed no action.

metadata.description: Evaluation detail: `scope_match`, `conditions[]` and `aggregations[]`. Each condition entry carries `field`, `operator`, `expected_value`, the `current_value` read from the transaction, `matched`, `group_index` and `group_logic`. Each aggregation entry (velocity / count / sum) carries `metric`, `field`, `operator`, `expected_value`, the `computed_value` the aggregate evaluated to, `window`, `filters`, `matched` and `sample_references`; deferred async aggregations have `computed_value: null` and `deferred: true`. A nested condition group is one `conditions[]` entry with `operator` `any_of` or `all_of`, `field` null, and its members' results under its own `conditions`.

rule_runs.description: Per-rule execution results — which rule fired, with what score impact.

provider_results.description: Raw provider payloads (AML screening, blockchain analytics, etc.).

travel_rule.description: Travel Rule transfer or check. Populated when `travel_rule_details` was submitted, and also when Travel Rule is enabled and the transaction was created with `transaction_category: travelRule` (Didit initiates the exchange itself, even without `travel_rule_details`). `null` when no transfer or check exists. On an inbound transfer, the counterparty's `originator_data` and `beneficiary_data` stay masked (`data_masked: true`) until wallet ownership is confirmed.

network_snapshot.description: Graph snapshot of related transactions/parties used by the rules engine. Either the `network_snapshot` submitted with the transaction or the graph Didit builds from a successful AML wallet screening (which replaces a submitted one). `null` when neither exists.

remediation.description: Remediation session offered to the user when re-verification is required. Superseded by `action_required`, which is the canonical block; kept for backward compatibility.

action_required.description: Pending end-user action required to complete this transaction, or null when there is none. The Didit SDKs auto-launch the action by default and refresh the transaction when it finishes. Two variants, discriminated by `type`: `verification_session` (a hosted verification session created by a rule action) and `wallet_ownership` (a wallet-ownership widget session auto-minted for a Travel Rule transfer that needs proof of wallet control, gated by the `auto_wallet_verification` Travel Rule setting). When both could apply, `wallet_ownership` takes precedence because it blocks the Travel Rule exchange.

cost_breakdown.description: Cost of this transaction: `total_price` and `items`, one per charge, each with `usage_type`, `price`, `details` and `created_at`. A re-screen of the same transaction is a new item.

is_enabled.description: Whether the managed Travel Rule negotiation flow is active for outbound `travelRule` transactions on this application.

jurisdiction.description: Your VASP's operating jurisdiction code. Default `"EU"`. Didit maps it to the regime it stamps on your Travel Rule transactions as `travel_rule_regime` (for example `EU` or an EU member code becomes `eu`), which transaction rules can key on. Other Didit customers see it as your jurisdiction in the VASP directory once the Didit network lists your profile.

name_matching_strictness.description: How strictly beneficiary names must match before a transfer can reach COMPLETED. `CONTAINS` accepts one name whose words all appear in the other.

confirmation_timeout_hours.description: Hours an AWAITING_COUNTERPARTY transfer may remain unconfirmed before the periodic sweeper expires it. Default 48.

timeout_outcome.description: What happens to the underlying transaction when a transfer expires. Default HOLD. sunrise_policy and non_responsive_policy take precedence when they apply and are set.

threshold_amount.description: Decimal string, in your application's default currency. Minimum transfer amount that triggers a managed exchange; transfers below it resolve straight to NOT_APPLICABLE. Didit compares the transaction amount converted to your default currency, or the `amount_in_default_currency` you send; when no converted amount is available, the threshold does not apply. Defaults to "0.00" (EU TFR applies no minimum amount).

ownership_validation_mode.description: How much proof a wallet's ownership takes. `FULL` always needs a proof (signed message, test deposit or reviewed screenshot), never the end user's word. `SIMPLIFIED` accepts a self-declaration below `simplified_validation_threshold` and a proof above it. `AUTOMATED` lets the address book and earlier proofs answer on their own, self-declarations included while `allow_self_declaration` is true. Default `AUTOMATED`.

simplified_validation_threshold.description: Decimal string, default "0.00". In `SIMPLIFIED` mode a transfer below this amount (in the threshold currency) accepts a self-declaration. A transfer with no amount in that currency counts as above it.

legal_name.description: Your VASP's legal name. Required (non-blank) to set is_enabled to true.

lei.description: Your Legal Entity Identifier, surfaced in the VASP directory.

compliance_email.description: Compliance contact email for your VASP profile. The Didit network lists your profile only once this address is confirmed through an emailed link (POST /v3/travel-rule/settings/compliance-email/confirmation/); changing it needs a new confirmation.

is_discoverable.description: Whether your VASP profile can be listed in the Didit network: found in GET /v3/travel-rule/vasps/ by other Didit customers and reached on the INTERNAL rail. Listing also needs a live application, Travel Rule on, a legal name and a confirmed compliance email; didit_network says which are missing. Default true.

inbound_auto_accept.description: When true, an inbound TRP inquiry whose beneficiary wallet is a verified address-book entry with a matching name is approved automatically. When false, that inquiry waits in ON_HOLD for you to approve or deny it with the ownership endpoint. INTERNAL-rail and after-deposit transfers are not affected. Default true.

allow_self_declaration.description: When true, the wallet-ownership widget offers self-declaration as a fallback proof method. Default true.

allow_screenshot_proof.description: When true, the wallet-ownership widget offers screenshot upload as an ownership evidence method. Default true.

auto_wallet_verification.description: When true, submitting an outbound Travel Rule transfer that needs end-user proof of wallet control auto-mints a wallet-ownership widget session bound to the transaction and exposes it in the transaction's action_required block. Default true.

vasp_attribution_enabled.description: When true, an outbound Travel Rule transfer that no rail can route is attributed through blockchain analytics: the destination wallet is resolved to its owning VASP, the entity is recorded on the transfer and in the VASP directory, and the rails are re-run once with the attributed name. Default true.

counterparty_screening_enabled.description: Opt-in sanctions and adverse-media screening of counterparty VASPs, billed per screening at the Company AML Screening price. When on, Didit screens the counterparty an outbound exchange reaches (reusing a screening younger than 30 days) and you can screen one with POST /v3/travel-rule/vasps/{vasp_id}/screening/. Default false: nothing is screened or billed.

sunrise_policy.description: What an expired transfer does to its transaction when the counterparty is a directory entry in a jurisdiction on sunrise_jurisdictions, which does not enforce the Travel Rule yet: HOLD moves it to review, REJECT declines it, PROCEED leaves its status untouched. Empty (the default) follows timeout_outcome. Applies before non_responsive_policy.

sunrise_jurisdictions.description: Read-only. The countries (ISO 3166 alpha-2) Didit treats as in a Travel Rule sunrise period, where sunrise_policy applies. Currently CO, KH and VN. Any other jurisdiction, and an empty or unknown one, follows timeout_outcome.

non_responsive_policy.description: What an expired transfer does to its transaction when the counterparty is a directory entry whose responsiveness is UNRESPONSIVE: HOLD, REJECT or PROCEED, as for timeout_outcome. Empty (the default) follows timeout_outcome. sunrise_policy applies first when both fit.

travel_address.description: Read-only. Your VASP's own travel address - the encoded inbound TRP inquiry endpoint other VASPs use to reach you. Empty while `is_enabled` is false.

disabled_networks.description: Networks opted out of platform membership. Does not disable your connected own memberships or provision unavailable networks.

networks.description: Effective membership configuration for each network. No network, including GTR, is included by default. This is not a live health or delivery check.

mode.description: own: connected customer membership takes precedence; didit: configured platform membership allowed; off: platform routing disabled with no own membership; unavailable: neither membership available.

platform_available.description: Whether platform membership is configured; not a live health check.

connected.description: Whether a connected customer membership exists. Credentials are validated locally; network validation occurs on a live exchange.

mode.description: own: connected customer membership takes precedence; didit: configured platform membership allowed; off: platform routing disabled with no own membership; unavailable: neither membership available.

platform_available.description: Whether platform membership is configured; not a live health check.

connected.description: Whether a connected customer membership exists. Credentials are validated locally; network validation occurs on a live exchange.
