platform_available.description: Whether platform membership is configured; not a live health check.

connected.description: Whether a connected customer membership exists. Credentials are validated locally; network validation occurs on a live exchange.

didit_network.description: Whether the Didit network lists your VASP profile, so other Didit customers find it in the directory and reach it on the INTERNAL rail, and each condition it still misses.

missing.description: Empty when listed. compliance_email_unconfirmed: send the confirmation with POST /v3/travel-rule/settings/compliance-email/confirmation/ and open the emailed link. excluded_by_staff: Didit marked the application as a test, demo or internal one.

compliance_email_confirmed.description: Whether the current compliance_email was confirmed through the emailed link.

name_matching_strictness.description: `CONTAINS` accepts one name whose words all appear in the other.

compliance_email.description: Compliance contact email for your VASP profile. The Didit network lists your profile only once this address is confirmed through an emailed link (POST /v3/travel-rule/settings/compliance-email/confirmation/); changing it needs a new confirmation.

is_discoverable.description: Whether your VASP profile can be listed in the Didit network: found in GET /v3/travel-rule/vasps/ by other Didit customers and reached on the INTERNAL rail. Listing also needs a live application, Travel Rule on, a legal name and a confirmed compliance email; didit_network says which are missing. Default true.

threshold_amount.description: Decimal string, zero or greater, in your application's default currency. Minimum transfer amount that triggers a managed exchange.

ownership_validation_mode.description: See the response field of the same name.

data_sharing_fields.description: Merged per entity type: an entity type you leave out keeps its current choice. A choice that cannot meet the originator obligations of your `jurisdiction` regime (EU TFR or FATF Recommendation 16), an empty list included, is refused with `400`.

matching_rules.description: Merged per entity type, and per field inside it. A field that entity type does not compare (for example `date_of_birth` for `company`) is refused with `400`.

allow_screenshot_proof.description: When true, the wallet-ownership widget offers screenshot upload as an ownership evidence method. Default true.

counterparty_screening_enabled.description: Opt-in sanctions and adverse-media screening of counterparty VASPs, billed per screening at the Company AML Screening price. When on, Didit screens the counterparty an outbound exchange reaches (reusing a screening younger than 30 days) and you can screen one with POST /v3/travel-rule/vasps/{vasp_id}/screening/. Default false: nothing is screened or billed.

sunrise_policy.description: HOLD, REJECT, PROCEED, or empty to follow timeout_outcome. See the response field of the same name.

non_responsive_policy.description: HOLD, REJECT, PROCEED, or empty to follow timeout_outcome. See the response field of the same name.

disabled_networks.description: Networks opted out of platform membership. Does not disable your connected own memberships or provision unavailable networks.

TravelRuleSettingsUpdate.description: All fields optional; PUT applies a partial update.

address.description: The wallet address; `""` for an entry imported by its hash only. Unique per application, chain and memo, comparing the address without regard to case. After you delete an entry, you can register the same address again.

chain.description: Chain token for the address, for example `ETH` or `BTC`. When Didit routes or registers a transfer, it matches address book entries on the wallet address and, when the transfer carries a chain, on this value too, ignoring case. A transfer's chain is `beneficiary_data.chain`, filled from the transaction's crypto chain or currency symbol (for example `ETH`) when you do not send it, or the `chain` of an after-deposit registration, so use the same token everywhere. An entry with an empty chain matches any chain. A Lightning payee (a node id or a Lightning Address) registered on bitcoin is stored lowercased on `LIGHTNING`, where Lightning transfers are matched.

holder_vendor_data.description: Your internal identifier for the holder.

holder_name.description: Name of the wallet holder, used for the beneficiary name match.

is_ownership_verified.description: Read-only. Whether ownership of this address has been proven.

travel_address.description: The counterparty VASP's travel address for this wallet, if known. Lets Didit route this beneficiary's transfers over the TRP rail, for the assets TRP carries (BTC, ETH, and USDC on a named network).

address_hash.description: Read-only. SHA-256 of the lowercased address, in lowercase hex. An entry imported by its hash only is matched on it.

memo.description: The destination tag or memo that is part of the wallet on a memo network (XRP, XLM, EOS, ATOM, HBAR); `""` for the whole address. An entry with a memo matches only transfers naming that memo; one without matches the whole address.

receiving_travel_address.description: Your per-wallet travel address for this wallet: give it to the sending VASP so its TRP inquiry names this wallet. Empty for a wallet recorded as another VASP's, while Travel Rule is off, and before your VASP profile is saved.

address.description: The wallet address. An XRP X-address is stored as its classic address and its tag, so it matches transfers that name either form.

chain.description: Chain token for the address, for example `ETH` or `BTC`. When Didit routes or registers a transfer, it matches address book entries on the wallet address and, when the transfer carries a chain, on this value too, ignoring case. A transfer's chain is `beneficiary_data.chain`, filled from the transaction's crypto chain or currency symbol (for example `ETH`) when you do not send it, or the `chain` of an after-deposit registration, so use the same token everywhere. An entry with an empty chain matches any chain.

self_declared.description: Write-only. When true, the entry is created already ownership-verified via a SELF_DECLARATION proof. Returns 400 when `allow_self_declaration` is off in your Travel Rule settings.

travel_address.description: Optional. The counterparty VASP's travel address for this wallet, enabling TRP routing for the assets TRP carries (BTC, ETH, and USDC on a named network). An invalid travel address returns 400.

memo.description: Optional. The destination tag or memo that is part of the wallet. XRP: a destination tag, a whole number from 0 to 4294967295 (a JSON number is accepted). XLM: a text memo of up to 28 bytes, a 64-bit id or a 32-byte hash in hex. EOS: up to 256 bytes. ATOM: up to 256 characters. HBAR: up to 100 bytes. Bitcoin, EVM, Solana, Tron, Litecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Dogecoin and Lightning wallets take no memo: one there is a `400`. Alias: `destinationTag` or `destination_tag`.

WalletAddressEntryUpdate.description: PATCH is a partial update; the response echoes only holder_name, holder_vendor_data, entity_type, travel_address, receiving_travel_address, label, and owner_type.

TravelRuleTransferDetail.description: Full transfer object returned by the ownership-confirmation and finish/cancel endpoints. While an inbound transfer's wallet ownership is unconfirmed, the counterparty's `originator_data` and `beneficiary_data` come back masked (the first letter of each word is kept; the wallet, chain and VASP routing stay readable) and `data_masked` is true.

rail.description: The rail the transfer was routed over, or null when no rail was selected (for example below the threshold, a self-hosted counterparty wallet, an after-deposit registration, or no reachable counterparty). INTERNAL means both sides are Didit applications; EMAIL means the counterparty was reached by an emailed pickup link. TEST_VASP means the Didit Test VASP answered a sandbox application's transfer. Over GTR, VERIFYVASP and SYGNA, Didit reads the counterparty's answer from the network's response or by polling it every 5 minutes. TRUST only sends, so a TRUST transfer stays AWAITING_COUNTERPARTY until it expires. A network rail is used only when you have connected your own membership for that network. It is chosen after the transaction create returns, so it is null in that response.

name_match.description: The name comparison this entry decided, next to `detail`. Absent on entries that compared no name.

reason.description: Present only on the entry of a transition a failed delivery caused: `email_undeliverable` or `delivery_failed`, the value the transfer's `reason` reports.

dd_score.description: Due-diligence score from 0 to 100, where higher is better. Same scale as in the VASP directory.

dd_score_breakdown.description: Per-component contributions to dd_score, one object per component as in the VASP directory (jurisdiction, verification, protocol, lei, history, essentials, responsiveness), each {points, max, reason, detail}. {} until the counterparty has been assessed.

max.description: Maximum points this component can award.

reason.description: Machine-readable code of the component's verdict.

detail.description: Human-readable reason for the awarded points.

dd_assessed_at.description: When the due-diligence assessment last ran. Null until the counterparty has been assessed.

originator_data.description: Originator party. For an inbound transfer the counterparty's values are masked until ownership is confirmed.

beneficiary_data.description: Beneficiary party. For an inbound transfer the counterparty's values are masked until ownership is confirmed.

name_match.description: The name comparison that decided the transfer, or null until one ran. While the parties are masked, and on the other customer's copy of an INTERNAL exchange, `transfer_name`, `compared_name`, `matched_names` and `mismatched_names` are hidden. `score` and `matched` can disagree: `matched` follows the strictness, `score` is the similarity of the two full names.

mismatched_fields.description: Shortcut for `data_match.mismatched_fields`. Empty when nothing differs.

data_masked.description: True while the counterparty's personal data is masked in this response.

delivery.description: Where the latest message this transfer owes the other side stands. Null when the transfer never owed one (for example below `threshold_amount`, a declared self-hosted wallet, or a sunrise registration).

discovery.description: How Didit looked for the counterparty, one entry per step that ran. Empty when no discovery ran, for example on an inbound transfer.

reason.description: Why a `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_FOUND` or `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_REACHABLE` transfer is stuck; `""` for any other status. A failed delivery decides it first, on `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_REACHABLE` only: `email_undeliverable` (the mail provider refused the compliance email and no address is left to try: when it was sent, on a reminder, or as a permanent bounce reported later) or `delivery_failed` (the rail that was delivering failed for good: a network rail refused the message or ran out of retries, a `TRP` identity host did not answer, or the counterparty's `TRP` host did not accept the inquiry). Otherwise the `discovery` trace decides it: `awaiting_end_user` (no step named a counterparty Didit can reach), `directory_match_no_route` (a step named a directory VASP that has no route), `picked_member_without_proven_wallet` (the end user picked a Didit customer that has not proven control of the wallet), or `no_directory_match` when the trace gives no other reason. A resend moves the transfer on, so the reason clears. See [Why a transfer is stuck](/transaction-monitoring/travel-rule#why-a-transfer-is-stuck).

next_actions.description: What moves the transfer on; `[]` for any status but `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_FOUND` or `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_REACHABLE`. `email_undeliverable` offers `update_compliance_email`, then `resend`. `delivery_failed` offers `resend`. A discovery reason offers `select_counterparty_vasp`, `declare_self_hosted`, `add_vasp_hint` and `resend`.

confirmed.description: true to confirm ownership, false to deny it.

wallet_address.description: Inbound TRP transfers: the payment address Didit returns to the originating VASP when you approve. Defaults to the matched address book entry's address, then beneficiary_data.wallet_address. On a declared self-hosted wallet transfer that names no counterparty wallet, the wallet whose ownership you verified; without it the request is rejected with 400. Ignored for other transfers.

TravelRuleTransferPatchRequest.description: Provide exactly one of: payment_txn_id (finish), action=cancel, action=resend, action=update_compliance_email with compliance_email, or action=update_originator_wallet with wallet_address.

payment_txn_id.description: The on-chain transaction hash. Requires the transfer to be an outbound transfer in COMPLETED status.

action.description: "cancel" cancels a non-terminal transfer. "resend" re-runs routing for an outbound transfer stuck in COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_FOUND, COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_REACHABLE, or NOT_ENOUGH_COUNTERPARTY_DATA. "update_compliance_email" replaces the compliance email the request goes to, on an outbound transfer in one of those three statuses; send "resend" afterwards. "update_originator_wallet" records the wallet the funds actually left from (`wallet_address`, `memo`).

compliance_email.description: Required with `action: update_compliance_email`. Kept as this transfer's `beneficiary_data.counterparty_vasp_email`: it belongs to this transfer only and joins no directory entry and no contact list.

wallet_address.description: With `action: update_originator_wallet`: the wallet the funds left from. When the transfer's UTXO inputs are known it must be one of them.

memo.description: With `action: update_originator_wallet`: the wallet's memo or tag on a memo network. Optional.

VaspDirectoryEntry.description: A VASP of the directory or a member of the Didit network, with the routes your application has to it. A customer is a member of the Didit network only while its application is live, its Travel Rule is on, its profile is discoverable, has a legal name and a confirmed compliance email, and Didit has not marked the application as a test, demo or internal one. Each row also carries the shared due-diligence assessment (dd_score, risk_level, responsiveness, essential_checks) and your application's own decision, entity screening and questionnaires, which no other customer sees.

kind.description: directory for an entry of the shared directory; didit for a member of the Didit network.

jurisdiction.description: ISO 3166 country code, as the source gives it.

domains.description: The VASP's web domains. Always empty for Didit network members.

reachable.description: Whether your application has an available route to this VASP, or to one of its entities for a brand. Always true for a Didit network member, except on a sandbox application, where every row is false.

kind.description: trading_name, other_legal_name (from the global LEI register), network_name (the name on a Travel Rule network), attribution (the entity name blockchain analytics gives the VASP's wallets), merged (the name of a duplicate entry merged into this one) or staff.

aliases.description: Other names the VASP is found by.

items.description: A current listing of this VASP in a Travel Rule network's member directory. A TRISA listing says who the VASP is on TRISA; Didit has no TRISA rail, so it is never a route.

code.description: The VASP's identifier on that network.

listed_name.description: The name the network lists the VASP under.

country.description: The country the network lists, when it gives one.

verified_at.description: When Didit staff verified the listing. Null for listings read from a public directory.

last_seen_at.description: When the source last showed the listing. A listing the source has not shown for three weeks is removed.

source.description: Where the listing comes from: the public TRISA directory, or Didit staff.

items.description: One way your application can deliver Travel Rule data to this VASP, in the order dispatch tries them. A network route needs a membership on that network: your own (connected in the Marketplace) or Didit's once Didit holds one. Without it the route is listed as unavailable with the reason, never as a way to reach the VASP.

reason.description: Why an unavailable route cannot be used: no_membership (neither you nor Didit holds a membership on that network), network_switched_off (you turned that network off in your settings) or sandbox_application (a sandbox application sends only to the Didit Test VASP, so no route is available to it). Empty when the route is available.

via.description: How an available route is reached: own_membership or didit_membership for a network rail, directory for a TRP endpoint the directory verified, contact for the EMAIL rail, didit_network for a Didit network member. Empty when the route is unavailable.

umbrella.description: The brand this entry is a regulated entity of. Null when it is not part of one.

items.description: A regulated entity of a brand: the legal entity that receives a transfer.

reachable.description: Whether your application has an available route to it.

entities.description: For a brand, the regulated entities that receive its transfers. A transfer naming the brand goes to the reachable entity in the jurisdiction it states (beneficiary_data.counterparty_vasp_jurisdiction), else to the entity blockchain analytics attribution linked to the destination wallet, else to the only reachable entity when no jurisdiction is stated. Two entities that fit equally are never guessed between.

items.description: A compliance contact the EMAIL rail can write to.

source.description: staff: curated by Didit; application: added by your application; learned: an address that answered a Travel Rule request through its response link.

scope.description: platform contacts are used for every Didit customer's transfers; application contacts are private to your application, which sees only its own.

verified_at.description: When someone at this address answered a request. Null when it has not yet.

contacts.description: The platform's contacts for this VASP and your application's own.

dd_status.description: Didit's verification status of the entry, scored by the verification component of dd_score. Always COMPLETED for a Didit network member.

dd_score.description: The shared due-diligence score of a directory entry, 0 to 100, where higher is safer (see dd_score_semantic): the sum of the points in dd_score_breakdown. Null for a Didit network member, which is not scored. An entry not assessed yet (dd_assessed_at null) shows 0 with an empty risk_level, so read risk_level rather than the raw score.

reachable_rails.description: Rails recorded on the entry. Read routes for what your application can use today.

is_didit_customer.description: true for a member of the Didit network (dd_status is always COMPLETED, dd_score null and risk_level empty for these) and for a directory entry linked to a Didit customer.

dd_score_breakdown.description: One object per component of dd_score. Components, their weight (max) and their reason codes: jurisdiction, 25 (jurisdiction_not_high_risk, jurisdiction_high_risk, jurisdiction_unknown); verification, 15 (dd_status_completed, dd_status_in_progress, dd_status_not_started, dd_status_rejected); protocol, 15 (native_rail, email_only, no_rail); lei, 10 (lei_valid, lei_missing); history, 10 (history, no_history); essentials, 15 (essential_checks, no_essential_checks); responsiveness, 10 (responsive, unresponsive, responsiveness_unknown). Empty for a Didit network member.

points.description: Points the component contributes, rounded to one decimal.

max.description: The component's weight: the points it contributes at best.

reason.description: Machine-readable code of the component's verdict.

dd_assessed_at.description: When dd_score, risk_level and responsiveness were last computed: after an exchange with the entry completes, finishes, expires, mismatches or is declined, when Didit refreshes or curates the entry, and in the weekly directory refresh. Null for a Didit network member.

dd_score_semantic.description: Which way dd_score points: always higher_is_safer.

risk_level.description: The band dd_score falls in: LOW (70 or more), MEDIUM (40 to 69) or HIGH (below 40). Empty for a Didit network member and for an entry not assessed yet. Filter on it with risk. Your own flagged screening never changes this shared value: it makes counterparty_risk_level HIGH in your rules instead.

responsiveness.description: Whether the VASP answers Travel Rule requests: the share of the requests Didit customers started towards it in the last 90 days that it answered. Only requests sent over a network or protocol rail, or by email to a shared address (the entry's compliance address or a platform contact), count; a request sent to an address a customer typed, or to a customer's private contact, never does. An expired request is unanswered; a completed exchange, a decline or a data mismatch is an answer; a cancelled request or an unreachable rail is neither. Always UNKNOWN with zero counts for a Didit network member.

status.description: UNKNOWN with fewer than 5 decided requests in the window; UNRESPONSIVE when less than 10 percent of them were answered; RESPONSIVE otherwise.

answered.description: Decided requests in the window that the VASP answered.

total.description: Decided requests in the window: answered plus expired.

essential_checks.description: The essential-checks report of a directory entry, built only from the platform's verified sources: registration (an official register lists the VASP: the EU's interim MiCA register, the public TRISA directory or the global LEI register), licence (a MiCA authorisation is on record and current), domain (the entry's domain matches its TRP endpoint or the website its register gives) and lei (its LEI record is active, issued and consistent with the entry's names and country). The essentials component of dd_score is the share of decided checks that pass. Empty until the weekly directory refresh first checks the entry, and always empty for a Didit network member.

status.description: unknown when no source on record can decide the check.

reason.description: Machine-readable code of the verdict.

decision.description: Your application's decision on this VASP, or for an entity with no decision of its own its brand's (inherited_from names the brand). Null when there is none. Private to your application.

entity_screening.description: Your application's latest sanctions and adverse-media screening of this VASP. Null when you never screened it. Private to your application.

questionnaires.description: Your application's due-diligence questionnaires with this VASP, newest first. Private to your application.

jurisdiction.detail: DEU is not on the high-risk jurisdiction list

protocol.detail: reachable over the email fallback only

responsiveness.detail: 0 decided recent requests, too few to judge

answers.legal_name: Example Counterparty VASP, incorporated in the example jurisdiction.
answers.licensing: Crypto-asset service provider authorised under MiCA by its national regulator, licence active.
answers.jurisdictions: EU and EEA. We do not serve the United States.
answers.aml_program: Written AML/CFT policy, annual independent review, last completed in March 2026.
answers.compliance_officer: Head of Compliance, reachable at compliance@counterparty.example.
answers.sanctions_screening: Customers at onboarding and daily; counterparties on every transfer.
answers.transaction_monitoring: Rule-based monitoring with analyst review; suspicious activity reports filed with the FIU.
answers.travel_rule: TRP and email; we answer requests within one business day.
answers.custody: Segregated customer wallets held with a qualified custodian, insured.
answers.ownership: No shareholder holds 25 percent or more; parent company Example Holding Group.
answers.record_keeping: Five-year record-keeping for Travel Rule and transaction data, as our regulator requires.
answers.data_protection: Encrypted at rest and in transit, stored in the EU.

TravelRuleCounterpartyDecision.description: Your application's decision on a counterparty VASP. Private to your application: it never changes the shared directory entry and another customer never sees it. It acts only through your transaction rules (the counterparty_dd_status rule field and the travel-rule-counterparty-blocked and travel-rule-counterparty-restricted presets); it never changes how a transfer is routed.

decision.description: APPROVED: your team cleared the counterparty. RESTRICTED: transfers to it may go ahead after review. BLOCKED: your team refused it.

reason.description: Free-text reason you gave, empty when none.

decided_by.description: The console user who made or last changed the decision. Empty when an API key made it.

inherited_from.description: The brand whose decision this entity follows because you made none on the entity itself. Null when the decision is the counterparty's own.

decision.description: The decision that applies to the counterparty for your application: its own, else (for an entity of a brand) the brand's. Null when there is none.

reason.description: Optional. Replaces the previous reason; omit it to clear it.

TravelRuleCounterpartyScreening.description: One sanctions and adverse-media screening of the counterparty entity, run for and billed to your application. Private to your application: another customer never sees it.

status.description: Approved: no possible match needs attention. In Review or Declined: a possible sanctions or adverse-media match.

total_hits.description: How many possible matches the screening returned.

score.description: The highest risk score among the possible matches. Null when nothing matched.

fresh.description: Whether the screening is younger than fresh_days (30 days). A fresh screening is reused instead of billed again.

flagged.description: true while the screening is fresh and its status is In Review or Declined. While your latest screening is flagged and counterparty screening stays on, counterparty_risk_level is HIGH in your rules.

enabled.description: Your counterparty_screening_enabled Travel Rule setting. Off by default; nothing is screened or billed while it is off.

price.description: Decimal string, in USD: what one screening costs your organization, the Company AML Screening price.

fresh_days.description: How many days a screening stays fresh and is reused.

screening.description: Your latest screening of the counterparty. Null when you never screened it.

refresh.description: true screens again (and bills again) even when a fresh screening exists.

outcome.description: screened: a new screening ran and was billed (201). reused: a fresh screening was returned and nothing was billed (200).

TravelRuleCounterpartyQuestionnaire.description: One due-diligence questionnaire your application sent the counterparty: Didit's standard questionnaire, emailed to a compliance address on record with a single-use answer link. Private to your application.

status.description: SENT: waiting for answers. ANSWERED: the counterparty answered every question. EXPIRED: the answer link closed unanswered (its deadline passed, or a newer questionnaire replaced it), or answers passed valid_until.

form_version.description: Version of Didit's standard questionnaire the answers belong to. Currently 1.

expires_at.description: The answer-by deadline, 30 days after sending. The link stops working after it.

valid_until.description: How long the answers stay current: 365 days after answering. Null until answered.

current.description: true while the questionnaire is ANSWERED and valid_until has not passed.

answers.description: The answers keyed by question id: legal_name, licensing, jurisdictions, aml_program, compliance_officer, sanctions_screening, transaction_monitoring, travel_rule, custody, ownership, record_keeping, data_protection. Each answer is up to 2,000 characters. Empty until answered.

sent_to.description: Optional. A compliance address on record for the counterparty: for a directory entry its compliance address or a contact your application sees, for a Didit network member its confirmed compliance email. Default: the address a Travel Rule email to the counterparty goes to (your own contact first, then a platform contact, then the entry's compliance address).

TravelRulePickupInfo.description: The pending exchange behind an emailed pickup link, as the counterparty's response page shows it.

reference.description: The transfer's uuid, as the sending VASP's console shows it.

recipient_vasp_name.description: The counterparty VASP the request is addressed to.

language.description: The language of the request email and the response page, from the counterparty's jurisdiction.

fiat_amount.description: The converted value the sender gave, or empty.

contact.description: The `?contact=` value of the link, echoed back; empty when the link has none.

join_invitation.description: Whether the counterparty holds a live invitation to join Didit for free. The invitation link travels only in the email to the invited address, so `url` is empty here.

originator_data.description: The originator fields the sending VASP shares (`data_sharing_fields`). The name and the wallet are always included.

ivms_request.description: The same request as an IVMS 101 object. Left out while `data_masked` is true.

data_masked.description: Always false on this endpoint: an email request is outbound, and the sender's own user is never masked.

beneficiary_name.description: The beneficiary's name as your records hold it, run through the sending VASP's name rule. `ivms_response` takes precedence when it names the beneficiary.

decline_reason.description: Why you decline. Recorded on the sending VASP's transfer timeline. Empty (the default) when you give no reason.

decline_detail.description: Free text; required when `decision` is `decline` and `decline_reason` is `other`.

ivms_response.description: Your full IVMS 101 response. Its beneficiary name wins over `beneficiary_name`.

contact.description: The contact the link was sent to, from the link's `?contact=` value. When the body leaves it out, the `contact` query parameter is used.

chain.description: Chain the deposit settled on, for example `ETH`. Stored lowercase and compared case-insensitively with your wallet address book entries, so use the same chain token there.

txid.description: On-chain transaction hash. Deduped together with wallet_address.

wallet_address.description: The destination wallet you received the deposit on. An XRP X-address is split into its classic address and tag.

amount.description: Deposit amount as a decimal string, zero or greater, with up to 18 decimal places.

originator_data.description: Originator details from the sending VASP, if known, as a flat object such as `{"name": "..."}`. Didit reads name (or full_name), first_name, last_name and vendor_data from it.

beneficiary_data.description: Beneficiary details (your customer), as a flat object such as `{"name": "..."}`. Didit matches name against the holder_name of the matched address book entry, and sets wallet_address and chain from the request.

originating_vasp.description: Optional description of the sending VASP. It stays on this transfer only (`metadata.originating_vasp`, and the transfer's originator VASP in GET /v3/travel-rule/transfers/); it never creates, edits or links a shared VASP directory entry.

lei.description: Optional. A valid 20-character ISO 17442 LEI, or empty.

travel_address.description: The sender's travel address, recorded on this transfer.

memo.description: Optional. The deposit's destination tag or memo on a memo network: on a shared deposit address it is what tells your customers apart, and the address-book entry for that memo is matched. XRP: a destination tag, a whole number from 0 to 4294967295 (a JSON number is accepted). XLM: a text memo of up to 28 bytes, a 64-bit id or a 32-byte hash in hex. EOS: up to 256 bytes. ATOM: up to 256 characters. HBAR: up to 100 bytes. Bitcoin, EVM, Solana, Tron, Litecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Dogecoin and Lightning wallets take no memo: one there is a `400`. Alias: `destinationTag` or `destination_tag`.

utxo.description: Optional, UTXO chains only. The deposit transaction's inputs and outputs: the sender's wallet is the declared `originator_data.wallet_address`, else the largest input.

transaction_id.description: Didit transaction UUID for the inbound deposit.

txn_id.description: txn_id of the inbound transaction: Didit-generated when Didit created the transaction, or your own when an unclaimed deposit was reused.

created.description: true when this call registered the transfer (HTTP 201); false when a transfer for the same txid and wallet_address already existed (HTTP 200).

beneficiary_wallet_address.description: The destination wallet address. The Didit Test VASP sends to it, matched against your wallet address book on the chain of the asset. A wallet with no matching entry is accepted and the inbound transaction is booked ON_HOLD.

scenario.description: What the Didit Test VASP declares the beneficiary to be. `accept` declares the holder's own name; `name_mismatch` declares a name no holder agrees with. The decision itself is always yours.

reference.description: Optional idempotency key. A repeat with the same value returns the transfer the first call booked.

transaction_id.description: Didit transaction UUID of the inbound transfer.

travel_rule_status.description: The status your application's own decision resolved to.

detail.description: Why the transfer resolved to that status.

test_vasp.description: Always true: the sender was the Didit Test VASP.

wallet_address.description: The wallet address to verify. Optional; when empty, the address must be supplied when a proof is started.

chain.description: Chain token for the address, for example `ETH`, `BTC` or `SOL`. Use the same token as in your wallet address book. Message signing and the Satoshi test are offered only for a supported chain.

holder_name.description: Name of the wallet holder, used for the beneficiary name match.

vendor_data.description: Your internal identifier for the holder, carried onto the created address-book entry.

transaction_id.description: Optional. Didit transaction UUID of a Travel Rule transfer to advance when the proof verifies.

satoshi_deposit_address.description: Optional. A deposit address you control; supplying it enables the SATOSHI_TEST proof method.

callback_url.description: Optional. Absolute http(s) URL where the widget returns the customer after completion.

expires_in_minutes.description: Optional. Lifetime of the minted link, in minutes. Automatically extended to cover the Satoshi test window when SATOSHI_TEST is offered.

token.description: Opaque session token embedded in the widget URL.

url.description: The hosted wallet-ownership widget URL. Open it verbatim in the system browser (never inside a mobile SDK webview).

vasp_name.description: Legal name from your VASP profile, shown to the customer in the widget. Empty when no profile exists.

allowed_methods.description: Proof methods available for this session. MESSAGE_SIGNING requires a supported chain family, SATOSHI_TEST requires a satoshi_deposit_address on the session, SCREENSHOT requires the allow_screenshot_proof setting, and SELF_DECLARATION requires the allow_self_declaration setting and an `ownership_validation_mode` that accepts a declaration for the linked transfer (never in `FULL`; in `SIMPLIFIED` only below `simplified_validation_threshold`). Initiating a SELF_DECLARATION the mode does not accept answers 403.

transfer_status.description: Status of the linked Travel Rule transfer. Null when the session was minted without a transaction_id.

callback_url.description: Where the widget returns the customer after completion. Empty when not set.

completed_at.description: Non-null once a proof has been verified.

max_attempts.description: Rejected wallet proofs this session allows.

attempts_remaining.description: When 0, starting another proof answers 409 and you mint a new widget session.

customization.description: The application's whitelabel customization (colors, logo, font family) when white label is enabled - the widget renders with the same branding as the verification flow. Null otherwise.

status.description: PENDING on a SATOSHI_TEST proof means the deposit has been seen on-chain but has not yet reached enough confirmations; a background job automatically rechecks it and moves it to VERIFIED once it confirms, with no resubmission needed. REJECTED means a genuinely wrong deposit was submitted (absent, wrong sender, or wrong amount). EXPIRED means the proof's own test window closed before a valid deposit was seen.

deposit_address.description: Deposit address the customer must send the Satoshi test amount to. Present only on a SATOSHI_TEST proof.

expected_amount.description: Exact on-chain amount, in the deposit's native currency, the Satoshi test deposit must match. Present only on a SATOSHI_TEST proof.

expires_at.description: Deadline for this proof's own Satoshi test window. Present only on a SATOSHI_TEST proof; the widget session's own expires_at is extended to cover it when SATOSHI_TEST is offered.

challenge.description: Didit-issued message the customer signs with their wallet. Present only on a MESSAGE_SIGNING proof.

rejection_reason.description: Why the proof was rejected. Present only when `status` is REJECTED.

CaseSubject.description: The single user or business the case is anchored to.

country.description: Three-letter country code of the subject (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3), or null when it is not known. For a business, its country of incorporation. For a person, the issuing country of an identity document from their verifications; a person with documents from several countries shows one of them, and ICAO document codes such as `XXA` can appear.

portrait.description: Short-lived signed URL of the person's portrait image. Always null for a business, and null for a person without a portrait. The URL expires, so download the image when you read the case instead of storing the URL.

CaseContentConfig.description: The six togglable sections that drive which tabs and fields appear on the case page. Unknown sections or keys are rejected.

optional.description: When true, a case can be resolved with incomplete checklist items.

linked_entity_summary.description: session_id/session_number/status for session and business_session links; uuid/txn_id/status for transaction links.

content_config.description: The six togglable sections that drive which tabs and fields appear on the case page. Unknown sections or keys are rejected.

optional.description: When true, a case can be resolved with incomplete checklist items.

creation_sources.description: Connectors currently routing new cases into this blueprint.

receives_escalation_from.description: Other blueprints whose Escalation target points at this one.

pending_resolution.description: Set only while a 4-eyes resolution is staged on the checker blueprint, awaiting approve or reject-approval.

maker_email.description: Email of the officer who submitted the resolution. Null when an API key submitted it: that resolution has no recorded maker, so approve and reject-approval return 403 for every caller.

maker_user_id.description: Member user uuid of the officer who submitted the resolution. Null when an API key submitted it. That member cannot be named as `checker`.

pending_resolution.description: Set only while a 4-eyes resolution is staged on the checker blueprint, awaiting approve or reject-approval.

maker_email.description: Email of the officer who submitted the resolution. Null when an API key submitted it: that resolution has no recorded maker, so approve and reject-approval return 403 for every caller.

maker_user_id.description: Member user uuid of the officer who submitted the resolution. Null when an API key submitted it. That member cannot be named as `checker`.

field_config.description: Reusable goAML header defaults. Template-level obligatory fields: rentity_id, submission_code, and currency_code_local (3-letter). Optional: enabled_fields (which optional report blocks to include) plus reporting_person, location, reason, and action defaults. Per-filing header fields (action, submission_date, transactions, jurisdiction) are enforced when the report is validated or finalized, not on the template.

report_code.description: goAML report code derived from report_type, e.g. STR, CTR, BCR.

rentity_id.description: Reporting entity ID issued by the FIU.

validation_errors.description: Result of the most recent validation; each entry is a {field, message} object.

field.description: Transaction field path to evaluate. Core fields: amount, currency, direction, action_type, score, severity, transaction_type, payment_details, preferred_currency_amount (falls back to amount_in_default_currency), default_currency_code, subject_country, counterparty_country, subject_vendor_data, counterparty_vendor_data, subject_device_fingerprint, counterparty_device_fingerprint, subject_browser_family, subject_browser_version, subject_platform, subject_accept_language, subject_session_age_ms, subject_ip_country, counterparty_ip_country, subject_ip_address, counterparty_ip_address, subject_payment_method_type, subject_payment_method_country, subject_payment_method_fingerprint, subject_payment_method_account_id (and the counterparty_payment_method_* equivalents), travel_rule_status, travel_rule_required, travel_rule_obligations_count, counterparty_dd_status (your decision on the Travel Rule counterparty: APPROVED, RESTRICTED or BLOCKED, an entity following its brand's), counterparty_risk_level (LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH; HIGH while your own counterparty screening is flagged), counterparty_jurisdiction (the counterparty VASP's country), counterparty_responsiveness (RESPONSIVE, UNRESPONSIVE or UNKNOWN), subject_days_since_previous_transaction, tags, and custom_values.<key> for any key submitted in custom_properties on transaction create. Country-code fields accept ISO-2 or ISO-3; both sides are normalized to ISO-3 before comparison.

operator.description: Comparison operator. in/not_in test membership (value may be a list or a single scalar). contains/not_contains are case-insensitive substring checks against a string value. contains_any takes a list of strings and matches when any is a case-insensitive substring of the field value. regex matches the value pattern against the field. fuzzy_match compares against the value string with the required `score` threshold (0-100). gt/gte/lt/lte never match when either side is missing. exists/is_not_empty/is_not_null (aliases) and not_exists/is_empty/is_null (aliases) are presence checks that ignore `value`.

value.description: Comparison value. Its shape depends on the operator and value_type; omit for the presence-check operators.

value_type.description: Optional value interpretation. `list`: value is a List UUID and the list's entries become the comparison value. `field`: value is another field path, compared field-to-field. `relative_date`: value is a relative-date object, e.g. {"direction": "past", "unit": "days", "amount": 30}.

score.description: Required when operator is fuzzy_match: the 0-100 similarity threshold.

group_index.description: Optional grouped logic. When any condition carries group_index, conditions sharing an index form a group and grouped evaluation replaces evaluation_mode.

group_logic.description: How conditions combine WITHIN a group.

groups_logic.description: How group outcomes combine ACROSS groups. Read from the first condition.

TransactionRuleCondition.description: A condition reads only the transaction being evaluated - it never filters the aggregation window.

metric.description: How the matching historical transactions are aggregated. unique_count is accepted as an alias of distinct_count.

field.description: Field aggregated by sum/max/min/avg/distinct_count. Ignored for count.

operator.description: Comparison applied to the computed metric.

value.description: Threshold the computed metric is compared against.

window.description: Look-back window ending at the transaction's txn_date: <N>m (MINUTES, not months), <N>h (hours) or <N>d (days), e.g. 30m, 24h, 7d, 30d.

filters.description: Narrows which historical transactions are aggregated. Keys are field paths from the condition field catalog; a value of "__current__" resolves to the same field's value on the transaction being evaluated (e.g. {"subject_vendor_data": "__current__"} scopes the window to the same subject), and a list value means membership. Filters compare by equality or membership ONLY - there is no lt/gte filter, so a range such as "historical transactions under 10,000" cannot be expressed here. Put the range on the metric instead (metric max with operator lt keeps every transaction in the window below the threshold).

TransactionRuleAggregation.description: Velocity check over the application's historical transactions inside the window. Every aggregation entry must match for the rule to match, regardless of evaluation_mode. An aggregation constrains only the window; the transaction being evaluated is constrained by scope and conditions, so repeat direction, currency or transaction_type on both halves when the rule promises them.

transaction_types.description: Restrict to transaction types, e.g. finance, kyc, travel_rule, user_event. Empty or missing = no restriction.

directions.description: Restrict to transaction directions (case-insensitive on write).

action_types.description: Restrict to your action_type values, e.g. withdrawal, deposit.

TransactionRuleScope.description: Which transactions the rule applies to. Only these three keys are accepted.

Omitted evaluation_mode defaults to ALL (which can reduce matches for an ANY rule), and omitted period_days defaults to 90 days, not unlimited history.

counterparty_connections.description: Entities the provider attributes the screened address to. For Merkle Science these come from the address's own owner and user tags, so the same entity can appear twice, and they carry no fund flows: `received_usd`, `sent_usd`, `received_hops` and `sent_hops` are `null` and `percentage` is 0. Do not route on `risk_level` or `is_direct` here: use `sanctions_hit`, `dominant_risk_category` and `risk_factors[].is_high_risk` for the verdict, and `exposure_type` in `source_of_funds`/`destination_of_funds` for directness.

risk_level.description: Lowercase and provider-dependent. For Merkle Science it is the address's own 0-5 risk grade (`no_risk`, `low`, `medium_low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`), raised to `high` when the entity's category is high risk; it is not a separate grade of the entity.

sent_usd.description: USD sent to the entity, when the provider reports it.

received_hops.description: Hops to the entity on the receiving side, when the provider reports them.

sent_hops.description: Hops to the entity on the sending side, when the provider reports them.

percentage.description: Share of the address's exposure, when the provider reports it; otherwise 0.

is_direct.description: Always `true` for Merkle Science, whose connections are attributions rather than counterparties.

country.description: Country of the entity, when known.

sanctions_hit.description: True if the address has direct or indirect sanctions exposure.

pep_counterparty.description: Politically exposed person exposure. `null` when no PEP finding is available, which is every result today because no provider reports one; `false` only for an explicit negative screening result. Do not read `null` as a completed PEP check.

dominant_risk_category.description: Highest-weighted high-risk category, or `null` when none is dominant (e.g. `sanctioned`, `mixer`, `stolen_funds`).

risk_factors.description: Ranked explanation of `risk_score`: what produced this verdict. Providers grade an address on their own model and return only a verdict (Merkle Science returns an integer 0-5), so the score alone is not actionable. Ordered high-risk first, then by the value that moved through each driver, capped at the five strongest; `source_of_funds` and `destination_of_funds` always carry the complete breakdown. A high `risk_score` with no `is_high_risk` entry means the provider reported no sanctions or attributed-entity match and graded the address purely on its own exposure model - `summary` states this explicitly.

source.description: `attribution` is what the provider says the address itself is (its own tag or cluster); `exposure` is where its funds actually moved.

category.description: Normalised risk category, same vocabulary as the exposure breakdown.

label.description: The provider's own wording for the driver (e.g. `Gambling / Crypto only`), which is what you would also see in the provider's console.

entity_name.description: Attributed entity behind the driver, for example a gambling site or an exchange.

direction.description: Direction of the fund flow, `attribution` when the driver is the address's own tag, or `unknown` when the provider did not report a direction.

exposure_type.description: `direct` (1 hop) or `indirect` (multi-hop), `attribution` for the address's own tag, or `unknown` when the provider did not state how many hops away the counterparty is. Treat `unknown` as unclassified, not as `direct`.

amount_usd.description: USD value attributed to this driver.

percentage.description: Share of the address's TOTAL screened volume, both directions combined - unlike `percentage` inside `source_of_funds`/`destination_of_funds`, which is normalised per direction. Comparable and summable across the whole list.

is_high_risk.description: Whether the category is one Didit treats as high risk (`sanctioned`, `mixer`, `stolen_funds`, `ransomware`, `scam`, `darknet_market`, `terrorist_financing`, `child_exploitation`, `hacked_exchange`, `high_risk_exchange`, `seized_funds`).

description.description: One-line rendering of the driver, e.g. `9.01% indirect outgoing exposure to Gambling / Crypto only (Example Gambling)`.

raw_response.description: The provider's own payload. Its shape is provider-specific and can change without notice: read the normalised fields instead of parsing it.

report_signature.description: Opaque HMAC-SHA256 signature over this exact result, scoped to your application. Not meaningful on its own — repost the full response body, unmodified and including this field, to `POST /v3/wallet-screening/pdf/` to render it as a PDF. The PDF endpoint rejects the request with `400` if `report_signature` is missing or if any signed field (e.g. `risk_score`, `severity`, `sanctions_hit`) was edited before repost.

Every count may be null when no data was returned for it. `profiles_registered: 0` means the platforms were checked and the email address was found on none of them - a valid, billable answer and a common synthetic-identity signal.

profiles_registered.description: Platforms where the email address is confirmed registered.

names_found.description: Platforms that returned an associated name.

photos_found.description: Platforms that returned a profile photo.

digital_footprint_diversity.description: Distinct platform categories with detected presence.

whatsapp_profile_completeness.description: Completeness of the WhatsApp profile. Phone only; null for email.

not_registered_platforms.description: Platforms checked with a negative result.

categories.description: Registered count and ratio per platform category.

profiles.description: Per-platform profile details, keyed by platform, when the platform exposes them.

KYBRegistryAddress.description: An address the registry states, in the same shape for every country and registry source. Every key is always present; a part the registry does not publish is null.

type.description: Address type in lower case: `registered` for the registered office; other types as the registry names them (for example `postal`, `office`). `null` when the registry does not say what the address is.

address.description: The full address as one line. Always present on every address.

description.description: The registry's own label for the address, when it gives one.

KYBRegistryIndustry.description: An activity the registry classifies the company under, in the same shape for every country and registry source.

code.description: Activity code as the registry prints it (for example `73110`).

description.description: Activity label, when the registry publishes one.

scheme.description: Classification system, one name per system whichever source reported it: `UK SIC 2007`, `US SIC`, `NACE Rev. 2`, `NACE Rev. 2.1`, `NAF Rev. 2`, `CNAE`, `SBI`, `NOGA 2008`, `CAE Rev. 4`, `Canada SIC 1977`; other national systems keep the registry's own name. Null when the registry does not name the system.

is_primary.description: True for the company's main activity. Exactly one entry is primary when the list is not empty.

KYBRegistryShareholding.description: What an owner holds, in the same shape for every country and registry source. Null when the registry states no holding. A band (for example a UK PSC's 25-50%) is not a stake: `percentage` is null and the band stays in `ownership_min_shares` / `ownership_max_shares`.

share_class.description: Share class or type as the registry names it.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of the values below.

percentage.description: Exact stake in percent, to four decimal places.

KYBRegistryOwnership.description: The outcome of the ownership (Shareholders / UBO) tier, in the same shape for every country and registry source.

status.description: `delivered` when the registry published ownership; `unavailable` when it did not (see `unavailable_reason`); `pending` while the registry is still fetching it; `not_requested` for the Basic tier.

tier_delivered.description: The tier the registry delivered (and that is billed). A UBO request answered with direct shareholders only is `shareholders`.

unavailable_reason.description: Why a requested ownership tier was not delivered. Null unless `status` is `unavailable` or `pending`.

direct_ownership_complete.description: True when the direct shareholders' stated stakes add up to 100% (within one percentage point of rounding); false when they do not; null when ownership was not delivered or a stake is not stated.

unresolved.description: Parts of the ownership chain the registry could not resolve, for example no group structure on record above the direct owners.

DigitalIdWalletApiWalletVerificationFiel.description: Request validation errors: each rejected field with its messages.

DigitalIdWalletApiWalletVerificationResp.description: One standalone wallet verification, as every wallet endpoint answers it.

metadata.description: The metadata object sent at start, or null.

status.description: Not Finished while pending, then Approved (verified) or Declined.

signature_valid.description: True once the credential's signature was verified; null for a simulated one.

nationality.description: ISO3 nationality, only when the wallet asserts one (never inferred).

issuing_state.description: ISO3 country whose scheme issued the identity.

type.description:
redirect: send the user's browser to url. confirm_in_app: show verification_code to the user, who checks it matches the code in their wallet app and confirms there; then poll.

* `redirect` - redirect
* `confirm_in_app` - confirm_in_app

url.description: redirect only: where the user signs in with the wallet.

verification_code.description: confirm_in_app only: the 4-digit comparison code the wallet app shows too.

poll_interval_seconds.description: confirm_in_app only: how often to call POST .../verifications/{request_id}/poll/ for prompt feedback. Didit also polls pending sign-ins in the background, so the webhook reports the outcome even when you do not poll.

DigitalIdWalletApiWalletVerificationResu.description:
* `pending` - Pending
* `verified` - Verified
* `cancelled` - Cancelled by the user
* `timeout` - Timed out
* `failed` - Failed

id.description: Catalog id of the wallet, e.g. bankid_se.

publish.description: Set false to save a never-published draft. The record remains inactive at version 0 until the draft is explicitly published. Omitting this field preserves immediate creation for existing integrations.

type.description:
Identifier type. Determines which namespace fields are required.

* `email` - Email
* `phone` - Phone
* `national_id` - National Id
* `tax_number` - Tax Number
* `passport_number` - Passport Number

value.description: The identifier value, in any customary format.

country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 or alpha-3 issuing country. Required for government identifier types: the same digits mean different people in different countries.

issuer.description: Optional issuing authority or sub-national issuer, when the country alone is not unique.

SignatureField.description: A field to place on a session document: which signer fills it, how, and where. Give either a position (`page`, `x`, `y`, `width` and `height`) or an `anchor`. Positions are fractions of the page as it's displayed, from its top-left corner, rounded to 4 decimals, and the field must fit inside the page. A document takes up to 200 fields and one signer up to 500, and every role with fields on a document needs a `signature` or `initials` field there. See [Fields on the document](/core-technology/electronic-signature/overview#fields-on-the-document).

key.description: Names the field in the results and in `sign.field_values`. Unique within the document.

type.description: What the field holds. The signer applies their adopted `signature` and `initials`, types `text`, ticks a `checkbox`, and types an `email` when the session has no verified email. Didit fills `full_name` (the verified name), `date_signed` (the date of signing, in the signer's time zone), `data` (from `prefill`) and a verified `email`, and shows them read-only. There is no date picker type: use `text`.

role.description: Who fills the field, with the `signature_signer` values. A step fills and stamps only the fields of its own signer. Defaults to the step's signer.

page.description: Page number, from 1 to the document's page count. For a Word document, a page of the converted PDF.

x.description: Left edge, as a fraction of the page width.

y.description: Top edge, as a fraction of the page height.

width.description: Width, as a fraction of the page width. A signature is at least `0.12` wide.

height.description: Height, as a fraction of the page height. A signature is at least `0.035` high.

required.description: `signature` and `initials` are required unless you set `false`. `full_name`, `date_signed` and `data` are always required. The signer can't finish a document until its required fields have a value, and a required checkbox must be ticked.

label.description: Shown to the signer and in the results. Defaults from the type.

prefill.description: Where the value comes from: `identity.full_name`, `identity.first_name`, `identity.last_name`, `identity.date_of_birth` (`DD/MM/YYYY`), `identity.nationality`, `identity.document_number`, `identity.document_type`, `identity.issuing_country`, `identity.address`, `contact.email`, `contact.phone`, `company.name`, `company.registration_number`, `company.address`, `company.country` (KYB), `session.vendor_data`, `metadata.<key>` (a key of the session's `metadata`) or `api.<key>` (a key of `sign.field_values`). Required for `data`. `full_name` always uses `identity.full_name` and `email` uses `contact.email`. The values of `data`, `full_name` and verified `email` fields are fixed when the signer starts signing.

editable_when_prefilled.description: `text` and `email` only: the signer can change a pre-filled value.

title.description: Title shown to the signer. Defaults to `file_name`.

content_base64.description: The file, base64-encoded. A PDF can have up to 20 MB and 100 pages, without a password, scripts or attached files. A Word file (`.docx`) can have up to 20 MB and is converted to PDF while the request runs, in at most 25 seconds; the PDF then has the same limits. Up to 5 Word files per session. A Word file with macros, tracked changes, links to external content or embedded objects is refused with `signature_document_not_supported`, and one that can't be converted returns `signature_document_conversion_failed`, each with a `reason`.

fields.description: Optional fields to place on this document, up to 200. Pages and positions refer to the PDF, or to the converted PDF for a Word file. Without fields, the signer reads the document and agrees to it.

SignatureResult.description: One signer's result for one Electronic Signature step. See the [Electronic Signature report](/core-technology/electronic-signature/report-electronic-signature).

id.description: Pass it as `signature_id` to download this signer's evidence or validate their signature.

node_id.description: The workflow step that produced it.

status.description: Where the signer is in the step. Only `signed` means the documents are signed.

verdict.description: The step's outcome. A warning sets it through its rule; custom status rules apply after.

level.description: `aes`. `qes` (Qualified Electronic Signature, QES) is coming soon.

name.description: Verified name.

role.description: The key person's designation, as declared.

roles.description: The key person's structured roles, as declared for the company.

identity_session_id.description: The KYC session that verified the signer.

expected_name.description: The name the signer had to match.

certificate.description: The certificate the documents were signed with. `null` until signed.

destination.description: The masked contact the code went to.

attempts.description: Codes entered, the right one included.

timestamp.description: The trusted timestamp in the signature. `null` until signed.

id.description: The document on this signer's copy. Use it to download the signed file.

uuid.description: Same as `id`.

pages.description: Pages of the document signed. For Word, of the converted PDF.

sha256_original.description: SHA-256 of the document as the signer was shown it.

sha256_signed.description: SHA-256 of the signed PDF, once signed.

status.description: `not_signed`: opened but not signed. `not_reached`: never opened.

read_at.description: When the signer reached the end of a document without fields, when the step requires it.

consented_at.description: When the signer agreed to a document without fields, or finished the fields of a document with fields.

signed_file.description: Path of the signed PDF, once signed. See [Download a signed document](/sessions-api/electronic-signature/download-signed-document).

mode.description: `fields` for a document with fields, `read_and_agree` for a document without.

source_format.description: `pdf`, or `docx` for a Word document Didit converted to PDF.

conversion.description: `null` for a PDF. For a Word document, the original file and the conversion.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of your original Word file.

size_bytes.description: Size of your original Word file.

converter.description: Version of the converter that produced the PDF.

fields.description: Fields on the document, with their values. Empty for a document without fields.

adopted_signature.description: The signature and initials the signer adopted for signature and initials fields. `null` until the signer adopts one.

method.description: `typed`: the verified name in a handwriting style. `drawn`: drawn with a finger or a mouse.

font.description: The handwriting style of a typed signature. `null` when drawn.

electronic_signature_consent_at.description: When the signer agreed, on the review screen, to sign the documents electronically. Set when any document has fields.

evidence_file.description: Path of the evidence PDF, once signed. See [Download the signature evidence](/sessions-api/electronic-signature/download-evidence).

warnings.description: Warnings raised for this signer. See [Electronic Signature warnings](/core-technology/electronic-signature/warnings-electronic-signature).

validation.description: The last cryptographic check of the signed documents. `null` until the documents are signed. If Didit can't confirm the outcome of signing, it's `{"valid": null, "reason": "signature_provider_outcome_unknown", "checked_at": ...}` and `status` stays `signing`: treat it as not signed.

valid.description: `true` when every document is valid. `null` when the outcome of signing couldn't be confirmed.

reason.description: Set when `valid` is `null`: `signature_provider_outcome_unknown`.

valid.description: `true` when the signature and the timestamp are both valid and trusted.

integrity.description: `true` when the document is unchanged since signing.

trusted.description: `true` when the signing certificate chains to a trusted root.

trusted_list.description: EU Trusted List check. For AES: `{"status": "not_applicable", "reason": "aes_not_qualified"}`.

certificate.description: The certificate the documents were signed with. `null` until signed.

timestamp.description: The trusted timestamp in the signature. `null` until signed.

expires_at.description: When the signing link stops working.

ip_address.description: The signer's IP address when they asked for their code.

SignatureFieldValidation.description: Rules for a `text` field's value. The console preview, the signing flow and the API apply the same rules.

kind.description: `letters`: letters in any script, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes. `number`: digits with an optional decimal separator. `pattern`: the value must match `pattern`.

pattern.description: Required with `kind: "pattern"`. A regular expression the whole value must match. Lookarounds and backreferences aren't supported.

message.description: Shown to the signer instead of the default error.

SignatureFieldAnchor.description: Places a field by a piece of text in the document instead of a position. Didit doesn't remove the text from the PDF, so write it in the same color as the page background. When the text isn't found, the call returns `400` with `field_anchor_not_found`. See [Place fields by anchor text](/sessions-api/create-session#place-fields-by-anchor-text).

text.description: Text searched in the document. For a Word file, in the converted PDF.

occurrence.description: `all` places one field per match; the keys after the first get `_2`, `_3` and so on.

offset_x.description: Added to the left edge of the text, as a fraction of the page width.

offset_y.description: Added to the top edge of the text, as a fraction of the page height.

width.description: Width of the field, as a fraction of the page width.

height.description: Height of the field, as a fraction of the page height.

SignatureFieldResult.description: A field of a signed document, with its value on this signer's copy. See [Fields](/core-technology/electronic-signature/report-electronic-signature#fields).

key.description: The field's key, as used in `sign.field_values`.

page.description: Page number, from 1. For a Word document, a page of the converted PDF.

x.description: Left edge, as a fraction of the page width.

y.description: Top edge, as a fraction of the page height.

width.description: Width, as a fraction of the page width.

height.description: Height, as a fraction of the page height.

value.description: A string for `text`, `email`, `full_name`, `date_signed` and `data`, a boolean for a `checkbox`, and `true` for an applied signature or initials. `null` when empty.

display_value.description: The value as stamped on the page: dates in the field's `date_format`, `Yes` or `No` for a checkbox, `Signed` for a signature or initials.

value_source.description: Where the value came from: `signer` (typed, ticked or applied by the signer), `identity` (the verified ID), `contact` (the verified email or phone), `company` (the verified company), `session` (`vendor_data`), `metadata`, `api` (`sign.field_values`) or `signing_time` (the date signed).

image_url.description: Signature and initials only: the path of the applied image. See [Download a signature image](/sessions-api/electronic-signature/download-field-image).

value_unavailable_reason.description: `source_empty` when a pre-filled field had no value in the session and `signature_field_data_missing_action` let the signer sign anyway.

VaspDirectoryWidgetEntry.description: What the end user's VASP picker shows: who the VASP is and whether it can be reached.

kind.description: directory for an entry of the shared directory; didit for a member of the Didit network.

jurisdiction.description: ISO 3166 country code, as the source gives it.

domains.description: The VASP's web domains. Always empty for Didit network members.

reachable.description: Whether your application has an available route to this VASP, or to one of its entities for a brand. Always true for a Didit network member.

TravelRuleDataSharingFields.description: The fields Didit sends to the counterparty VASP about your own users, per entity type. The `name` and the `wallet_address` are always sent, whatever the list says. An entity type you never chose shares every field. An empty list is a choice too: it shares the name and the wallet only.

individual.description: Fields shared about a natural person.

company.description: Fields shared about a legal person.

TravelRuleMatchingRules.description: How strictly each field of the counterparty's data is compared with what you hold, per entity type. A field you leave out keeps its default. `NONE` skips the comparison, `STRICT` needs exactly the same words, `CONTAINS` accepts one value whose words all appear in the other, `DEFAULT` is the standard subset match, and `FUZZY` accepts close spellings (and, for dates of birth, a swapped day and month).

name.description: Default: follows `name_matching_strictness`.

date_of_birth.description: Default `NONE`.

address.description: Default `NONE`.

account.description: The wallet the exchange was routed by. Default `STRICT`.

name.description: Default: follows `name_matching_strictness`.

address.description: Default `NONE`.

account.description: The wallet the exchange was routed by. Default `STRICT`.

TravelRuleDataMatch.description: Field-by-field comparison of the transfer's party data with what the other side knows about the wallet holder. It names fields and results, never values, so it stays readable while the counterparty's data is masked. Null until a comparison ran.

matched.description: True when no compared field differs.

fields.description: One entry per field compared for the party's entity type (`name`, `date_of_birth`, `address`, `account`; a company has no `date_of_birth`).

result.description: `not_compared` when the rule is `NONE` or either side has no value for the field.

TravelRuleDataUnmasked.description: Audit record of the moment the counterparty's data was unmasked. Null while the data is still masked, and for outbound transfers.

reason.description: What confirmed ownership: ownership_confirmed (your confirmation through the console or the API), wallet_proof (a wallet proof in the widget, or an INTERNAL inbound transfer, set when it is created), address_book_match (a verified address-book wallet), own_verified_wallet (your user's own verified wallet), inquiry_approved (your approval of an inbound TRP inquiry or a GTR or Sygna message), known_payment_method (a wallet your user already paid with) or travel_address (the per-wallet travel address named the wallet).

actor.description: Who confirmed it: the console user's email or the API key's label. Blank for an automatic decision.

TravelRuleMessageAttachment.description: The document attached to a message, stored like any other transaction document.

uploaded_by.description: Who attached it. In the pickup portal, a file you sent shows your VASP name, never the person or API key behind it.

direction.description: `OUTBOUND` is what the reader's own side sent. In the pickup portal the direction is from the counterparty's side.

author.description: Who wrote it on its own side: a console user's email or an API key label, or the other VASP's name.

requested_documents.description: What a DOCUMENT_REQUEST asks for, in the requester's words.

fulfilled_at.description: Set on a DOCUMENT_REQUEST once a reply to it carries a document.

TravelRuleMessageCreateRequest.description: Send as JSON, or as multipart/form-data with the attachments in `files`.

body.description: Required for a MESSAGE unless a file is attached.

requested_documents.description: Required (at least one) for a DOCUMENT_REQUEST, and only allowed there.

reply_to.description: A message of the same transfer. A reply that carries a document fulfils the document request it answers.

files.description: Multipart only. Up to 5 files of 10 MB each.

SessionDeletionJob.description: A bulk session deletion running in the background: progress and counts per outcome, never which sessions it deleted.

status.description: `PENDING`: accepted, not started yet. `PROCESSING`: deleting; `processed` and `outcomes` are updating. `COMPLETED`: every selected session is accounted for. `FAILED`: the job stopped early; see `error`.

total.description: Sessions selected when the deletion was requested.

processed.description: Sessions the job has finished with so far.

outcomes.description: How many sessions ended in each outcome. Every key is always present.

deleted.description: Sessions deleted together with their face embedding.

none.description: Sessions deleted that had no face embedding.

retained_with_user.description: Sessions deleted while one image-free biometric template was retained for their User, as the request or the application policy asked.

ineligible_no_vendor_user.description: Sessions deleted, with their face embedding, because retention was requested but they had no linked User.

failed_retryable.description: Sessions reported as not deleted. A job retries a group it could not delete by itself instead of counting it here.

already_deleted.description: Selected sessions that were already deleted, for example by another request, when the job reached them.

deleted_child_verifications.description: Verifications that the deleted business verifications created, deleted with them. Always `0` for a job started by `POST /v3/sessions/delete/`, which deletes KYC sessions only.

error.description: `null` unless `status` is `FAILED`; then why the deletion stopped. The sessions the job had not reached are still in place: repeat the request to delete them.

created_at.description: When the deletion was requested.

completed_at.description: When the job finished; `null` while it runs.

status.description: New lifecycle status. `BLOCKED` also adds the `vendor_data` to the system blocklist.

oneOf.description: Cost preview. Returned directly when estimate_only is true (nothing is written).

already_enabled.description: Profiles already monitored (nothing to do when enabling; these are what disabling turns off).

with_existing_aml.description: Profiles whose existing AML screening will be switched to monitored (no new screening).

needing_screening.description: Profiles without any AML screening that will be screened first (billed as a regular AML screening).

skipped_no_identity_data.description: Profiles that cannot be screened because identity data is missing.

skipped_blocked.description: Blocked users that will be skipped (always 0 for businesses).

estimated_screening_cost_usd.description: One-time cost of the new screenings.

estimated_annual_monitoring_cost_usd.description: Yearly monitoring cost of the profiles that will become monitored.

balance_sufficient.description: Whether the organization balance covers the screening plus the first year of monitoring.

unmatched.description: Identifiers of the request that matched no profile in this application, exactly as sent.

is_enabled.description: true when the job enables monitoring, false when it disables it.

target_type.description: Which profile family the job toggles.

outcomes.description: Per-record outcome counters. Every selected profile resolves to exactly one counter; nothing is silently skipped.

enabled.description: Monitoring enabled on an existing AML screening.

screened_and_enabled.description: A new AML screening was created (billed) and monitoring enabled on it.

already_enabled.description: Monitoring was already active; nothing changed and nothing was billed.

disabled.description: Monitoring turned off across every AML screening of the profile.

skipped_no_identity_data.description: Skipped: the profile lacks the full name, date of birth and country (users) or a name (businesses) needed to screen.
