count.description: Number of matching rows, capped at 100 for performance.

session_id.description: The unique identifier of the session.

session_kind.description: Discriminator indicating whether this is a User Verification (KYC) or Business Verification (KYB) session. When `user`, the KYC feature arrays (`id_verifications`, `nfc_verifications`, `liveness_checks`, `face_matches`, `poa_verifications`, `document_ai_documents`, `database_validations`, ...) apply and the business arrays are absent. When `business`, the payload instead carries `registry_checks`, `document_verifications`, `key_people_checks` plus the shared arrays (`aml_screenings`, `phone_verifications`, `email_verifications`, `ip_analyses`, `questionnaire_responses`). **Omitted when `include=events` is passed** — the events shape only exists for user sessions, so the discriminator is dropped from that variant.

shared_from_session.description: For a session cloned with `POST /v3/session/import-shared/`: the `session_id` of the original session in the source application. `null` for every other session. Omitted when `include=events` is passed.

status.description: Overall lifecycle status of the session — the rolled-up workflow result. Terminal values are `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review`, `Expired`, `Kyc Expired`, and `Abandoned`; `Not Started`, `In Progress`, `Awaiting User`, and `Resubmitted` indicate the session is still moving through the workflow.

workflow_id.description: Stable identifier of the workflow group that produced this session. Workflows are versioned — this value identifies the workflow itself, not the specific version.

items.description: The feature of the session.

features.description: List of verification features configured for this session, as display names: `ID_VERIFICATION`, `NFC`, `LIVENESS`, `FACE_MATCH`, `POA`, `PHONE`, `EMAIL_VERIFICATION`, `AML`, `IP_ANALYSIS`, `DATABASE_VALIDATION`, `QUESTIONNAIRE`, `AGE_ESTIMATION`, `FACE_SEARCH` (Business Verification sessions use the KYB feature set: `KYB_REGISTRY`, `KYB_DOCUMENTS`, `KYB_KEY_PEOPLE`, `AML`, `PHONE`, `EMAIL_VERIFICATION`, `IP_ANALYSIS`, `QUESTIONNAIRE`). With `include=events` each entry becomes an object `{feature, node_id}` instead of a plain string, and the email feature is renamed: it appears as `EMAIL` in events mode instead of the `EMAIL_VERIFICATION` used here.

vendor_data.description: The vendor data of the session.

metadata.description: The metadata of the session.

expected_details.description: Expected details supplied at session creation — used for cross-validation against extracted data (KYC) or to pre-fill the company registry search (KYB). Echoes back exactly the keys that were provided; `null` when none were supplied. KYC sessions carry the person fields; Business (KYB) sessions carry `company_name`, `registry_country` and `registration_number`.

date_of_birth.description: User's date of birth with format: YYYY-MM-DD. For example, `1990-05-15`.

gender.description: User's gender. Must be either 'M', 'F', or null.

nationality.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the applicant's country of origin. For example, `USA`.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the country of the Proof of Address document, or the country of the applicant's ID document, which may differ from nationality. For example, `GBR`.

address.description: The address in a human readable format, including as much information as possible. For example, `123 Main St, San Francisco, CA 94105, USA`.

identification_number.description: The user's document number, personal number, or tax number. For example, `123456789`.

ip_address.description: Expected IP address for the session. If the actual IP address differs from this value, a warning will be logged. For example, `192.168.1.100`.

expected_document_types.description: Document types the ID verification step was restricted to at session creation. Empty/unset means no restriction. Codes: `P` (passport), `ID` (national ID), `DL` (driver's license), `RP` (residence permit), `HIC` (health insurance card), `TC` (tax card), `SSC` (social security card).

id_country.description: Expected ID-document issuing country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3), when restricted at creation time.

poa_country.description: Expected Proof of Address document country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3), when restricted at creation time.

company_name.description: Expected legal name of the business. Business (KYB) sessions only.

registry_country.description: Expected registry country as `XX` or `XX-YY` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, optionally with an ISO 3166-2 subdivision for state-level registries, e.g. `US-CA`). Business (KYB) sessions only.

registration_number.description: Expected company registration number. Business (KYB) sessions only.

contact_details.description: Contact details supplied when the session was created (used for notification emails, prefilled phone/email verification, and communication language). `null` when neither an email nor a phone number was provided.

email.description: Email address of the user (e.g., "john.doe@example.com") that will be used during the Email Verification step. If not provided, the user must provide it during the verification flow.

email_lang.description: Language code (ISO 639-1) for email notifications. Controls the language of all email communications (e.g., "en", "es", "fr").

send_notification_emails.description: If true and an email is provided, Didit sends the initial "Verify your identity" email asynchronously when the User Verification (KYC) or Business Verification (KYB) session is created. Didit also sends verification status notifications for sessions requiring manual review to the provided email address.

phone.description: Phone number of the user in E.164 format if available (e.g., +14155552671). `null` when only an email was supplied at session creation. Note: This field returns the original phone number provided during session creation. If the number was invalid, it may not be in E.164 format.

callback.description: The callback URL of the session.

id_verifications.description: **Array of ID verification (OCR) reports** produced by ID-document steps in the workflow graph. Always a JSON array — read `id_verifications[0]` and iterate if your workflow can run more than one ID check (for example a primary check plus a step-up). `null` until at least one ID step has produced data. Each item is the full report, including `node_id`, feature-level `status`, extracted document fields, image URLs, quality scores, MRZ, address parsing, cross-session matches, and `warnings[]`.

items.description: One ID verification report - the full report for a single ID Verification step. `verification_method` says which of the three methods produced it (document capture, non-doc lookup or wallet sign-in) and the method-specific evidence block is populated accordingly.

node_id.description: Workflow graph node id of the OCR step that produced this report.

verification_method.description: Which ID Verification method produced this report. `document` - the user photographed a physical ID (the default, and the value on every session created before the other methods existed). `id_lookup` - the user typed their national ID number and it was checked against a government register or another authoritative source for that country (`id_lookup.source` names which). `wallet` - the user signed in with a government or bank digital identity.

assurance.description: Assurance tier derived from `verification_method`: `documentary` for a document that was captured and checked, `data_match` for details that matched a record held by the source queried, `cryptographic` for attributes an identity provider authenticated and signed.

wallet_provider.description: Catalog wallet id when `verification_method` is `wallet` (`mitid`, `bankid_se`, `itsme`, ...). `null` otherwise.

fallback_from.description: Why a non-document method ended the ID step. Set on the declined report when a lookup or a wallet sign-in failed and the country's fallback switch was `decline`. `null` otherwise.

reason.description: The outcome that ended it, e.g. `no_match`, `provider_error`, `cancelled`, `timeout`.

action.description: The configured action that was taken, e.g. `decline`.

id_lookup.description: Registry evidence. Present only when `verification_method` is `id_lookup`; `null` otherwise.

source.description: Customer-facing name of the source queried, e.g. `Department of Home Affairs` (a government register) or `UK credit bureau and financial services records` (not a government register). This is the only statement of provenance for the lookup; do not assume a government source.

attempts.description: 1-based attempt number this report came from.

max_attempts.description: Attempt budget configured for the country (1 to 5, default 1).

outcome.description: What the register answered. Only `match`, `partial_match` and `no_match` count against the attempt budget and bill.

comparison.description: One row per comparable field the source answered on, plus one row per source error. Comparison rows use the normalised field names below rather than the country's request field keys, because several request fields (first and last name, or any of the identifier aliases) collapse into a single comparison. A source that failed appends a row with `field: "provider"` and `result: "error"`, so read `result` before treating a row as a field verdict.

field.description: Normalised comparison field. `provider` is not a user field: it marks a source error row.

label.description: Display label for the row, e.g. `ID number`, `Full name`, `Provider`.

provided.description: What the user typed. `null` on a `provider` error row.

record.description: What the source held. On a `provider` error row this carries the error message instead.

result.description: Per-field comparison result. `error` appears only on a `provider` row and means that source did not answer; treat it as evidence about the query, never as a field mismatch.

registry_portrait.description: Short-lived presigned URL to the portrait the source returned. Only the four government registers that return one (South Africa, Nigeria, Argentina, Panama).

face_match_score.description: Selfie against the registry portrait, 0-100. Only where the register returns a portrait.

wallet_verification.description: Credential evidence. Present only when `verification_method` is `wallet`; `null` otherwise.

provider_name.description: Wallet name as the end user knows it, e.g. `MitID`.

issuing_authority.description: The authority behind the wallet, e.g. `Danish Agency for Digital Government`.

issuing_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country the wallet was offered in.

level_of_assurance.description: The level of assurance the wallet asserted. A sign-in that asserts less than the level requested fails instead of downgrading.

signature_valid.description: Whether the signed assertion the wallet returned validated.

attributes.description: The attributes the wallet shared, keyed as the wallet's catalog entry lists them.

portrait.description: Short-lived presigned URL to the portrait the wallet shared, where it shares one.

face_match_score.description: Selfie against the wallet portrait, 0-100, where the wallet shares one.

status.description: Feature-level status of this ID verification step. Independent of the top-level session `status` — a session can reach its overall decision while an individual feature stays `In Review`.

document_subtype.description: Accepted document subtype code from the workflow document settings, including the document region when applicable. Examples: `ID_CARD_GENERIC`, `QUEENSLAND_DRIVER_LICENSE_GENERIC`.

front_image.description: URL of the front document image

front_video.description: URL of the front document video

back_image.description: URL of the back document image

back_video.description: URL of the back document video

full_front_image.description: URL of the full front document image

full_back_image.description: URL of the full back document image

front_image_camera_front.description: URL of the front document image captured from the front-facing camera

back_image_camera_front.description: URL of the back document image captured from the front-facing camera

date_of_birth.description: Date of birth from document

age.description: Calculated age from date of birth

address.description: Raw address from document

extra_fields.description: Additional document fields. Includes document-specific attributes (e.g. `dl_categories`, `blood_group`, `sponsor`, `employer`, `dl_class_code_b_from`, `dl_class_code_b_to`). Driver license class validity dates are returned as `dl_class_code_<class>_from` and `dl_class_code_<class>_to`, and per-class restriction/information codes (e.g. column 12 of UK licences) as `dl_class_code_<class>_notes`. When the document carries names, address, or place of birth in multiple scripts, this object also includes alternate-script versions of those fields. The workflow setting `preferred_characters` (`latin` or `non_latin`) controls which script populates the top-level fields (`first_name`, `last_name`, `full_name`, `address`, `place_of_birth`); the opposite script lands here as `first_name_non_latin` / `last_name_non_latin` / `full_name_non_latin` / `middle_name_non_latin` / `address_non_latin` / `place_of_birth_non_latin` (when `preferred_characters` is `latin`) or with a `_latin` suffix (when `preferred_characters` is `non_latin`). Keys appear only when the OCR actually extracts a real alternate-script value — a field whose alternate value is in the same script as the preferred set (for example, a Cyrillic-labelled field whose OCR value came back in Latin homoglyphs) is skipped. When `preferred_characters` is `latin` but the document only carries non-Latin text, Didit transliterates the extracted values and exposes `first_name_latin` / `last_name_latin` / etc. as a fallback.

first_name_non_latin.description: First name in the non-Latin script when `preferred_characters=latin` and a non-Latin version is present on the document (e.g. `Айна` for a Kyrgyz ID).

last_name_non_latin.description: Surname in the non-Latin script when `preferred_characters=latin` and a non-Latin version is present on the document.

middle_name_non_latin.description: Middle name / patronymic in the non-Latin script when `preferred_characters=latin` and a non-Latin version is present on the document.

full_name_non_latin.description: Composed full name in the non-Latin script. Reconstructed from the individual components when both first and last names are available.

address_non_latin.description: Address in the non-Latin script when `preferred_characters=latin` and a non-Latin version is present on the document.

place_of_birth_non_latin.description: Place of birth in the non-Latin script when `preferred_characters=latin` and a non-Latin version is present on the document.

first_name_latin.description: First name in Latin script. Populated when `preferred_characters=non_latin` and a Latin version is present on the document, or — as a transliteration fallback — when `preferred_characters=latin` but the document only carries non-Latin text.

last_name_latin.description: Surname in Latin script. Same rules as `first_name_latin`.

middle_name_latin.description: Middle name / patronymic in Latin script. Same rules as `first_name_latin`.

full_name_latin.description: Composed full name in Latin script. Always reconstructed from the individual components when both first and last names are available.

address_latin.description: Address in Latin script. Same rules as `first_name_latin`.

place_of_birth_latin.description: Place of birth in Latin script. Same rules as `first_name_latin`.

mrz.description: Parsed Machine-Readable Zone (MRZ) fields extracted from the document. `null` if no MRZ was detected.

country.description: Two-letter country code

is_verified.description: Whether the address has been verified

front_image_camera_front_face_match_scor.description: Face match score between the portrait extracted from the front document image and the front camera image

back_image_camera_front_face_match_score.description: Face match score between the portrait extracted from the back document image and the front camera image

document_selfie_face_matches.description: Previous sessions or face blocklist entries whose face matched the selfie the front camera took during document capture (Silent Capture Face Search). Same entry format as `liveness_checks[].matches`. `null` for sessions created before this field existed or when the search did not run; an empty array when it ran and found nothing. `match_image_url` is a presigned URL that expires.

session_id.description: Session ID of the matching face. `null` when `source` is `imported`, `list_entry`, or `retained_template`.

similarity_percentage.description: Face similarity between the two images, clamped to 0–100.

vendor_data.description: `vendor_data` of the matching session or linked User for imported and retained-template faces.

vendor_user_id.description: Linked User id for `imported` and `retained_template` matches and for session matches linked to a User. `null` for list entries and sessions without a User.

biometric_template_id.description: Id of the retained biometric template. Set only when `source` is `retained_template`; `null` otherwise.

verification_date.description: When the matching face was captured, or when a retained template was created. `null` for list entries.

user_details.description: Identity data from the matching session or imported User profile. Always `null` for `retained_template` and `list_entry` matches.

match_image_url.description: Reference image for image-backed matches. Always `null` for `retained_template` matches because retained templates contain no image.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the matching session. `null` for non-session sources.

is_blocklisted.description: Whether the matching face is on a blocklist.

is_allowlisted.description: Whether the matching face is on an allowlist.

api_service.description: Standalone API service of the matching session (e.g. `PASSIVE_LIVENESS`, `FACE_MATCH`); `null` for workflow sessions and non-session sources.

source.description: Origin of the matching face: `session`, `imported` (User face upload), `list_entry` (allow/block list), or `retained_template` (an image-free biometric template stored on a User, listed under `/v3/biometric-templates/`).

front_image_quality_score.description: Quality metrics for the front document image. Each sub-score ranges from 0 to 100.

focus_score.description: Sharpness of the image measured via top-10% local Laplacian variance. Robust to documents with large uniform backgrounds. Higher values indicate a sharper, less blurry image.

brightness_score.description: How well-lit the image is. Penalizes images that are too dark or overexposed, with ideal brightness around mid-range.

brightness_issue.description: Indicates the direction of the brightness problem when the brightness_score is low. 'ok' means brightness is acceptable, 'too_dark' means the image is underexposed, 'too_bright' means the image is overexposed.

is_document_fully_visible.description: true if all four corners of the document are fully visible inside the image frame, false if any corner is cut off. Null when corner coordinates are unavailable.

resolution_score.description: Effective resolution of the image based on total pixel count.

overall_score.description: Weighted composite of sub-scores (focus 45%, brightness 30%, resolution 25%).

back_image_quality_score.description: Quality metrics for the back document image. Same structure as front_image_quality_score.

focus_score.description: Sharpness of the image measured via top-10% local Laplacian variance. Robust to documents with large uniform backgrounds. Higher values indicate a sharper, less blurry image.

brightness_score.description: How well-lit the image is. Penalizes images that are too dark or overexposed, with ideal brightness around mid-range.

brightness_issue.description: Indicates the direction of the brightness problem when the brightness_score is low. 'ok' means brightness is acceptable, 'too_dark' means the image is underexposed, 'too_bright' means the image is overexposed.

is_document_fully_visible.description: true if all four corners of the document are fully visible inside the image frame, false if any corner is cut off. Null when corner coordinates are unavailable.

resolution_score.description: Effective resolution of the image based on total pixel count.

overall_score.description: Weighted composite of sub-scores (focus 45%, brightness 30%, resolution 25%).

feature.description: The feature that generated this warning (e.g., `ID_VERIFICATION`, `NFC`, `LIVENESS`). The value identifies the feature block the warning belongs to. Each module's warnings array typically uses the value matching its module, but the enum above is authoritative across all feature warnings on the decision payload.

additional_data.description: Additional contextual data about the warning

log_type.description: Type of log: information, warning, or error

node_id.description: The workflow graph node ID that generated this warning (for graph-based workflows)

warnings.description: Document verification warnings

matches.description: Matching documents found during duplicate/blocklist detection (up to 5 matches)

score.description: Likelihood that the document is genuine for this fraud type, 0-100 (higher = more likely genuine). The lowest of the two sides - the value the decision used. `null` when neither side produced a usable score.

front.description: Score for the front side; `null` when not captured or when the score was dropped.

back.description: Score for the back side; `null` when not captured or when the score was dropped.

bucket.description: The fraud-type bucket saved at evaluation time. Null when there is no usable score, the check was not applied, or historical evaluation evidence is unavailable. Later workflow edits do not change it.

nfc_skip_reason.description: Why NFC chip verification did not run, populated whenever the workflow includes an NFC step. `null` while NFC is pending or when the chip was actually read. Values: `USER_SKIPPED` - the user chose to skip on an NFC-capable device (allowed by `allow_nfc_skip`); `DOCUMENT_WITHOUT_CHIP` - the document has no readable NFC chip (not an ICAO 9303 electronic document); `CHIP_CERTIFICATE_UNAVAILABLE` - the issuing country's signing certificate (CSCA) covering the document's issue period is unavailable, so the chip signature cannot be verified; `DEVICE_WITHOUT_NFC` - the device reported no NFC reader; `INTEGRATION_WITHOUT_NFC_ACCESS` - the verification ran without a native SDK (e.g. in a web browser), which has no access to the phone's NFC reader; `MRZ_KEY_UNAVAILABLE` - the chip access key could not be derived from the document's MRZ; `JPKI_UNAVAILABLE` - the document is a Japan My Number Card, whose chip is read through JPKI, and JPKI was not available for this verification: it is not enabled, or the app's native SDK cannot read My Number Cards.

nfc_verifications.description: **Array of NFC / ePassport reports** produced by NFC steps in the workflow graph. **This is always a JSON array, never a singular `nfc` object** — read `nfc_verifications[0]` and iterate if your workflow can run NFC more than once. `null` until at least one NFC step has produced data. Each item is the full report, including `node_id`, feature-level `status`, `chip_protocol`, `chip_data`, `authenticity` (SOD + DG integrity), `certificate_summary`, and `warnings[]`. A Japan My Number Card is read through JPKI instead of ICAO 9303: its item has `chip_protocol: "jpki"`, carries its evidence under `jpki`, and leaves the ICAO fields `null`. When the NFC step was bypassed before it could ever be offered (chipless document, missing certificate, no NFC capability reported, unreadable MRZ key, JPKI unavailable for a My Number Card), this stays `null` and `nfc_skip_reason` explains why; a skip at the step itself (user tapped skip, or the reader turned out unavailable at scan time) still produces a report with `is_nfc_skipped: true`.

items.description: One NFC report: the full report for a single chip read (an ICAO 9303 ePassport or eID chip, or a Japan My Number Card read through JPKI).

node_id.description: Workflow graph node id of the NFC step that produced this report. Use it to correlate the report with the workflow definition.

status.description: Feature-level status of this NFC step. Independent of the top-level session `status` — a session can reach its overall decision while an individual feature stays `In Review`.

is_nfc_skipped.description: `true` when this NFC step was explicitly skipped instead of read; `skip_reason` says why.

skip_reason.description: Why this NFC step was skipped. Only set when `is_nfc_skipped` is `true`. Same taxonomy as the session-level `nfc_skip_reason`, which additionally covers the cases where NFC never produced a report at all.

chip_protocol.description: How the NFC step reads the chip. `icao`: ICAO 9303 ePassport or eID chip, opened with the access key from the MRZ. `jpki`: Japan My Number Card, where the card signs a one-time challenge after the holder enters the card PIN in a native SDK; the result is under `jpki`. Also set on skipped steps, so you can tell a skipped My Number Card read apart.

jpki.description: What a Japan My Number Card read through JPKI proved. Present when `chip_protocol` is `jpki` and the card was read. `null` for ICAO chips, for skipped steps, and when the NFC step closed without any card read (that case raises `JPKI_SIGNATURE_INVALID`). Never carries the certificates, their serial numbers, the signatures or the 12-digit My Number.

certificate_types.description: The card certificates read. `user_authentication` (4-digit PIN) is always read; `signature` (signature PIN) is read when the NFC node's `jpki_request_attributes` setting is on.

chain_valid.description: `true` when every certificate read chains to the JPKI certification authority, is inside its validity period and is a My Number Card certificate of its type.

signature_valid.description: `true` when every signature the card made over the one-time challenge verifies. The card only signs after its PIN is entered, so this proves possession of the card and knowledge of the PIN.

revocation_status.description: `good` when the revocation check confirmed every certificate is valid, `revoked` when any certificate is revoked (for example a card reported lost), `unchecked` when no revocation answer was available. `unchecked` is never treated as `good`: the NFC node's `jpki_revocation_unchecked_action` decides the outcome (default `REVIEW`).

ca_generation.description: Generation of the JPKI certification authority that issued the certificates, for example `2023`. `null` when no certificate chains to one.

certificate_expires_at.description: The earliest expiry among the certificates read.

items.description: What one certificate read from the card proved. Never the certificate itself or its serial number.

type.description: Which card certificate this entry describes.

chain_valid.description: `true` when the certificate chains to the JPKI certification authority of its type, is inside its validity period and is a My Number Card certificate of that type.

signature_valid.description: `true` when the card's signature over the one-time challenge verifies against this certificate.

ca_generation.description: Generation of the JPKI certification authority that issued the certificate, for example `2023`. `null` when no trusted issuer was found.

not_valid_before.description: Start of the certificate's validity period. `null` when the certificate could not be read.

not_valid_after.description: End of the certificate's validity period. `null` when the certificate could not be read.

failure.description: Why `chain_valid` is `false`: `unreadable_certificate`, `untrusted_issuer` (not issued by the JPKI certification authority of its type), `expired`, `not_yet_valid`, `wrong_policy` (not a My Number Card certificate of that type) or `key_usage` (the key may not sign). `null` when the chain is valid.

certificates.description: Per-certificate results, one entry per certificate read.

attributes.description: The holder's data from the signature certificate, once its chain is valid. `null` when the signature certificate was not requested or did not chain to the JPKI certification authority.

full_name.description: Name as registered, usually in Japanese script.

date_of_birth.description: Date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`. `null` when the registered date is incomplete.

address.description: Registered address.

name_substitute_characters.description: Position string marking the characters of `full_name` that were replaced by a substitute because the original character is outside the standard character set. `null` when none were replaced.

address_substitute_characters.description: Position string marking substitute characters in `address`, as for `name_substitute_characters`.

attributes_match_ocr.description: `true` when the attributes match the data read from the photo of the same card, `false` when any attribute differs (`JPKI_AND_OCR_DATA_NOT_SAME`), `null` when nothing could be compared, including whenever `attributes` is `null`.

mismatched_attributes.description: Names of the attributes that differ from the photo data, never their values. Empty when everything compared matches.

portrait_image.description: Presigned URL to the portrait read from the chip (ICAO DG2). `null` for a JPKI read (`chip_protocol: "jpki"`) and for skipped steps.

signature_image.description: Presigned URL to the holder's signature image read from the chip (ICAO DG7), when the chip stores one. `null` for a JPKI read (`chip_protocol: "jpki"`) and for skipped steps.

chip_data.description: Personal data parsed from the ICAO chip's Data Groups. `null` for a JPKI read (`chip_protocol: "jpki"`) and for skipped steps.

authenticity.description: ICAO passive authentication: SOD signature (`sod_integrity`) and Data Group hashes (`dg_integrity`). `null` for a JPKI read, which reports its proof under `jpki`.

certificate_summary.description: Summary of the ICAO Document Signer Certificate. `null` for a JPKI read (`chip_protocol: "jpki"`) and for skipped steps.

feature.description: The feature that generated this warning. The value identifies the feature block the warning belongs to. Each module's warnings array typically uses the value matching its module (e.g. `PHONE` inside `phone_verifications[].warnings`), but the enum above is authoritative across all feature warnings on the decision payload.

Each item is the full report, including `node_id`, feature-level `status`, `method`, `score`, `reference_image`, `video_url`, optional `age_estimation`, cross-session `matches[]`, and `warnings[]`.

node_id.description: Workflow graph node id of the liveness step that produced this report.

status.description: Feature-level status of this liveness step. Independent of the top-level session `status` — a session can reach its overall decision while an individual feature stays `In Review`.

reference_image.description: URL of the reference image used

video_url.description: URL of the liveness check video

matches.description: Similar faces found by the duplicate-face search (top matches, blocklisted/allowlisted entries first). Each entry's `source` tells you where the matching face came from: `session` (another verification session), `imported` (a face uploaded against a vendor user), `list_entry` (an org-managed allow/block list face), or `retained_template` (an image-free biometric template stored on a User, listed under `/v3/biometric-templates/`). `session_id`, `session_number`, `status` and `api_service` are `null` for non-session sources. `imported` matches still populate `vendor_data`, `verification_date` and — when the vendor user has a name on file — `user_details` (with `full_name` only) from the vendor-user record; `retained_template` matches populate `vendor_user_id`, `vendor_data`, `biometric_template_id` and `verification_date`, while their image and identity fields are `null`; `list_entry` matches return all of these as `null`.

session_id.description: Session ID of the matching face. `null` when `source` is `imported`, `list_entry`, or `retained_template`.

similarity_percentage.description: Face similarity between the two images, clamped to 0–100.

vendor_data.description: `vendor_data` of the matching session or linked User for imported and retained-template faces.

vendor_user_id.description: Linked User id for `imported` and `retained_template` matches and for session matches linked to a User. `null` for list entries and sessions without a User.

biometric_template_id.description: Id of the retained biometric template. Set only when `source` is `retained_template`; `null` otherwise.

verification_date.description: When the matching face was captured, or when a retained template was created. `null` for list entries.

user_details.description: Identity data from the matching session or imported User profile. Always `null` for `retained_template` and `list_entry` matches.

match_image_url.description: Reference image for image-backed matches. Always `null` for `retained_template` matches because retained templates contain no image.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the matching session. `null` for non-session sources.

is_blocklisted.description: Whether the matching face is on a blocklist.

is_allowlisted.description: Whether the matching face is on an allowlist.

api_service.description: Standalone API service of the matching session (e.g. `PASSIVE_LIVENESS`, `FACE_MATCH`); `null` for workflow sessions and non-session sources.

source.description: Origin of the matching face: `session`, `imported` (User face upload), `list_entry` (allow/block list), or `retained_template` (an image-free biometric template stored on a User, listed under `/v3/biometric-templates/`).

node_id.description: The workflow graph node ID that generated this warning

matches.description: Cross-session matches found for this entry's IP address or device identity. Every match is another verification session in your application (`source` is always `session`) that shares the same value, always belonging to a different vendor user / `vendor_data` than the current session, capped at 5 per collector (`device_fingerprint` sums two independently capped collectors, so up to 10 entries are possible). Every item carries `match_source`, `confidence`, `match_mode`, `device_info` and `location_info`; the keys `recovery_similarity`, `tls_ja4_corroborated` and `recovery_gate_reason` are present only when `match_source` is `recovered_high`.

session_id.description: Session ID of the matching session.

session_number.description: Sequential number of the matching session.

vendor_data.description: `vendor_data` of the matching session — always different from the current session's vendor user.

verification_date.description: Creation date of the matching session (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`).

match_type.description: Whether the match was on IP address or device fingerprint

match_source.description: How this match was reached: `ip_address` (shared IP address — network co-location, not a device-identity claim), `persistent_id` (exact stored persistent device identifier), `legacy_fp` (legacy `didit-fp-*` device-fingerprint hash), or `recovered_high` (high-confidence fuzzy fingerprint-recovery hit). Lower-confidence recovery candidates surface as risk warnings only, never in this array.

matched_value.description: The value that matched: the shared IP address, the persistent device identifier or legacy fingerprint hash, or — for `recovered_high` — the UUID of the recovered device.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the matching session.

is_blocklisted.description: Whether the matched value is on a blocklist. Currently always `false` for device/IP matches.

api_service.description: Standalone API service of the matching session; `null` for workflow sessions.

source.description: Always `session` for device/IP matches — every match is another verification session in your application.

device_info.description: Device details observed on the matching session.

location_info.description: Network and geolocation details observed on the matching session.

confidence.description: Server-side identification confidence, computed as `1 - P(false positive)`: `1.0` for deterministic matches (`persistent_id`, or hardware-rooted `recovered_high`), `0.5` for `legacy_fp`, `0.0` for `ip_address` (co-location only), and a corroboration-adjusted value below `1.0` for probabilistic recovered matches (higher when the TLS JA4 fingerprint and IP country independently agree).

match_mode.description: Evidence class of the match: `deterministic` (exact stored or hardware-rooted identifier that cannot collide between physical devices), `probabilistic` (fuzzy fingerprint evidence), or `co_occurrence` (shared network only, no device-identity claim).

recovery_similarity.description: Cosine similarity of the fingerprint-recovery match, rounded to 4 decimals. Present only when `match_source` is `recovered_high`.

tls_ja4_corroborated.description: Whether the TLS JA4 fingerprints of the two observations agree — a server-observed signal the browser cannot spoof. Present only when `match_source` is `recovered_high`.

recovery_gate_reason.description: Why the recovery match passed the false-positive hard gate: `hardware_root_match` (a hardware-rooted device identifier matched exactly) or, on configurations that admit probe-only evidence, `exact_composite_plus_<n>_families` / `very_high_similarity_plus_<n>_families`. Present only when `match_source` is `recovered_high`.

node_id.description: Unique identifier for this database validation step in the workflow graph.

issuing_state.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code of the country whose government/registry sources were queried (e.g. `BRA`, `MEX`, `ESP`, `NGA`, `IDN`). Database Validation covers 60+ countries across the Americas, Europe, Africa, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific, plus global multi-country sources — coverage expands regularly, so treat the value as an open set rather than a fixed enum.

validation_type.description: How the result was corroborated: `one_by_one` (single-service outcome), `two_by_two` (two or more distinct services independently full-matched the identification number), or `not_enabled` (persisted when no service produced a usable match). The value is never `null`. Dedicated biometric 2x2 validation modes are currently available for `ECU` and `PER`.

screened_data.description: The input data used for validation. Fields vary by country — see the Database Validation docs (`/core-technology/database-validation/overview`) for country-specific formats.

personal_number.description: Chile: RUT, DOM: Cédula (11 digits), ECU: Cédula (10 digits), ESP: DNI/NIE, MEX: CURP (18 chars), PER: DNI (8 digits), URY: CI

document_number.description: ARG: DNI, BOL: CI, COL: Cédula, GTM: DPI, HND: DNI, PAN: Cédula, PRY: CI, SLV: DUI, VEN: Cédula

validations.description: One entry per registry service that returned a validation payload. Each entry identifies the service (`service_id`, `service_name`) and carries the per-field `validation` comparison, the service `outcome_code` / `outcome_detail` when reported, and the normalised registry record in `source_data`.

service_id.description: Identifier of the registry service that produced this validation result.

service_name.description: Human-readable name of the registry service.

validation.description: The results of the field validations.

date_of_birth.description: Match result for date of birth.

outcome_code.description: Machine-readable outcome of the registry lookup (e.g. `MATCH`, `NO_MATCH`, `PARTIAL_MATCH`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, source-specific codes). Present when the service reports one.

outcome_detail.description: Human-readable explanation of `outcome_code`, when provided by the service.

source_data.description: The data returned from the government database. Common fields: identification_number, first_name, last_name, full_name, date_of_birth, gender. Additional fields by country: BRA always includes lgpd_minor, minor_under_18, and minor_under_16 on successful CPF matches; it also includes the upstream HTTP status when CPF data is withheld under LGPD (HTTP 422/451). ECU adds street, formatted_address, nationality, education, marital_status, spouse, mother_name, father_name, profession. PER adds paternal_name, maternal_name, verification_number, verification_letter. ESP adds document_type, expiration_date. VEN/COL add document_type.

errors.description: Errors returned by registry services while validating, each tagged with the `service_id` that produced it. **This key is omitted entirely when there are no errors.**

items.description: The upstream service's error object spread as-is — its keys vary by service (commonly a message/code and any provider-specific details) — plus `service_id` identifying the service that errored.

service_id.description: Identifier of the registry service that errored.

match_type.description: The aggregate match outcome across the queried services. `null` until the validation has been evaluated.

status.description: Feature-level status of this database validation. Independent of the top-level session `status` — a session can reach its overall decision while an individual feature stays `In Review`.

feature.description: The feature that generated this warning. The value identifies the feature block the warning belongs to. Each module's warnings array typically uses the value matching its module (e.g. `PHONE` inside `phone_verifications[].warnings`), but the enum above is authoritative across all feature warnings on the decision payload.

node_id.description: The workflow graph node ID that generated this warning

warnings.description: Warnings related to the database validation.

user.description: Who performed the review. Usually the console reviewer's identifier (their email), but the value is `"API Client"` for status updates made with an API key and `"Unknown"` when no actor could be resolved — so do not parse this field as an email address.

created_at.description: Timestamp at which the session was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

expires_at.description: Timestamp at which this session is scheduled to expire. Set on User Verification (KYC) sessions when an expiration was configured at creation time (or once `Approved` status triggers KYC expiry computation). `null` for sessions without a configured expiration, and for kinds that do not use expiry (e.g. Business Verification (KYB) sessions that never received an `expires_at`).

registry_checks.description: Company registry checks. Present only when `session_kind = business`. Each item wraps the full company-registry payload.

items.description: One company registry check — the full company-registry payload enriched with ownership structure and warnings. Present only when `session_kind = business`.

status.description: Feature lifecycle status.

company.description: Full registry payload for the company (registry record merged with any user-provided or console-edited data).

region.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code when applicable (e.g. `CA`, `NY` for US states).

alternative_names.description: Alternative, trading, former or original-language company names as text, when reported.

registered_capital_amount.description: Registered/share capital amount as a decimal string (e.g. `"100.00"`), parsed from the registry filing. `null` when not available.

registered_capital_currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code of `registered_capital_amount` (e.g. `"GBP"`). `null` when not available.

vat_number.description: EU VAT number, when collected during the hosted registry step or edited afterwards.

vat_validation_status.description: Result of validating the VAT number or, when there is none, the `tax_number`, at registry submit. `valid` / `invalid`: decided by the official registry of the country (EU VIES, Norway, Switzerland, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Paraguay; Poland also by its domestic VAT register). `format_valid` / `invalid_format`: decided by the country's format and check-digit rules where no registry can be queried. `could_not_validate`: the registry was unavailable. `not_applicable`: no number, a country without registry or rules, or a sandbox session.

vat_validated_number.description: The number that was checked, as the source knows it (for example the VAT number derived from a French SIREN or a Dutch RSIN). `null` when no check ran.

vat_validation_source.description: The source that decided `vat_validation_status`: an official registry, or `format_rules`. `null` when no check ran.

vat_validated_name.description: Name registered with the source that validated the number, when it discloses one. Only set when the status is `valid`.

vat_validated_address.description: Address registered with the source that validated the number, when it discloses one. Only set when the status is `valid`.

vat_checked_at.description: Timestamp of the check. `null` when no check ran.

first_name.description: Given name when explicitly reported by the registry; not inferred from the full name.

last_name.description: Family name when explicitly reported by the registry.

address.description: Officer address reported by the registry.

termination_date.description: Date the appointment ended, when reported.

date_of_birth.description: Complete registry-reported birth date. Null when only a birth year or month is known.

date_of_birth_year.description: Registry-reported birth year, including when the full date is unavailable.

date_of_birth_month.description: Registry-reported birth month. Null when only the year is known.

ownership_min_shares.description: Lower bound of the ownership percentage as reported by the registry. Free-form string (e.g. `"25.00"`, `"50"`); use `effective_ownership_percent` for a parsed numeric value.

ownership_max_shares.description: Upper bound of the ownership percentage as reported by the registry. Free-form string; use `effective_ownership_percent` for a parsed numeric value.

date_of_birth.description: Complete birth date when reported.

addresses.description: Every address the registry states, one canonical shape. Null when it states none.

industries.description: The activities the registry classifies the company under, one canonical shape. Null when it states none.

accounts.description: Registry filing dates, when available. Annual returns and general meetings use last_annual_return_date and last_agm_date; they are distinct from financial accounts.

registry_data.description: Raw record returned by the registry source, kept for reviewers. Its shape differs by country and source and is not a stable contract: read the canonical fields (`addresses`, `industries`, `ownership`, `beneficial_owners[].shareholding`) instead.

user_provided_data.description: Data confirmed or edited by the end user.

registry_tier.description: The registry tier the workflow ordered: `basic`, `shareholders` or `ubo`. Also in `ownership.tier_requested`.

registry_tier_delivered.description: The tier the registry delivered and that is billed. Also in `ownership.tier_delivered`.

ownership_structure.description: Raw ownership snapshot kept for reviewers; its shape differs by registry source and is not a stable contract. Read `company.beneficial_owners` and `company.ownership` instead.

key_people_checks.description: Aggregate key-people checks. Present only when `session_kind = business`. Each item uses the two-bucket shape (`registry`, `submitted`, `ubo_kyc_summary`).

items.description: Aggregate check over the company's officers + UBOs. Uses the `registry` / `submitted` shape. Present only when session_kind = business.

registry.description: Parties discovered via the registry check.

officers.description: Officers discovered via the registry check, each enriched with the status of any child KYC session and AML screening spawned for them.

name.description: Officer's full name as recorded in the registry.

designation.description: Free-text designation from the registry (e.g. `Director`, `Company Secretary`).

termination_date.description: Date the appointment ended, when reported.

address.description: Officer address reported by the registry.

aml_status.description: Status of the AML screening run for this officer. `null` when no AML screening was run.

kyc_status.description: Raw lifecycle status of the child KYC session spawned for this officer. This is the full session status enum (not a reduced Approved/Declined/Pending set). `null` when no child KYC session exists.

kyc_session_url.description: Shareable URL of the child KYC session. `null` when no child session exists.

kyc_session_id.description: Session id of the child KYC session. Pass it to this same decision endpoint to fetch the person's full KYC report. `null` when no child session exists.

verification_workflow_type.description: Base workflow type of the child session's workflow (e.g. `kyc`). `null` for graph-based workflows or when no child session exists.

verification_workflow_id.description: Workflow id used by the child session. `null` when no child session exists.

verification_workflow_label.description: Human-readable label of the child session's workflow. `null` when unset.

verification_workflow_features.description: Per-feature progress of the child verification session, e.g. `[{"feature": "ID_VERIFICATION", "status": "Approved"}]`. `null` when the child session has no resolvable feature list.

feature.description: Feature display name (e.g. `ID_VERIFICATION`, `LIVENESS`, `AML`).

status.description: Feature-level status inside the child session.

didit_internal_id.description: Stable internal identifier of the verified individual behind the child session — useful for cross-session linking. `null` when no child session exists or the user has not been resolved yet.

kyc_document_type.description: Document type presented in the child KYC session (e.g. `P`, `ID`, `DL`). `null` until the child session has an ID verification result.

kyc_nationality.description: Nationality extracted from the document in the child KYC session. `null` until available.

kyc_liveness_passed.description: Whether the child KYC session's liveness check passed. `null` when no liveness check has run.

kyc_verified_at.description: When the child KYC session reached `Approved`. `null` while the child session has any other status.

kyc_aml_categories.description: Per-category summary derived from the person's AML hits. `null` when there are no hits.

kyc_notification_sent_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last verification-invite notification sent for this person's child session. `null` when none was sent.

first_name.description: Given name when explicitly reported by the registry; not inferred from the full name.

last_name.description: Family name when explicitly reported by the registry.

date_of_birth.description: Complete registry-reported birth date. Null when only a birth year or month is known.

date_of_birth_year.description: Registry-reported birth year, including when the full date is unavailable.

date_of_birth_month.description: Registry-reported birth month. Null when only the year is known.

beneficial_owners.description: Beneficial owners discovered via the registry check, each enriched with the status of any child KYC session and AML screening spawned for them.

name.description: Beneficial owner's full name (or company name for corporate UBOs).

date_of_birth.description: Complete birth date when reported.

roles.description: Role names held by this owner, e.g. `["ubo", "shareholder"]`.

ownership_min_shares.description: Lower bound of the ownership percentage as reported by the registry. Free-form string (e.g. `"25"`, `"25-50%"`); use `effective_ownership_percent` for a parsed numeric value.

ownership_max_shares.description: Upper bound of the ownership percentage as reported by the registry. Free-form string; use `effective_ownership_percent` for a parsed numeric value.

aml_status.description: Status of the AML screening run for this beneficial owner. `null` when no AML screening was run.

kyc_status.description: Raw lifecycle status of the child KYC session spawned for this beneficial owner. This is the full session status enum (not a reduced Approved/Declined/Pending set). `null` when no child KYC session exists.

kyc_session_url.description: Shareable URL of the child KYC session. `null` when no child session exists.

kyc_session_id.description: Session id of the child KYC session. Pass it to this same decision endpoint to fetch the person's full KYC report. `null` when no child session exists.

verification_workflow_type.description: Base workflow type of the child session's workflow (e.g. `kyc`). `null` for graph-based workflows or when no child session exists.

verification_workflow_id.description: Workflow id used by the child session. `null` when no child session exists.

verification_workflow_label.description: Human-readable label of the child session's workflow. `null` when unset.

verification_workflow_features.description: Per-feature progress of the child verification session, e.g. `[{"feature": "ID_VERIFICATION", "status": "Approved"}]`. `null` when the child session has no resolvable feature list.

feature.description: Feature display name (e.g. `ID_VERIFICATION`, `LIVENESS`, `AML`).

status.description: Feature-level status inside the child session.

didit_internal_id.description: Stable internal identifier of the verified individual behind the child session — useful for cross-session linking. `null` when no child session exists or the user has not been resolved yet.

kyc_document_type.description: Document type presented in the child KYC session (e.g. `P`, `ID`, `DL`). `null` until the child session has an ID verification result.

kyc_nationality.description: Nationality extracted from the document in the child KYC session. `null` until available.

kyc_liveness_passed.description: Whether the child KYC session's liveness check passed. `null` when no liveness check has run.

kyc_verified_at.description: When the child KYC session reached `Approved`. `null` while the child session has any other status.

kyc_aml_categories.description: Per-category summary derived from the person's AML hits. `null` when there are no hits.

kyc_notification_sent_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last verification-invite notification sent for this person's child session. `null` when none was sent.

child_beneficial_owners.description: For corporate UBOs: the owning entity's own beneficial owners, as raw objects extracted from the registry. Empty array when not applicable.

effective_ownership_percent.description: Parsed numeric ownership percentage — the max bound when available, otherwise the min bound. `null` when neither bound could be parsed.

submitted.description: Parties submitted by the business admin during the Key People flow (BusinessParty rows where source=USER).

items.description: Party submitted by the business admin via the Key People flow (source=USER).

source.description: Always `USER` here — this bucket only contains parties entered or confirmed by the end user in the Key People flow (registry-discovered people appear under `registry`).

nationality.description: Nationality for persons; country of incorporation for company parties.

custom_fields.description: Workflow-defined custom fields collected for this party; keys are defined by the workflow's key-people field descriptors.

is_skipped.description: True when the end user skipped verification for this party (only possible when the role allows skipping).

requires_verification.description: True when a child KYC / KYB sub-session is required for this party based on role settings and ownership thresholds.

roles.description: All roles held by this party, each with its own ownership and voting percentages. There is no scalar `role`/`ownership_percent` on the party itself.

kyc_session_id.description: Child KYC session id for person parties requiring verification. `null` otherwise.

kyc_session_status.description: Lifecycle status of the child KYC session. `null` when no child KYC session exists.

kyb_sub_session_id.description: Child KYB sub-session id for corporate parties requiring verification. `null` otherwise.

kyb_sub_session_status.description: Lifecycle status of the child KYB sub-session. `null` when no sub-session exists.

kyb_sub_session_url.description: Shareable URL of the child KYB sub-session. `null` when no sub-session exists.

verification_workflow_type.description: Base workflow type of the child session's workflow (KYC session preferred, falling back to the KYB sub-session). `null` for graph-based workflows or when no child session exists.

verification_workflow_id.description: Workflow id used by the child session. `null` when no child session exists.

verification_workflow_label.description: Human-readable label of the child session's workflow. `null` when unset.

verification_workflow_features.description: Per-feature progress of the child verification session, e.g. `[{"feature": "ID_VERIFICATION", "status": "Approved"}]`. `null` when the child session has no resolvable feature list.

feature.description: Feature display name (e.g. `ID_VERIFICATION`, `LIVENESS`, `AML`).

status.description: Feature-level status inside the child session.

didit_internal_id.description: Stable internal identifier of the verified individual behind the child session. `null` when not resolved.

ubo_kyc_summary.description: Aggregate UBO KYC progress, or null when no UBOs have linked KYC sessions.

flagged.description: UBOs whose KYC is Declined or In Review.

document_verifications.description: Document verification checks grouped by workflow node. Present only when `session_kind = business`.

items.description: Documents grouped by workflow node. Present only when session_kind = business.

document_type.description: High-level KYB document group the file was classified into. `null` while unclassified.

document_subtype.description: Specific OCR-detected subtype (e.g. `CERTIFICATE_OF_INCORPORATION`, `SHAREHOLDER_REGISTRY`); `UNKNOWN` when the OCR could not confidently classify the document.

document_group.description: Alias of `document_type` — the group name used by `groups` and `required_groups`.

file_url.description: Short-lived presigned link to the uploaded file. `null` for analyst-created document request placeholders (`is_requested = true`) that have not been fulfilled yet.

original_filename.description: Filename as uploaded by the user or analyst.

status.description: Per-document verification status.

cross_check_result.description: Cross-reference of the OCR-extracted document fields against the registry company profile. An object with `critical`, `non_critical` and `people` sections, each mapping a field name (e.g. `company_name`, `registration_number`, `incorporation_date`, `registered_address`) to a comparison record like `{"document": "...", "registry": "...", "match": true, "score": 0.97}`. `null` when the document had no OCR data or there was no registry company to compare against.

document_metadata.description: Metadata extracted from the uploaded corporate document. When metadata extraction succeeded, all 16 keys are always present (individual values are `null` when not applicable to the file type); the whole object is `null` when nothing could be extracted. For PDFs, `overlay_manipulation` carries forensic overlay-text analysis.

creation_date.description: Date when the document was created.

modified_date.description: Date when the document was modified.

creator.description: Authoring tool/user recorded in the file metadata (PDF `Creator`).

software.description: Editing software recorded in the file metadata.

encryption.description: Encryption scheme of the file, when encrypted.

is_signed.description: Whether the document carries a digital signature.

is_tampered.description: Whether the digital signature failed validation (post-signing modification).

signature_info.description: Details of the digital signature(s), when present.

exif_original_date.description: EXIF original capture date, for image uploads.

exif_digitized_date.description: EXIF digitization date, for image uploads.

processed_by_known_editor.description: Whether metadata indicates the file passed through a known image/PDF editor.

has_different_creation_mod_date.description: Whether creation and modification dates differ — a possible (but not conclusive) editing signal.

overlay_manipulation.description: PDF forensic analysis for suspected overlay-text manipulation. Null when no overlay manipulation evidence was found or the document was not a PDF.

detected.description: Whether overlay-text manipulation evidence was detected.

analyzed.description: Whether the PDF could be analyzed.

signals.description: Forensic signals that fired, such as duplicate_font_subset or glyph_fragmentation.

manipulated_regions.description: Suspected manipulated areas in PDF page coordinates.

description.description: Analyst-provided label or reason for a document request. `null` for regular uploads.

is_requested.description: True for analyst-created document request placeholders awaiting an upload.

is_console_upload.description: True for documents uploaded from the console rather than the end-user flow. Console uploads never change the feature-level aggregate status.

is_confirmed.description: Console uploads start `false` and flip `true` once the admin confirms them; end-user uploads are always `true`.

groups.description: Per-group progress counters keyed by group name (e.g. legal_presence, ownership_structure).

missing.description: Requested placeholders with no file uploaded yet.

environment.description: Whether the session was created by a live application (`live`) or a sandbox application (`sandbox`). Sandbox sessions are free, fully simulated, and never bill credits.

resubmissions.description: Returned only with `include=resubmissions`, for user and business sessions. One entry per resubmission request, oldest first. Each entry carries the results the resubmitted steps returned before the request, so earlier submissions stay readable. Deleting the session deletes every submission.

number.description: 1 for the first resubmission of the session, 2 for the second, and so on.

created_at.description: When the resubmission was requested.

previous_status.description: The session status just before the request.

nodes.description: The workflow steps sent back to the user.

reasons.description: The reason given for each step, keyed by `node_id`.

results.description: What the resubmitted steps returned before the request, under the same keys and in the same shape as the current results of this response (`id_verifications`, `nfc_verifications`, `liveness_checks`, `face_matches`, `poa_verifications`, `phone_verifications`, `email_verifications`, `aml_screenings`, `ip_analyses`, `database_validations`, `questionnaire_responses`, `document_ai_documents`, `geolocation_checks`; for business sessions also `document_verifications`). Only the keys of the steps that were sent back appear.

WorkflowDetail.description: The fields below are typed; the object also carries every other column of the workflow configuration (feature toggles, thresholds, warning actions, allowed documents, callbacks) as additional properties. Fields that do not apply to the `workflow_type` are `null`.

uuid.description: Per-version identifier (`settings_uuid`). Every version of a workflow has its own.

workflow_id.description: Stable identifier shared by every version of the workflow. Sessions created with it use the latest published version.

workflow_type.description: Workflow template. `null` for graph workflows created without a template.

is_default.description: Whether this is the application's default workflow.

is_archived.description: Archived workflows cannot start new sessions.

status.description: Draft versions are editable; published versions are immutable and used for new sessions.

published_at.description: When this version was published. `null` for drafts.

is_simple_workflow.description: `true` when the workflow has no custom `workflow_graph`.

workflow_url.description: Public URL that starts a session with this workflow.

workflow_graph.description: Graph structure of the workflow (nodes and edges). `null` for simple workflows.

features.description: Enabled features joined with `" + "`, for example `"OCR + LIVENESS"`.

total_price.description: Price per session; for graph workflows the most expensive path.

min_price.description: Price of the cheapest path through the workflow.

max_price.description: Price of the most expensive path through the workflow.

special_add_on_prices.description: Organization-specific add-on prices, or `null` when none are set.

max_retry_attempts.description: Retries allowed after a declined verification.

retry_window_days.description: Days during which the retries are allowed.

session_expiration_time.description: Seconds before an unfinished session expires.

questionnaire.description: The questionnaire attached to the workflow, or `null`.

kyb_role_settings.description: Per-role verification settings for KYB key people.

UserSessionListItem.title: KYC session row (session_kind: user)
UserSessionListItem.description: Summary row for a User Verification (KYC) session. Identity fields (`full_name`, `country`, `document_type`, `portrait_image`, contact fields) are populated progressively as the user completes verification steps, and are `null` until the relevant step finishes. Fields restricted by the workflow's response-attributes configuration are also returned as `null`.

session_id.description: Unique identifier of the verification session. Use it with `GET /v3/session/{sessionId}/decision/` to fetch the full decision payload.

session_kind.description: Row discriminator. Always `"user"` for KYC rows; Business Verification (KYB) rows have `"business"` and a different shape.

session_number.description: Human-friendly sequential number of the session within your application. Also matched by the `search` parameter.

session_url.description: Hosted verification URL the end user opens to complete the flow. `null` when the session has no hosted URL.

portrait_image.description: Expiring (presigned) URL of the best available portrait: the NFC chip photo when available, otherwise the ID document portrait, otherwise the liveness reference image. `null` until one of those exists. Download promptly; the link expires.

document_type.description: Human-readable type of the verified ID document. `null` before document verification completes, and also `null` after completion when the verified code has no display mapping (`SSC`, `WP`, `VISA`, `PSC`, `BC`, `OTHER`). Note: the `document_type` query parameter filters by short codes (`P`, `ID`, `DL`, `RP`, ...), not by these display values.

full_name.description: Best available full name for the session, resolved in order: ID document OCR, AML screened data, database-validation screened data, proof-of-address document, then the expected details provided at session creation. `null` when none is available yet.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country associated with the session, resolved in order: ID document issuing state, database-validation issuing state, proof-of-address issuing state, expected details, then the verified phone's country. May differ from nationality.

status.description: Overall session status. See the [Verification Statuses](/integration/verification-statuses) page for the lifecycle.

vendor_data.description: Your own identifier for the end user, echoed back exactly as sent at session creation.

didit_internal_id.description: Didit's internal identifier for the verified user profile behind this session. Stable across multiple sessions of the same user; filterable via the `didit_internal_id` query parameter.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when the session was created.

features.description: Per-feature status for every verification step configured in the session's workflow, in workflow order.

feature.description: Verification feature identifier.

status.description: Status of this feature. `Not Finished` until the step completes.

phone_number.description: Phone associated with the session: the verified phone when phone verification ran, otherwise the contact phone provided at session creation. `null` when neither exists.

is_verified.description: `true` only when the phone-verification feature approved this number.

email_address.description: Email associated with the session: the verified email when email verification ran, otherwise the contact email provided at session creation. `null` when neither exists.

is_verified.description: `true` only when the email-verification feature approved this address.

additional_details.description: Compact per-feature extras. Only features that produced data appear as keys; `null` when no feature produced extras. Fields excluded by the workflow's response-attributes configuration are omitted.

screened_data.description: Subset of the data that was screened. Only non-empty keys are included.

identification_number.description: Tax, personal, or document number that was validated (first available).

poa.description: Present when proof of address ran.

liveness.description: Present when a liveness check ran.

score.description: Liveness confidence score, rounded to 2 decimals.
Face-match similarity score, rounded to 2 decimals.

source_image.description: Expiring (presigned) URL of the source face image.

target_image.description: Expiring (presigned) URL of the target face image.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the phone number.

BusinessSessionListItem.title: KYB session row (session_kind: business)
BusinessSessionListItem.description: Summary row for a Business Verification (KYB) session. Returned only when `session_kind` is `business` or `all`.

session_id.description: Unique identifier of the business verification session.

session_kind.description: Row discriminator. Always `"business"` for KYB rows.

session_number.description: Human-friendly sequential number of the business session within your application. Numbered independently from KYC sessions.

status.description: Overall session status. See the [Verification Statuses](/integration/verification-statuses) page.

vendor_data.description: Your own identifier for the business, echoed back exactly as sent at session creation.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when the session was created.

workflow_id.description: Identifier of the workflow this session was created with.

company_name.description: Name of the company being verified, from the registry company linked to the session. `null` until a company is selected.

registration_number.description: Company registration number from the registry company linked to the session.

country.description: Country code of the registry company linked to the session.

url.description: Hosted verification URL to open for the end user.

session_id.description: Verification session id.

session_token.description: Session token, used by the mobile SDKs to launch the flow natively.

status.description: Verification session status.

url.description: Hosted wallet-ownership widget URL. Open it in a real browser surface - on mobile use SFSafariViewController or a Chrome Custom Tab, never an embedded webview.

value.description: Points added to the transaction's risk score. May be negative.

TransactionRuleActionAddScore.description: Add points to the transaction's cumulative risk score; the total decides the status via the application's review/decline thresholds.

value.description: Status to set immediately, regardless of score. Alias key: status.

workflow_id.description: REQUIRED when value is AWAITING_USER: the verification workflow the subject is asked to complete. Alias key: remediation_workflow_id. Didit creates a hosted remediation session for the subject when the rule fires.

TransactionRuleActionChangeStatus.description: Directly set the transaction status. DECLINED always wins across matched rules.

tag_name.description: Tag name to attach; created on first use (stored uppercased). Provide tag_uuid or tag_name.

tag_color.description: Hex color used when tag_name creates a new tag, e.g. #007AFE.

TransactionRuleActionAddTags.description: Attach an application tag to the matched transaction.

note.description: Note text attached to the transaction (author: Rule Engine). Alias key: value.

TransactionRuleActionAddNote.description: Attach an automated analyst note to the matched transaction.

list_id.description: List to add the subject's vendor_data to.

TransactionRuleActionAddToList.description: Add the subject's vendor_data to a blocklist, allowlist or custom list.

blueprint.description: Case blueprint UUID; defaults to the application's default blueprint.

grouping.description: Whether repeat matches join one case per applicant or one per rule+applicant.

attach_matched_transaction.description: Attach the matched transaction to the case.

TransactionRuleActionOpenCase.description: Open (or add to) an investigation case. Only the first open_case action on a rule is applied.

kyb_response_id.description: Handle for this candidate — pass it to `POST /v3/kyb/select/` to retrieve the full profile. Ephemeral and scoped to this search: do not store it long-term; re-search to get a fresh one.

name.description: Registered company name.

status.description: Normalized registry status of the company (e.g. `active`, `dissolved`, `inactive`, `struck off`).

type.description: Legal form as reported by the registry.

registered_address.description: Registered address of the candidate, when the registry returns one. Use it, with the registration number, to tell same-named companies apart: in the United States a candidate can be listed under the state where the company operates rather than the state you searched.
registered_address.example: Tesco House, Shire Park, Kestrel Way, Welwyn Garden City, AL7 1GA

risk_level.description: Registry-reported risk level, when available. Usually `null` at search time.

fetch_status.description: Always `pending` for search candidates — the full company profile is only fetched (and billed) when you select the candidate.

companies.description: Deduplicated candidate list. Empty while `search_resolved=false` (webhook mode) or when nothing matched.

search_resolved.description: `true` once the candidate list is final.

kyb_response_id.description: Candidate handle from `POST /v3/kyb/search/` (`kyb_registry.companies[].kyb_response_id`). Ephemeral — use it shortly after the search that produced it.

vendor_data.description: Your identifier for this company; echoed back and stored with the business session.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON stored with the business session and echoed back.

save_api_request.description: Must be `true` (the default). KYB registry selects are always persisted so billing and retrieval can be tracked; `false` returns `400`.

WebhookEventEnvelope.description: Fields Didit adds to every signed webhook delivery, whatever the event type. Read `webhook_type` to know which payload you received.

event_id.description: Identifier of the event. Every destination receives the same value and a redelivery keeps it, so use it to deduplicate.

timestamp.description: Unix time in seconds at which this delivery was signed. Equal to the `X-Timestamp` header; a redelivery carries a new value.

created_at.description: Unix time in seconds of the change that produced the event.

application_id.description: The application the event belongs to.

environment.description: `sandbox` for sandbox sessions and sandbox applications, otherwise `live`.

SessionWebhookEventData.description: Session fields of `status.updated` and `data.updated`. Optional fields are omitted, never sent as `null`, when they do not apply. Business (KYB) sessions add `business_session_id`, `session_kind` and `vendor_business_id`.

session_id.description: The verification session.

business_session_id.description: Business (KYB) sessions only: the same value as `session_id`.

session_kind.description: Business (KYB) sessions only. User (KYC) session events carry no top-level `session_kind`; read `decision.session_kind` instead.

status.description: Session status after the change.

trigger.description: Present when the event was not produced by the verification flow itself, for example `manual_review`, `manual_step_update`, `ongoing_monitoring`, `webhook_reconciliation`, `manual_webhook_recovery`, `kyb_registry_change` or a `console_*` edit.

workflow_id.description: The session's workflow. Omitted when the session has none.

workflow_version.description: Version of the workflow the session ran. Sent together with `workflow_id`.

vendor_data.description: Your `vendor_data` for the session. Omitted when empty.

vendor_business_id.description: Business (KYB) sessions only: the business the session belongs to. Omitted when none.

metadata.description: Your session `metadata`. Omitted when empty.

resubmit_info.description: Only when `status` is `Resubmitted`: the steps the user must redo and why.

node_id.description: Node identifier as it appears in the session's workflow definition (for example `feature_ocr`, `feature_liveness`).

feature.description: Feature type of the node, for example `OCR`, `LIVENESS` or `PROOF_OF_ADDRESS`.

nodes_to_resubmit.description: Workflow steps the user must redo. The same `{node_id, feature}` entries as `nodes_to_resubmit` in [Update Status](#patch-/v3/session/-sessionId-/update-status/).

sandbox_scenario.description: The simulated outcome armed on a sandbox session, or `null`. Always `null` for live sessions.

SessionStatusUpdatedEvent.description: A verification session changed status. `decision` is sent only for `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review` and `Abandoned`; it has the shape of `GET /v3/session/{sessionId}/decision/` for destinations on webhook version 3 (the default), and the older reduced shape for version 1 or 2 destinations. Business sessions always receive the version 3 business decision.

SessionDataUpdatedEvent.description: Data of a verification session changed without a status change, for example after a manual review edit, a step override or an ongoing-monitoring rescreen. `decision` is sent only for `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review` and `Abandoned`; it has the shape of `GET /v3/session/{sessionId}/decision/` for destinations on webhook version 3 (the default), and the older reduced shape for version 1 or 2 destinations. Business sessions always receive the version 3 business decision.

UserStatusUpdatedEvent.description: A user changed status. Not sent when the user is created.

vendor_user_id.description: The user the event is about.

vendor_data.description: Your `vendor_data` for the user, or `null`.

status.description: User status after the change.

UserDataUpdatedEvent.description: Fields of a user changed. Not sent when the user is created. One save can produce both a status and a data event.

vendor_user_id.description: The user the event is about.

vendor_data.description: Your `vendor_data` for the user, or `null`.

status.description: User status after the change.

changed_fields.description: Names of the fields that changed.
