previous.description: Value before the change. Dates are ISO 8601 strings.

current.description: Value after the change. Dates are ISO 8601 strings.

changes.description: Previous and current value of each changed field, keyed by field name. Values can be personal data (names, dates of birth, portrait links, emails, phone numbers); handle them accordingly.

BusinessStatusUpdatedEvent.description: A business changed status. Not sent when the business is created.

vendor_business_id.description: The business the event is about.

vendor_data.description: Your `vendor_data` for the business, or `null`.

status.description: Business status after the change.

BusinessDataUpdatedEvent.description: Fields of a business changed. Not sent when the business is created. One save can produce both a status and a data event.

vendor_business_id.description: The business the event is about.

vendor_data.description: Your `vendor_data` for the business, or `null`.

status.description: Business status after the change.

changed_fields.description: Names of the fields that changed.

previous.description: Value before the change. Dates are ISO 8601 strings.

current.description: Value after the change. Dates are ISO 8601 strings.

changes.description: Previous and current value of each changed field, keyed by field name.

TransactionCreatedEvent.description: A transaction was created and screened. Sent for live applications only.

txn_id.description: The `transaction_id` you supplied at create time, or `null`.

status.description: Monitoring status after the change.

score.description: Risk score accumulated by rules.

severity.description: Risk severity, or `null` until a rule or provider sets one.

amount.description: Transaction amount as a decimal string. Unlike the API it is not normalized, so it can carry trailing zeros (up to 18 decimal places).

currency.description: Currency code or crypto asset symbol of `amount`.

action_required.description: Pending end-user action, or `null`. Same object as `action_required` on the transaction; `session_token` is a credential, so never log it.

TransactionStatusUpdatedEvent.description: A transaction changed status, from a rule, a review or an end-user action. Sent for live applications only.

txn_id.description: The `transaction_id` you supplied at create time, or `null`.

status.description: Monitoring status after the change.

score.description: Risk score accumulated by rules.

severity.description: Risk severity, or `null` until a rule or provider sets one.

amount.description: Transaction amount as a decimal string. Unlike the API it is not normalized, so it can carry trailing zeros (up to 18 decimal places).

currency.description: Currency code or crypto asset symbol of `amount`.

action_required.description: Pending end-user action, or `null`. Same object as `action_required` on the transaction; `session_token` is a credential, so never log it.

TravelRuleStatusUpdatedEvent.description: A Travel Rule exchange changed status. Sent on every transition up to and including `FINISHED`, `CANCELLED` or `EXPIRED`, never after. Sent for live applications only. There is no top-level `status`.

transaction_id.description: The transaction the exchange belongs to.

txn_id.description: The `transaction_id` you supplied at create time, or `null`.

rail.description: Network the exchange runs on, or an empty string when none could be resolved.

WorkflowComplianceChangedEvent.description: The compliance status of a published workflow changed after a re-evaluation. One event per workflow. There is no top-level `status`.

severity.description: `actionable` when gaps were detected, `indicative` for a pending change, `informative` when gaps were resolved.

kb_version.description: Version of the regulatory knowledge base used.

WebhookEventPayload.description: Body of a signed webhook delivery, discriminated by `webhook_type`. `activity.created` can be subscribed to but is not sent today. Treat any other `webhook_type` as a new event type and keep the raw body.

KYBRegistrySearchResolvedCallback.description: Body of the callback sent to the `webhook_url` of `POST /v3/kyb/search/` once the registry search resolves. It is not signed: the request carries `X-Didit-Unsigned-Callback: true` and none of the signature headers, so confirm it by matching `request_id` against a search you started. Uses `event_type`, not `webhook_type`.

request_id.description: The `request_id` returned by `POST /v3/kyb/search/`.

vendor_data.description: Echo of the `vendor_data` you sent.

metadata.description: Echo of the `metadata` you sent.

timestamp.description: Unix time in seconds at which the callback was queued.

created_at.description: Unix time in seconds at which the callback was queued.

node_id.description: Unique identifier for this AML step in the workflow graph.

status.description: Feature-level status of this AML screening. Independent of the top-level session `status` — a session can reach its overall decision while an individual feature stays `In Review`.

entity_type.description: Type of entity screened: person or company

match.description: Whether this is a confirmed match

score.description: Deprecated weighted match score in the 0-1 range (e.g. `0.73`). Use `match_score` (0-100) instead.

target.description: Whether the matched entity is the direct target of the listing (as opposed to a related party). `null` when the source does not specify it.

caption.description: Caption or title of the match

datasets.description: List of dataset categories where the match was found. Indicates whether the entity appeared in PEP lists (with level), sanctions databases, adverse media, warnings/regulatory enforcement, or other compliance datasets.

last_seen.description: Date when match was last seen

first_seen.description: Date when match was first seen

match_score.description: Weighted identity confidence score (0-100) calculated from name similarity, date of birth, and country matching. Used to determine if hit is a False Positive or Possible Match.

risk_score.description: Entity risk score (0-100). Used to determine final AML status (Approved/In Review/Declined) based on the highest risk_score among non-False-Positive hits.

review_status.description: Review status for this hit. Can be 'Unreviewed', 'Confirmed Match', 'False Positive', or 'Inconclusive'.

score_breakdown.description: Detailed breakdown of how the match_score was calculated.

name_weight.description: Original weight for name from config (0-100).

name_weight_normalized.description: Normalized weight for name after re-weighting for missing data (0-100).

name_contribution.description: Points contributed by name to the total score.

dob_weight.description: Original weight for DOB from config (0-100).

dob_weight_normalized.description: Normalized weight for DOB after re-weighting for missing data (0-100).

dob_contribution.description: Points contributed by DOB to the total score.

country_weight.description: Original weight for country from config (0-100).

country_weight_normalized.description: Normalized weight for country after re-weighting for missing data (0-100).

country_contribution.description: Points contributed by country to the total score.

document_number_match_type.description: Result of document number 'Golden Key' evaluation.

document_number_effect.description: Human-readable description of the document number effect on the score.

warning_matches.description: List of warning and regulatory enforcement matches. Includes entries from categories: Warning, SIP, Warnings and Regulatory Enforcement, Fitness and Probity, SIE, and Insolvency.

list_name.description: Name of the warning list publisher

matched_name.description: Name matched in the warning list

publisher.description: Publisher or source of the warning

source_url.description: URL to the source of the warning

created_at.description: Date the warning entry was created

updated_at.description: Date the warning entry was last updated

additional_data.description: Additional data from the warning source. May contain a `data` object with `case_details` array.

case_details.description: Details of warning cases associated with this match

sanction_matches.description: List of sanction list matches found for this entity.

matched_name.description: Name matched in the sanction list

reason.description: Free-text reason why the entity was sanctioned. Joined from the sanction list's reason entries. Examples: 'Executive Order 13224 (Terrorism)', 'Support for actions undermining Ukraine's sovereignty', 'Listed due to national security concerns.'

source_url.description: URL to the source of the sanction

listed_on.description: Date(s) when the entity was listed

sanction_program.description: Sanction program(s) the entity is listed under

updated_on.description: Date(s) when the sanction entry was last updated

additional_data.description: Additional data from the sanction source not captured in the main fields

score.description: Overall AML screening score — the highest risk score across all hits (float, 0-100). `null` until computed.

is_ongoing_monitoring_enabled.description: Whether AML ongoing monitoring is enabled for this screening. When `true`, the entity is re-screened periodically and any new hits update the report.

next_ongoing_monitoring_bill_date.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) when this ongoing-monitoring subscription will next be billed. Computed as the date of the last ongoing-monitoring billing plus 365 days when `is_ongoing_monitoring_enabled = true`; otherwise `null`. This is a billing date, not a screening date - use `last_ongoing_screening_at` for that.

last_ongoing_screening_at.description: When ongoing monitoring last completed a re-screening of this record, whether or not the result changed. `null` when the record has never been re-screened; it is never back-filled from the enablement or billing date.

last_ongoing_screening_datasets_updated_.description: The most recent AML dataset update date the provider reported at the time of that screening. `null` when the provider reported no dataset dates; never estimated.

feature.description: The feature that generated this warning. The value identifies the feature block the warning belongs to. Within an AML screening this is typically `AML`, but the enum above is authoritative across all feature warnings on the decision payload.

node_id.description: The workflow graph node ID that generated this warning

MonitoringEvent.description: One stored monitoring event as returned by the list and subject-timeline endpoints. Restricted evidence (payload, device context, rule evidence) is only returned by `GET /v3/events/{event_uuid}/`.

event_uuid.description: Didit identifier of the event. Use it as `{event_uuid}` in the retrieve and delete calls.

event_id.description: Your own identifier, the idempotency key you sent.

action_type.description: What happened within the category, as you sent it.

occurred_at.description: When the event happened on your side.

status.description: `ACCEPTED`: stored, no matched rule changed its standing (the normal answer for most events, and always the answer in a sandbox application, where no rules run). `APPROVED`: a rule matched and the score stayed under your review threshold. `IN_REVIEW`: a rule pushed the score over the review threshold or set the status. `DECLINED`: a rule declined it or the score crossed your decline threshold.

score.description: Accumulated rule score. Starts at 0; rule `add_score` actions move it (negative deltas are allowed).

subject_vendor_data.description: `subject.vendor_data` of the event: your id for the user or company.

subject_entity_type.description: `individual` or `company`: which kind of subject `subject_vendor_data` names.

subject_uuid.description: UUID of the user (individual) or company the event resolved to, or null when that record no longer exists.

counterparty_vendor_data.description: The other player of a P2P event (promoted from `payload.counterparty_vendor_data`).

session_id.description: `session.session_id` sent with the event.

ip_address.description: IP address of the event. On the server lane this is `device_context.network_context.ip_address` as you sent it; on the device lane it is the IP of the request.

ip_country.description: Country code of `ip_address` from IP enrichment, or null when the address was not enriched (missing, private, or low-value telemetry whose address was not already known).

amount.description: Amount as a decimal string with 18 decimal places, from `transaction_context.amount`, `payload.amount` or `payload.stake_amount`, in that order.

retention_class.description: Retention class. Payment and dispute events are `monetary_or_compliance`; security and responsible-gambling events are `risk_relevant`; `session.page_view`, `session.sdk_heartbeat`, `session.sdk_loaded`, `session.device_seen`, `session.bot_signal_observed`, `bonus.promotion_viewed` and `affiliate.referral_clicked` are `low_value`; everything else is `standard`. An event an active rule matched is promoted to `risk_relevant` (never demoted).

rules_matched_count.description: Number of rules that matched the event, including rules in `TEST` mode (which record evidence but apply no actions).

correlation_pending.description: `true` while an asynchronous rule (cross-subject correlation, or a sequence longer than 24 hours) still has to run for this event. It resolves within minutes and `status`, `score` and `rules_matched_count` update in place.

is_droppable.description: Whether an SDK under backpressure may drop events of this kind. `false` for every `security`, `payment`, `dispute` and `responsible_gambling` event and for `gameplay.bet_placed`, `gameplay.bet_settled` and `gameplay.p2p_settlement`.

MonitoringEventDetail.description: One monitoring event with its full envelope, enrichment and rule evidence. Every field of `MonitoringEvent` plus the fields below.

payload.description: The category fields you sent in `payload`.

custom_values.description: The scalar `custom_values` you sent. Didit adds `vpn_or_proxy_detected: true` or `is_data_center: true` when IP enrichment flags the address and you did not set them.

device_context.description: The device context as stored: your `device_context` (including `fingerprint`, `persistent_device_id` and `bot_score` when sent) with `network_context` completed by IP enrichment (`ip_country`, `ip_country_code`, `ip_city`, `asn_number`, `asn_organization`, `is_vpn_or_tor`, `is_data_center`, `proxy_type`, `connection_type`) for keys you left empty.

field_sources.description: Field path to provenance: `customer` (sent by your backend), `sdk` (sent through the device lane) or `server` (derived by Didit, such as `received_at` and enriched network fields). Check it before acting on a match.

net_result_amount.description: Promoted from `payload.net_result_amount`, as a decimal string with 18 decimal places.

schema_version.description: Version of the event envelope schema. Currently `1`.

expires_at.description: When the event expires under its retention class and is deleted: `occurred_at` plus the class period (14, 30 or 90 days by default, adjustable per application). Null for `monetary_or_compliance` events, which follow transaction retention.

rules_evaluated_count.description: Number of event rules evaluated for this event.

rule_runs.description: Every rule that matched the event, newest first.

ip_enrichment.description: Enrichment of the event's IP address, or null when the address was not enriched. See [IP enrichment](https://docs.didit.me/transaction-monitoring/ip-enrichment).

asn_organization.description: Organization that operates the autonomous system.

is_vpn_or_tor.description: Whether the address is a known VPN or Tor exit.

is_data_center.description: Whether the address belongs to a hosting or data-centre network.

proxy_type.description: Proxy classification of the address as an opaque string, or null.

last_enriched_at.description: When the address was last enriched.

subject_profile.description: Cached email and phone risk signals of the subject, or null when no profile exists for the subject.

email_is_disposable.description: Whether the email address is disposable.

email_is_breached.description: Whether the email address appears in known data breaches.

email_social_count.description: Number of online accounts linked to the email address.

email_social_providers.description: Names of the online services where an account linked to the email address was found.

phone_social_count.description: Number of online accounts linked to the phone number.

phone_social_providers.description: Names of the online services where an account linked to the phone number was found.

source_provider.description: Opaque identifier of the source of the profile.

last_enriched_at.description: When the profile was last refreshed.

tags.description: Names of the tags attached to the event (rule `add_tags` actions).

rule_uuid.description: UUID of the transaction monitoring rule.

library_key.description: Library key when the rule was installed from the rules library, otherwise null.

matched.description: Always `true`: only matching runs are recorded.

mode.description: Mode of the rule when it ran. A `TEST` run records evidence but applied no actions.

is_async.description: `true` when the run came from the asynchronous correlation pass rather than the ingest request.

severity.description: Severity of the rule. Null for `TEST` runs and for rules without a severity.

score_delta.description: How much this run changed the event's score (0 for `TEST` runs).

action_summary.description: Short summary of the actions applied, for example `score +40; add_tag:VPN_LOGIN`. Null when nothing was applied.

matched_payload.description: The conditions and aggregations that matched. Condition entries carry `field`, `operator`, `expected_value`, `current_value`, `matched`, `group_index`, `group_logic` and `field_source` (`server`, `sdk` or `customer`); aggregation entries carry `metric`, `field`, `operator`, `expected_value`, `computed_value`, `window`, `filters`, `matched` and `sample_references`.

created_at.description: When the rule run was recorded.

MonitoringEventPage.description: One page of monitoring events, newest `occurred_at` first.

count.description: Number of matching events, exact up to 100 and capped at 100 above that. Do not compute page counts from it; follow `next` until it is null.

next.description: URL of the next page, or null on the last page.

previous.description: URL of the previous page, or null on the first page.

MonitoringEventCreateRequest.description: The event envelope, the same for every category. camelCase aliases are accepted: `eventId`, `eventCategory` (or `category`), `actionType`, `occurredAt`, `timeZone` (or `zoneId`), `deviceContext` (or `device`), `transactionContext`, `customValues` (or `props`); inside `subject`: `vendorData`, `entityType`, `fullName`; inside `session`: `sessionId`, `pageUrl`; inside `transaction_context`: `paymentReferenceId`.

event_id.description: Your identifier for the event, unique per application. It is the idempotency key: resending the same `event_category`, `action_type`, `occurred_at`, `subject.vendor_data` and `payload` under it is a replay, anything different is a conflict.

action_type.description: What happened within the category. Open vocabulary; the managed actions listed in [Event ingestion](https://docs.didit.me/transaction-monitoring/events) (for example `login`, `deposit_completed`, `chargeback_opened`) unlock typed validation and managed rule fields. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed.

occurred_at.description: When the event happened on your side, ISO 8601 (a value without an offset is read as UTC). Must be no more than 7 days in the past and no more than 5 minutes in the future.

time_zone.description: Time zone of the occurrence on your side, for example `Europe/Madrid`. Stored with the event; not returned by the read endpoints.

subject.description: The user or company the event belongs to. It resolves to the user (or company) with this `vendor_data` in your application; one is created when none exists.

vendor_data.description: Your id for the subject.

entity_type.description: `company` resolves the subject to a company; any other value (default `individual`) resolves it to an individual. The same `vendor_data` can name one of each.

full_name.description: Display name, used only when this event creates the user or company.

email.description: Validated as an email address; not stored on the event.

phone.description: Validated; not stored on the event.

country.description: Validated; not stored on the event.

business.description: The business the event belongs to, when it differs from the subject. Only `vendor_data` is read.

vendor_data.description: Your id for the business. Filterable as `business_vendor_data`.

session.description: Your session context for the event.

session_id.description: Your session identifier. Filterable and returned as `session_id`.

sequence.description: Position of the event within the session. Returned as `session_sequence`.

page_url.description: Validated; not stored on the event.

referrer.description: Validated; not stored on the event.

device_context.description: Device and network context, stored as sent and returned by `GET /v3/events/{event_uuid}/`. On this server lane Didit does not see the end user's connection, so the IP enriched and used by rules is `network_context.ip_address` as you send it.

bot_score.description: Bot score from your own detection, as an integer.

ip_address.description: End user's IP address. Public addresses are enriched once per unique address.

transaction_context.description: Money context. Non-empty values here also satisfy the required payload keys of the action.

amount.description: Amount as a decimal string (a number is also accepted).

direction.description: Direction of the money movement, for example `inbound` or `outbound`.

payload.description: The category's domain fields, at most 16384 bytes once JSON-encoded. Some actions require keys (in `payload` or `transaction_context`): `gameplay.p2p_settlement` needs `game_id`, `counterparty_vendor_data`, `stake_amount`, `net_result_amount`, `role` and one of `hand_id`, `round_id`, `match_id`; `gameplay.bet_placed` and `gameplay.bet_settled` need `game_id`; `payment.deposit_initiated`, `payment.deposit_completed`, `payment.withdrawal_requested` and `payment.withdrawal_completed` need `payment_reference_id`, `amount`, `currency`, `payment_method`, `status`; `payment.withdrawal_address_changed` needs `withdrawal_address_hash`; `dispute.chargeback_opened`, `dispute.chargeback_won` and `dispute.chargeback_lost` need `payment_reference_id` and one of `dispute_id`, `chargeback_id`; `session.bot_signal_observed` needs `telemetry_schema_version` and one of `bot_score`, `actions_per_minute`, `timing_variance_ms`, `pointer_entropy`, `keystroke_entropy`, `reaction_time_ms_p50`; `responsible_gambling.self_exclusion_match` needs `registry_source`, `exclusion_status`, `identity_match_ref`. Every `security` action ending in `_changed` needs `changed_field`, plus `previous_reference_hash` or `new_reference_hash` when the field is `password`, `mfa_method`, `mfa`, `email`, `phone`, `withdrawal_address`, `payout_method` or `api_key`. Send hashes and references, never a card number, a full withdrawal address, a password hash or an MFA secret.

custom_values.description: Up to 100 keys of your own, addressable from rules as `custom_values.<key>`. Values must be scalars (string, number, boolean or null); nested objects and arrays are rejected.

MonitoringEventIngestResult.description: Outcome of ingesting one event. The same shape is returned for a new event and for an idempotent replay.

event_uuid.description: Didit identifier of the stored event.

status.description: Status after the real-time rules ran. See `MonitoringEvent.status`.

score.description: Score after the real-time rules ran.

rules_evaluated_count.description: Number of event rules evaluated in the request. 0 in a sandbox application, where no rules run.

rules_matched_count.description: Number of rules that matched, including `TEST` mode rules.

correlation_pending.description: `true` when an asynchronous rule still has to run. Read `GET /v3/events/{event_uuid}/` a few minutes later for the final `status` and `score`.

retention_class.description: Retention class, after any promotion by a matched rule.

expires_at.description: When the event expires under its retention class and is deleted. Null for `monetary_or_compliance` (payment and dispute) events.

idempotent_replay.description: `true` when an event with this `event_id` and the same content was already stored; the values are those of the stored event and no rule ran again.

library_key.description: Library key when the rule was installed from the rules library, otherwise null.

mode.description: `TEST` rules record the match but apply no actions.

is_async.description: `true` when the match came from the asynchronous pass.

ComplianceList.description: A blocklist, allowlist or custom list of one application.

uuid.description: List identifier. Use it as `list_uuid` in the list and entry endpoints, and as the value of a workflow or transaction rule condition with `value_type: "list"`.

name.description: List name, unique among the application's lists.

description.description: Free-text description. Empty string when not set.

list_type.description: `blocklist`: a match declines the session or transaction (system lists only, one per entry type). `allowlist`: matching items are trusted, for example a face allowlist skips the duplicated-face action; never overrides a blocklist match. `custom`: used in workflow and transaction rule conditions (`value_type: "list"`).

entry_type.description: What the list holds: `face`, `document` (document number), `phone`, `email`, `ip_address` (IP address or CIDR range), `device_fingerprint`, `wallet_address`, `bank_account`, `country` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3), `user` or `business` (your `vendor_data`), or `key` (any string). It decides how entry values are validated and matched.

is_system.description: `true` for the lists Didit provisions: one blocklist per entry type (`face`, `document`, `phone`, `email`, `ip_address`, `device_fingerprint`, `wallet_address`, `bank_account`, `user`, `business`), the **High Risk Countries** custom list, and system allowlists. System lists cannot be renamed, edited or deleted; you can add and delete their entries.

entry_count.description: Number of entries currently in the list.

last_entry_added_at.description: When the newest current entry was added. `null` for an empty list.

created_at.description: When the list was created.

updated_at.description: When the list was last updated.

uuid.description: Entry identifier. Use it as `entry_uuid` in Delete a list entry.

value.description: The listed value: a phone number in E.164, an email address, a document number, an IP address or CIDR range, a device fingerprint, a wallet address, a bank account, an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code, a `vendor_data`, any string on a `key` list, or the UUID of the stored face on a face list. Values you send are stored in lower case, except phone numbers and country codes. Matching is case-insensitive.

display_label.description: Human-readable label. Didit fills it for entries taken from a session (for example the holder's name and document number) when you send none.

comment.description: Free-text note. Empty string when not set.

added_by.description: Who added the entry: `api` (an API key), a console user's email address or `console`, `system` or `migration` (entries Didit created), or `rule` (a transaction or monitoring rule action).

reference_session_id.description: Verification session the entry was taken from. `null` when the entry was added by value.

reference_session_number.description: Application-scoped number of that session, as shown in the console.

reference_session_type.description: `kyc` for a person verification session, `kyb` for a business verification session, `null` when there is no session.

reference_object_uuid.description: The record the entry stands for: the face, document, phone or email record read from a session, the face created by Upload a face to a list, or the UUID you sent (for example a transaction UUID or a user's `didit_internal_id`).

metadata.description: Extra context. Holds the keys Didit sets (listed here) merged with any `metadata` you sent when creating the entry, returned as stored. `null` when there is none.

reference_image_url.description: Face entries: short-lived signed URL, issued again on every call; `null` for a scoped API key without `media: read`. Absent when no image belongs to the entry.

front_image_url.description: Document entries that carry a document front image: short-lived signed URL, issued again on every call; `null` for a scoped API key without `media: read`.

full_name.description: Document entries taken from a session: holder's full name.

issuing_state.description: Document entries taken from a session: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 issuing country.

document_type.description: Document entries taken from a session: document type code, for example `P`, `ID` or `DL`.

region.description: Document entries taken from a session: issuing state or province of a regionally issued document, empty when not applicable. Not set by Add session items to the blocklist.

document_number.description: Document entries taken from a session: the document number.

face_image_source.description: Face entries taken from a document-capture selfie: which selfie. Absent for liveness faces.

reference_node_id.description: Face entries taken from a document-capture selfie: the ID verification node the selfie came from.

fingerprint_tier.description: Device fingerprint entries taken from a session: how the fingerprint was derived. `persistent_id` identifies one device; `composite_hash` and `legacy_fp` can be shared by devices of the same model.

sandbox.description: `true` on a face entry uploaded in a sandbox application; such an entry matches nothing.

reference_type.description: Set by you: what `reference_object_uuid` points to, so the console links back to it.

reference_id.description: Set by you: identifier of the source record.

created_at.description: When the entry was added.

BlocklistedItem.description: One blocklisted face, identity document, phone number or email address of a verification session. Fields that do not apply to the item's `type` are `null`.

type.description: What was blocklisted.

session_id.description: Verification session the item belongs to.

session_number.description: Application-scoped number of that session, as shown in the console.

blocklisted_at.description: When the item was last blocklisted.

face_image.description: Face items: short-lived signed URL, issued again on every call; `null` for a scoped API key without `media: read`. Also `null` when no reference image is stored.

document_type.description: Document items: document type code, for example `P` (passport), `ID` (national ID), `DL` (driver's license) or `RP` (residence permit).

document_number.description: Document items: the document number, or the personal number when the document has none.

front_image.description: Document items: front image of the document, short-lived signed URL, issued again on every call; `null` for a scoped API key without `media: read`.

phone_number.description: Phone items: the phone number in E.164.

country_code.description: Phone items: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the number.

email.description: Email items: the email address.

TransactionNote.description: One note on a monitored transaction's review timeline.

uuid.description: Note identifier.

actor_email.description: Email of the Console user who wrote the note or changed the status. `null` for notes created with an API key and for notes Didit adds automatically.

actor_name.description: Display name of the Console user (their email when they have no name). `Rule Engine` on notes Didit adds automatically. `null` for notes created with an API key.

metadata.description: Tells the note types apart. Notes written through the API or the Console carry `mentioned_emails`. A status change made in the Console carries `type: status_change` with `previous_status`, `new_status`, `reason_code` and `reason_label`. Notes Didit adds carry `source`: `rule_action` (with `rule_uuid`) for a rule's `add_note` action, or `remediation_session` for a problem creating the user-action verification session.

mentioned_emails.description: Mentioned organization members, lower-cased and de-duplicated. Empty when nobody was mentioned.

type.description: Present on notes recording a status change made in the Console.

reason_code.description: Reason code given with the change.

reason_label.description: Reason label given with the change.

source.description: Present on notes Didit adds automatically.

rule_uuid.description: Rule whose `add_note` action wrote the note (with `source: rule_action`).

created_at.description: When the note was stored.

TransactionSummary.description: Summary of a monitored transaction, the shape `GET /v3/transactions/` lists. Call `GET /v3/transactions/{transaction_id}/` with `uuid` for parties, alerts and rule runs.

uuid.description: Didit transaction UUID. Use it as `{transaction_id}` on the transaction endpoints.

transaction_number.description: Application-scoped sequential number shown in the Console.

txn_id.description: Your own identifier from the create call. Unique per application.

action_type.description: Sub-type within the category, for example `withdrawal`.

status.description: Current monitoring verdict.

source.description: `LIVE` for transactions submitted for monitoring, `IMPORTED` for historical imports.

amount.description: Amount as a decimal string with trailing zeros removed (up to 18 decimal places).

currency.description: Currency code or crypto asset symbol of `amount`.

preferred_currency_amount.description: `amount` converted to the application's preferred currency, when a rate was available.

created_at.description: When Didit recorded it.

score.description: Risk score. Higher is riskier.

severity.description: Risk severity, `null` until something sets it.

source.description: Didit preset or custom tag.

subject_type.description: Whether the applicant is linked to a Didit user or business; `null` when it is linked to neither.

subject_uuid.description: UUID of the Didit user or business the applicant is linked to.

counterparty_name.description: Full name of the `COUNTERPARTY` party, if any.

assigned_to_name.description: Name of the Console reviewer assigned to the transaction.

travel_rule_status.description: Status of the transaction's Travel Rule transfer, or `null` when it has none.

ApplicationAnalyticsDataPoint.description: Session counts for one day, by creation date (UTC). Each count reflects the session's current status. Points of the previous period carry at least the required fields.

manually_approved.description: Sessions a reviewer approved after the workflow gave another verdict.

manually_declined.description: Sessions a reviewer declined after the workflow gave another verdict.

ApplicationAnalyticsRequestBreakdown.description: Status totals for the range. The previous-period breakdown carries at least the required fields.

country.description: Country name.

ip_countries.description: Countries of the users' IP addresses, most sessions first.

id_countries.description: Issuing countries of the verified ID documents, most sessions first.

conversion_by_country.description: Per document issuing country: finished sessions (approved, declined or in review) and how many were approved. Most finished first.

cities.description: Up to 100 IP cities, most sessions first.

age_distribution.description: Sessions per age band from the ID document. Empty when there is no data.

gender_distribution.description: Sessions per document gender code: `M`, `F` or `U` (unknown).

ApplicationAnalyticsDeviceDetails.description: Top five of each, most sessions first.

device_models.description: Device brands: `Apple`, `Android`, `LG`, everything else grouped as `Other`.

browsers.description: Browsers: `Chrome`, `Safari`, `Didit App`, `Firefox`, everything else grouped as `Other`.

ApplicationAnalyticsWorkflowFunnel.description: Keyed by workflow ID. `total` is the sessions started on that workflow; `steps` counts the sessions that reached each step (`OCR`, `LIVENESS`, `FACE_MATCH`, `AML`, `POA`, `PHONE`, `EMAIL`, `NFC`, `DATABASE_VALIDATION`, `QUESTIONNAIRE`, `IP_ANALYSIS`, `AGE_ESTIMATION`, `KYB_REGISTRY`, `KYB_DOCUMENTS`, `KYB_KEY_PEOPLE`). Reaching a step is not passing it.

ApplicationAnalyticsVerificationTimeStat.description: Active time users spent verifying, ignoring idle gaps. An empty object when there is no data.

per_feature.description: Keyed by feature, for example `OCR` or `LIVENESS`.

per_sub_step.description: Keyed by feature, then by sub-step, for example `front_id_photo`.

third_plus.description: Finished sessions resubmitted two or more times.

ApplicationAnalyticsOriginalStatusStats.description: The workflow's automatic verdict, before any reviewer changed it.

ApplicationAnalyticsWarningStats.description: Keyed by feature (`ID_VERIFICATION`, `LIVENESS`, `FACEMATCH`, `AML`, `PROOF_OF_ADDRESS`, `PHONE`, `EMAIL`, `NFC`, `LOCATION`, `DATABASE_VALIDATION`, `QUESTIONNAIRE` and the KYB features). `total` is the sessions that reached the feature; `risks` counts sessions per warning code and level.

date.description: Period key: `YYYY-MM-DD` for a day, the Monday of a week, or `YYYY-MM` for a month, following `grouping_mode`.
Period key: `YYYY-MM-DD` for a day, the Monday of a week, or `YYYY-MM` for a month, following `grouping_mode`.
Period key: `YYYY-MM-DD` for a day, the Monday of a week, or `YYYY-MM` for a month, following `grouping_mode`.
Period key: `YYYY-MM-DD` for a day, the Monday of a week, or `YYYY-MM` for a month, following `grouping_mode`.
Period key: `YYYY-MM-DD` for a day, the Monday of a week, or `YYYY-MM` for a month, following `grouping_mode`.

ApplicationAnalyticsSummary.description: User verification (KYC) summary, returned when neither `scope` nor `widget_keys` is sent.

data_points.description: One point per day, from the first day with sessions in the range to `end_date`. Always daily, whatever `grouping_mode` says.

previous_data_points.description: Daily points for the period of the same length right before `start_date`.

conversion_rate.description: `total_approved / (total_approved + total_declined + total_in_review) x 100`, one decimal. `null` when nothing finished.

grouping_mode.description: How the `*_time_series` lists are grouped: `day` for up to 14 days, `week` up to 90, `month` beyond. Measured from the first day with sessions in the range.

ApplicationAnalyticsWidget.description: One dashboard widget. Every widget has `kind` and `title`; the other fields depend on `kind`. The session widgets reuse the summary objects (`data_points`, `request_breakdown`, `workflow_funnel_stats` and so on); list widgets put their entries in `items`; transaction metrics use `value`.

grouping_mode.description: How the `*_time_series` lists are grouped: `day` for up to 14 days, `week` up to 90, `month` beyond. Measured from the first day with sessions in the range.

items.description: Entries of a list widget. `country_distribution` (KYC): `country`, `country_code`, `session_count`. `conversion_by_country`: `country`, `country_code`, `finished`, `approved`. `time_series`: `date`, `value`. `status_time_series`: `date`, `approved`, `declined`, `flagged`. `breakdown`: `transaction_type` or `action_type` with `count` and `volume`, or `tag_id`, `tag_name`, `count`. `leaderboard`: `rule_title`, `trigger_count` or `assignee`, `handled_count`, `average_processing_seconds`, each with `approved_percentage`, `declined_percentage`, `flagged_percentage`. `histogram`: `score`, `count`.

previous_items.description: Transaction time series for the period of the same length right before `start_date`.

value.description: `metric` widgets: the figure for the range.

currency.description: Transaction volume and amount widgets: the application's default transaction currency.

thresholds.description: `histogram` widget: the application's review and decline score thresholds.

ApplicationAnalyticsWidgetResponse.description: Dashboard widgets, returned when `scope` or `widget_keys` is sent.

available_widget_keys.description: Every widget key this scope accepts.

requested_widget_keys.description: The widget keys answered, in order: your valid `widget_keys`, or the scope's defaults.

widgets.description: Keyed by widget key, in the order of `requested_widget_keys`.

WebhookConfigDestination.description: A webhook destination as listed in the webhook configuration, without delivery metrics. `GET /v3/webhook/destinations/{destination_uuid}/` adds its delivery summary.

uuid.description: Destination ID.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint Didit posts events to.

webhook_version.description: Payload version sent to this destination.

secret_shared_key.description: This destination's signing secret (43-character URL-safe token). Verify each webhook with the secret of the destination it was sent to. API-key callers always receive it in full; Console users without `read:webhooks` receive an empty string.

subscribed_events.description: Event types delivered to this destination. Empty when the destination was created without events, in which case it receives nothing.

WebhookConfig.description: Application-level webhook configuration, retention policy and Digital ID wallet return hosts, with every webhook destination.

webhook_url.description: Application-level (legacy) webhook URL. Didit sends to it only while the application has no enabled destination, and then only `status.updated` and `data.updated`. Every create, update or delete of a destination sets it to the URL of the oldest enabled destination, or `null` when none is enabled.

webhook_version.description: Payload version of the legacy `webhook_url`. Each destination has its own `webhook_version`.

secret_shared_key.description: Application-level signing secret (43-character URL-safe token). It signs only deliveries to the legacy `webhook_url`; each destination signs with its own `secret_shared_key`. API-key callers always receive it in full; Console users without `read:webhooks` receive an empty string.

capture_method.description: Legacy application setting. The verification flow does not read it: capture options are configured per workflow.

data_retention_months.description: Automatic deletion window. User verification sessions created more than this many months ago (a month counts as 30 days) are deleted automatically, and that deletion is irreversible. `null` means sessions are never deleted automatically. See [Data retention](https://docs.didit.me/console/data-retention).

face_retention_policy.description: What happens to a session's face embedding when the session is deleted. `delete_with_session` (default) deletes it with the session. `retain_until_user_deleted` is the opt-in [biometric template retention](https://docs.didit.me/console/data-retention#biometric-template-retention): an image-free biometric template linked to the User is managed separately until its retention period ends, the User is deleted, or you purge it.

face_retention_days.description: Retention period, in days, of biometric templates under `retain_until_user_deleted`. Required when that policy is set.

available_events.description: Every event type a destination can subscribe to, with a display label.

label.description: Display label, for example `Session status updated`.

allowed_return_hosts.description: Hostnames (exact match, HTTPS only) a standalone Digital ID wallet verification may send the user back to with its `return_url`. Your white-label domain is always allowed as well. See [Register your return destination](https://docs.didit.me/standalone-apis/digital-id-wallets#register-your-return-destination).

endpoints.description: Every webhook destination of the application, oldest first, each with its signing secret. Read only here: manage destinations with the `/v3/webhook/destinations/` endpoints.

WebhookDestinationDelivery.description: One delivery attempt to a webhook destination. The first send of an event, each automatic retry and each resend are separate deliveries.

uuid.description: Delivery ID, for the detail and resend calls.

session_id.description: User verification session the event is about. `null` for business session, user, business, transaction, Travel Rule and workflow events.

request_url.description: URL the delivery was sent to: the destination's URL when the event was generated.

response_status.description: HTTP status your endpoint returned. `null` while the delivery is queued and not yet attempted. When no HTTP answer was received Didit records a status of its own: `504` when your endpoint did not answer within 5 seconds, `503` for a connection failure, `400` when the URL was refused as unsafe (for example a private or internal address), and `404` for any other request error. `400` or above counts as a failed delivery.

response_time_ms.description: Time the attempt took, in milliseconds. `null` while the delivery is queued.

status.description: Status the event reported when it was generated: the session status for session events (for example `Approved` or `In Review`), the person's or company's status for user and business events, and the transaction status for transaction events. `null` for events that carry no status.

created_at.description: When the delivery was created.

WebhookDestinationDeliveryDetail.description: One delivery attempt to a webhook destination, with the exact request headers and body Didit sent.

uuid.description: Delivery ID, for the detail and resend calls.

session_id.description: User verification session the event is about. `null` for business session, user, business, transaction, Travel Rule and workflow events.

request_url.description: URL the delivery was sent to: the destination's URL when the event was generated.

response_status.description: HTTP status your endpoint returned. `null` while the delivery is queued and not yet attempted. When no HTTP answer was received Didit records a status of its own: `504` when your endpoint did not answer within 5 seconds, `503` for a connection failure, `400` when the URL was refused as unsafe (for example a private or internal address), and `404` for any other request error. `400` or above counts as a failed delivery.

response_time_ms.description: Time the attempt took, in milliseconds. `null` while the delivery is queued.

status.description: Status the event reported when it was generated: the session status for session events (for example `Approved` or `In Review`), the person's or company's status for user and business events, and the transaction status for transaction events. `null` for events that carry no status.

created_at.description: When the delivery was created.

request_header.description: JSON text (a string) of the request headers Didit sent: `Content-Type`, `X-Signature`, `X-Signature-V2`, `X-Signature-Simple`, `X-Timestamp` and `User-Agent`. Parse it with a JSON parser. It holds signatures, never the signing secret.

request_body.description: JSON text (a string) of the exact payload Didit sent, keys sorted, including `event_id` and `timestamp`. Parse it with a JSON parser; see [Payload shape](https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks#payload-shape). For a scoped key without `media: read`, media URLs inside it are `null`; without `sessions: write`, session tokens and hosted verification links are `null`. A body changed that way no longer matches its signatures. Didit does not record the response body your endpoint returned.

SessionWebhookDelivery.description: One webhook delivery attempt recorded for a verification session, with the exact request headers and body Didit sent.

uuid.description: Delivery ID. Use it as `{webhook_uuid}` to get or resend this delivery.

session_id.description: The session the delivery belongs to (the session in the path).

request_url.description: URL the delivery was sent to.

response_status.description: HTTP status your endpoint returned. `null` while the delivery is queued and not yet attempted. When no HTTP answer was received Didit records a status of its own: `504` when your endpoint did not answer within 5 seconds, `503` for a connection failure, `400` when the URL was refused as unsafe (for example a private or internal address), and `404` for any other request error. `400` or above counts as a failed delivery.

status.description: Session status when the event was generated, for example `In Progress`, `Approved` or `Declined`.

request_header.description: JSON text (a string) of the request headers Didit sent: `Content-Type`, `X-Signature`, `X-Signature-V2`, `X-Signature-Simple`, `X-Timestamp` and `User-Agent`. Parse it with a JSON parser. It holds signatures, never the signing secret.

request_body.description: JSON text (a string) of the exact payload Didit sent, keys sorted, including `event_id` and `timestamp`. Parse it with a JSON parser; see [Payload shape](https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks#payload-shape). For a scoped key without `media: read`, media URLs inside it are `null`; without `sessions: write`, session tokens and hosted verification links are `null`. A body changed that way no longer matches its signatures. Didit does not record the response body your endpoint returned.

created_at.description: When the delivery was created.

SessionEvent.description: One entry of a verification session's event timeline.

uuid.description: Event identifier.

event_type.description: What happened. Reported by the device during the hosted flow or SDK: `LINK_OPENED`, `STEP_RENDERED`, `BUTTON_CLICKED`, `FORM_SUBMITTED`, `FILE_UPLOADED`, `ATTEMPT_FAILED` and `LOG` (debugging). Recorded by the server: `SESSION_CREATED`, `SESSION_STATUS_CHANGED` (`details.old_status`, `details.current_status`), `FEATURE_STEP_CHANGED` (`details.old_feature_step`, `details.current_feature_step`), `WORKFLOW_BRANCH_EVALUATED` and `WORKFLOW_STATUS_NODE_REACHED` (the workflow routing trace). `SESSION_COMPLETED`, `NOTE_ADDED` and `MANUAL_REVIEW_STARTED` can appear on older sessions.

created_at.description: When Didit stored the event. Events are stored asynchronously, a few seconds after `sent_at`.

component.description: UI component that reported the event (device events only).

feature_step.description: Verification feature the session was on when the event happened.

step.description: Screen within the feature, for example `DOCUMENT_CAPTURE_FRONT` or `FACE_PASSIVE_LIVENESS`.

details.description: Event-specific data. The keys depend on `event_type`.

ip_address.description: IP address the device reported the event from. `null` for server-recorded events.

user_agent.description: User agent of the device. `null` for server-recorded events.

device_info.description: Device details the SDK or browser reported.

file_url.description: Short-lived presigned link to a file attached to the event (for example a captured image). `null` when there is none, and always `null` for a scoped API key without `media: read`.

sent_at.description: When the event happened, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Results are ordered by it.

AMLDatasetSourceFreshness.description: Freshness of one family of AML datasets.

last_updated_at.description: Most recent update of any dataset in the family.

oldest_updated_at.description: Staleness bound: every dataset in the family is at least this current. `null` when at least one dataset in the family reported no update date, because the bound is then unknown.

dataset_count.description: Number of datasets in the family.

dated_dataset_count.description: Number of those datasets that reported an update date.

AMLDatasetFreshness.description: How current the AML datasets were when a screening ran. Dates are never estimated.

captured_at.description: When Didit read the dataset catalog this freshness comes from.

provider.description: Opaque identifier of the AML data source. Treat it as an opaque string; do not branch on it.

catalog_version.description: Version identifier of the dataset catalog, when the source reports one.

sources.description: Freshness per dataset family. A family whose datasets reported no update date is absent rather than filled with `null`.

AMLScreeningRun.description: One completed ongoing-monitoring re-screen of an AML check.

uuid.description: Identifier of this screening run.

completed_at.description: When this subject's re-screen finished. Results are ordered by it, newest first.

started_at.description: When the monitoring batch this re-screen belongs to started.

outcome.description: `NO_CHANGE`: completed and the result did not move. `CHANGED`: completed and the score, status, hit count or hits changed. `FAILED`: no usable answer for this subject, so the check was left as it was.

trigger.description: What started the screening. Always `ONGOING_MONITORING` today.

provider.description: Opaque identifier of the AML data source that answered. Treat it as an opaque string; do not branch on it.

status.description: AML check status this run left the check in.

score.description: AML score this run left the check in.

total_hits.description: Number of hits this run left the check in.

dataset_freshness.description: Dataset freshness behind this run, or `null` when no dates were available.

KYBKeyPeopleParty.description: A Key People party of a Business Verification (KYB) session, with its child verification. The same party appears in `key_people_checks[].submitted.parties[]` of the business session decision.

uuid.description: Party identifier.

entity_type.description: Whether the party is an individual or a company.

source.description: `REGISTRY`: taken from the company registry. `USER`: entered in the Key People screen.

name.description: Display name of the party.

email.description: Email the verification link is sent to.

nationality.description: Nationality for persons, country of incorporation for companies.

phone_number.description: Phone number collected for the party.

date_of_birth.description: Date of birth (persons).

custom_fields.description: Workflow-defined custom fields collected for the party, keyed by field key.

is_skipped.description: Whether the party is exempt from verification. Regenerating clears it.

requires_verification.description: Whether the role and ownership rules require a verification for this party.

roles.description: Roles the party holds in the company.

ownership_percent.description: Ownership percentage for this role, when known.

voting_percent.description: Voting-rights percentage for this role, when known.

kyc_session_status.description: Status of the child KYC session. A deleted session keeps the status it had when it was deleted.

kyc_session_url.description: Hosted link of the child KYC session. `null` when there is none or it was deleted, and for a scoped API key without `sessions: write`.

kyc_session_deleted.description: The child KYC session was deleted, so it can never settle.

kyb_sub_session_status.description: Status of the child KYB session.

kyb_sub_session_url.description: Hosted link of the child KYB session, with the same `null` rules as `kyc_session_url`.

verification_workflow_type.description: Type of the workflow the child session runs.

verification_workflow_features.description: Features of the child session's workflow with their current status.

feature.description: Feature code, for example `ID_VERIFICATION` or `LIVENESS`.

status.description: Feature status, `Not Finished` until it runs.

didit_internal_id.description: Didit's identifier of the verified person, once known.

TravelRuleDelivery.description: Where the latest message the transfer owes the other side stands. Didit contacts the counterparty after the request that created or changed the transfer has returned, so this object says whether that message got through: queued, being sent, waiting to be retried after an error, delivered, or failed. A failure the network may still recover from (no answer in time, a failed connection, HTTP `408`, `429` or `5xx`) is tried again after 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 30 minutes and 1 hour. When a first message (`kind: SEND`) fails for good, because the network refused it or the sixth attempt failed too, the transfer moves to `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_REACHABLE` with `last_error` in its `timeline`; any other message that fails for good is noted in the `timeline`. The transfer's `status` stays the source of truth for the exchange itself.

kind.description: What the message carries. `SEND`: the transfer's first message to the counterparty (outbound; the rail is chosen when it is sent). `ANSWER`: your accept or decline, owed to the network that asked (inbound). `TXID`: the on-chain transaction hash, after you finish the transfer. `CANCEL`: the cancellation, after you cancel it. `POLL`: a status query to a network that offers one, repeated every 5 minutes while the transfer waits on the counterparty.

status.description: `QUEUED`: waiting to be sent. `SENDING`: an attempt is running. `RETRYING`: an attempt failed and the next one runs at `next_attempt_at`. `DELIVERED`: the other side took the message. `FAILED`: the other side refused it, or the last attempt failed.

rail.description: The rail that carries the message. Empty until Didit has chosen one for a first message.

attempts.description: Attempts made so far for this message. A message that is not a status poll is attempted at most 6 times.

last_error.description:
The kind of failure the last attempt hit, `""` when none did: for example `email undeliverable`, `trp identity endpoint unreachable` or `trp transfer inquiry delivery failed`. It never carries the counterparty's own answer, which stays on the transfer's `timeline`.
When GTR answers with an error, its own status code and message are included. Response bodies are never included.

next_attempt_at.description: When the next attempt runs while the message is `QUEUED` or `RETRYING`.

delivered_at.description: When the other side took the message.

TravelRuleDiscoveryStep.description: One step of the counterparty discovery Didit ran for an outbound transfer, in the order it ran them. The first step that names a VASP with a route ends the chain.

step.description: `internal_address_book`: another Didit customer that proved control of the destination wallet. `wallet_attribution`: the wallet's blockchain analytics attribution. `network_lookup`: a network that can say which VASP holds the address. `customer_hint`: the VASP name, LEI or jurisdiction you sent in `beneficiary_data`. `end_user`: the counterparty the end user (or you) picked, or the request to pick one.

outcome.description: `match`: the step named a counterparty. `miss`: it ran and found none. `skipped`: it could not run, and `reason` says why.

reason.description: Machine-readable reason, `""` on a match: `no_proven_internal_wallet`, `attribution_disabled`, `already_attributed`, `no_attributed_entity`, `directory_match_no_route`, `gtr_address_lookup_runs_on_dispatch`, `no_membership`, `network_switched_off`, `no_network_address_lookup`, `no_directory_match`, `awaiting_end_user` or `picked_member_without_proven_wallet`.

vasp.description: The directory VASP the step named, when it named one.

rail.description: The rail that reaches that counterparty, when the step found one.

TravelRuleNextAction.description: One thing that moves a `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_FOUND` or `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_REACHABLE` transfer on. See [Why a transfer is stuck](/transaction-monitoring/travel-rule#why-a-transfer-is-stuck).

action.description: `select_counterparty_vasp`: the end user picks the destination VASP in the wallet-ownership widget. `declare_self_hosted`: the end user declares the wallet self-hosted in the widget. `add_vasp_hint`: tell Didit who the counterparty is, with a VASP name, LEI or travel address (for example a `travel_address` on the destination wallet's address-book entry), then resend. `update_compliance_email` and `resend` are `action` values of `PATCH /v3/transactions/{transaction_id}/travel-rule/`: give the counterparty's compliance email again, and re-run routing.

url.description: The wallet-ownership widget link, on `select_counterparty_vasp` and `declare_self_hosted` while the transfer has an open widget session.

TransactionTravelRule.description: A transaction's Travel Rule transfer, as `GET /v3/transactions/{transaction_id}/`, the `201` of `POST /v3/transactions/` and each row of `GET /v3/transactions/` return it. `direction`, `rail`, `counterparty_vasp`, `delivery`, `discovery`, `reason` and `next_actions` have the same shape as on `PATCH /v3/transactions/{transaction_id}/travel-rule/`, so one read of a transaction says why its transfer is stuck and what moves it on.

originator_data.description: Originator party. For an inbound transfer the counterparty's values are masked until ownership is confirmed.

beneficiary_data.description: Beneficiary party. For an inbound transfer the counterparty's values are masked until ownership is confirmed.

name_match.description: The name comparison that decided the transfer (score and strictness). Null until one ran. The compared names are masked together with the parties.

mismatched_fields.description: Shortcut for `data_match.mismatched_fields`. Empty when nothing differs.

data_masked.description: True while the counterparty's personal data is masked in this response.

direction.description: Which side of the exchange this transfer is.

rail.description: The rail the transfer went over: `INTERNAL`, `TRP`, `GTR`, `TRUST`, `VERIFYVASP`, `SYGNA` or `EMAIL` (`TEST_VASP` on a sandbox application, when the Didit Test VASP answered), or `null` until a rail is chosen.

dd_score.description: Due-diligence score from 0 to 100, where higher is better. Same scale as in the VASP directory.

dd_score_breakdown.description: Per-component contributions to dd_score, one object per component as in the VASP directory (jurisdiction, verification, protocol, lei, history, essentials, responsiveness), each {points, max, reason, detail}. {} until the counterparty has been assessed.

max.description: Maximum points this component can award.

reason.description: Machine-readable code of the component's verdict.

detail.description: Human-readable reason for the awarded points.

dd_assessed_at.description: When the due-diligence assessment last ran. Null until the counterparty has been assessed.

counterparty_vasp.description: The counterparty's directory entry, or `null` when the transfer links none.

delivery.description: The newest message the transfer owes another party. `null` when it has owed none, for example below `threshold_amount` or for a declared self-hosted wallet.

discovery.description: How Didit looked for the counterparty, one entry per step that ran. Empty when no discovery ran, for example on an inbound transfer.

reason.description: Why a `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_FOUND` or `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_REACHABLE` transfer is stuck; `""` for any other status. A failed delivery decides it first, on `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_REACHABLE` only: `email_undeliverable` (the mail provider refused the compliance email and no address is left to try: when it was sent, on a reminder, or as a permanent bounce reported later) or `delivery_failed` (the rail that was delivering failed for good: a network rail refused the message or ran out of retries, a `TRP` identity host did not answer, or the counterparty's `TRP` host did not accept the inquiry). Otherwise the `discovery` trace decides it: `awaiting_end_user` (no step named a counterparty Didit can reach), `directory_match_no_route` (a step named a directory VASP that has no route), `picked_member_without_proven_wallet` (the end user picked a Didit customer that has not proven control of the wallet), or `no_directory_match` when the trace gives no other reason. A resend moves the transfer on, so the reason clears. See [Why a transfer is stuck](/transaction-monitoring/travel-rule#why-a-transfer-is-stuck).

next_actions.description: What moves the transfer on; `[]` for any status but `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_FOUND` or `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_REACHABLE`. `email_undeliverable` offers `update_compliance_email`, then `resend`. `delivery_failed` offers `resend`. A discovery reason offers `select_counterparty_vasp`, `declare_self_hosted`, `add_vasp_hint` and `resend`.

NetworkListCounts.description: Network counts for the list's views and filter options, each network counted once. Returned only when `summary` is not `false`. `scopes` count every network visible to the application. `views` count the visible networks inside the selected `scope`. `facets` count the networks in the selected `scope` and `status` view (dismissed networks are left out unless `status` includes them). The other list filters do not change these counts.

transactions.description: Networks whose members are all transaction parties.

views.description: Visible networks inside the selected `scope`, by status, plus two saved views.

mine.description: Networks assigned to the calling console member. Always 0 for an API key.

high_risk.description: Networks with a risk score of 80 or more that are not dismissed.

facets.description: Counts for each filter option, inside the selected `scope` and status view.

total.description: Networks in the selected `scope` and status view.

last_activity_days.description: Networks with activity in the last 7, 30 and 90 days, keyed by the number of days.

risk_min.description: Networks with a risk score of at least 50 and at least 80, keyed by the threshold.

signal_types.description: Networks with at least one signal of each type.

priority.description: Networks by priority. `none` counts networks without a priority.

me.description: Assigned to the calling console member. Always 0 for an API key.

users.description: One entry per assignee, most networks first.

full_name.description: The assignee's name, or their email when no name is set.

has_case.description: Networks this application opened a case for.

min_size.description: Networks with at least 10 members, keyed by the minimum size.

NetworkTag.description: One of your application's tags on the network.

uuid.description: The tag's UUID, the same value you pass as `tag_uuid`.

source.description: `didit` for a Didit preset tag, `custom` for a tag your team created.

added_by.description: Email of the console member who added the tag. Null when an API key added it.

NetworkOutcomes.description: Where the network's people and businesses stand. Each member you may see counts once, by the status of their most recent verification that reached a decision. Transaction parties are not counted.

approved.description: Members whose most recent decided verification was approved.

declined.description: Members whose most recent decided verification was declined.

in_review.description: Members whose most recent decided verification is in review.

total.description: Members with at least one verification, decided or not. A member whose verifications are all undecided (not started, in progress, expired or abandoned) counts here and in no other key.

NetworkPatternScore.description: How alike one kind of the members' data is across the whole network. A pattern is not a signal: no shared value links the members.

type.description: `background`: the mean similarity of every pair of member selfie backgrounds, with the person masked out. It reads the newest selfie of each person, at most the 50 newest, and leaves out age assurance sessions. It covers the whole network, not only the members of your applications.

score.description: From 0 to 1, rounded to 4 decimals. Null when `reason` is set.

members.description: How many members' selfies the score compared. A selfie that cannot be read, or shows too little background, is not compared. Null while `computing`; 0 or 1 with `not_enough_selfies`.

reason.description: Why there is no score. `computing`: the score for the current members is being computed; read the network again later. `not_enough_selfies`: fewer than two members have a usable selfie. Null when there is a score.

computed_at.description: When the score was computed. Null while `computing`.

NetworkDetailResponse.description: The network detail, plus the organization's sharing mode, whether cross-organization signals apply to it, your application's tags on the network, member outcomes and pattern scores.

sharing_mode.description: The organization's cross-organization sharing mode. Only `global` compares networks across organizations; `private` and `off` keep them to the organization's own history.

cross_org_available.description: Whether cross-organization signals apply to this organization. They need both the Identity Enterprise plan and the `global` sharing mode.

cross_org_unavailable_reason.description: Why cross-organization signals do not apply, checked in this order. `plan`: the organization's Identity plan does not include the cross-organization fraud network (it needs Identity Enterprise), whatever the sharing mode. `sharing_mode`: the plan includes it, but the sharing mode is `private` or `off`. Null when `cross_org_available` is `true`.

tags.description: Your application's tags on the network, oldest first. Each application sees only its own tags. `fraud_tags` is separate and unchanged: the tags the network's members carry.

patterns.description: Pattern scores over the whole network. Today one item, `background`.

tag_uuid.description: UUID of one of your application's tags.

NetworkTimeline.title: Default timeline (no contract)
NetworkTimeline.description: Without `contract`: the network's own events, oldest first, not paginated.

NetworkTimelinePage.title: Typed timeline page (contract=2)
NetworkTimelinePage.description: With `contract=2`: one page of typed events, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to read the next page. Null on the last page.

NetworkTypedTimelineEvent.description: One typed timeline event: the four default fields, plus its id, when Didit stored it, the member account and record it belongs to, and the detail block of its event type. The other detail blocks are null.

label.description: A short English label, for example `Verification attempt 2 of 3`.

metadata.description: For the network's own events, the same metadata as the default timeline. Empty otherwise.

account.description: The member account. Null for the network's own events, `case_linked` and `note_added`.

source_ref.description: The source record. Null for the network's own events and `note_added`.

note_added.description: Set on `note_added` events. Never returned to an API key.

NetworkTimelineAccount.description: The member account the event belongs to.

node_id.description: `<kind>:<uuid>`, where kind is `vendor_user`, `vendor_business` or `transaction_party`.

ownership.description: `owned` when the record belongs to the application you called (for a console member, to an application they were granted). `organization` when it belongs to another application of your organization.

NetworkTimelineSourceRef.description: The record the event was read from.

ownership.description: `owned` when the record belongs to the application you called (for a console member, to an application they were granted). `organization` when it belongs to another application of your organization.

NetworkTimelineRoute.description: Where the record opens: its kind, its UUID and the application it belongs to.

kind.description: `user`, `business` or `transaction_party` for an account; `session`, `business_session` or `transaction` for a source record.

NetworkTimelineAttempt.description: One verification session of the account.

session_id.description: The session UUID, or the business session UUID for a company.

attempt.description: This session's position among the account's sessions, in creation order.

attempt_count.description: How many sessions the account has.

status.description: The session status, for example `Approved` or `Declined`.

decline_reasons.description: For a declined session only: its warnings, oldest first, once per warning. Empty otherwise.

feature.description: The feature that raised the warning.

NetworkTimelineTransaction.description: A transaction a member account took part in, dated by its transaction date.

amount.description: Null when the transaction has no amount.

party_role.description: The account's role in the transaction: `APPLICANT`, `REMITTER`, `BENEFICIARY` or `COUNTERPARTY`.

NetworkTimelineLogin.description: A sign-in event you posted for a person through the events API.

action.description: `<event_category>.<action_type>`: `auth.login` or `security.login_succeeded` for a sign-in, `auth.login_failed` or `security.login_failed` for a failed one.

status.description: The event's status.

ip.description: Null when the event has no IP address.

device.description: Null when the event has no device fingerprint or context.

is_first_login.description: The account's first successful sign-in on record.

is_new_device.description: A successful sign-in from a device none of the account's earlier successful sign-ins came from. Never true on the first sign-in.

connection_type.description: The connection type label for the address, as free text.

label.description: A readable device label built from the event's device context.

NetworkTimelineRuleHit.description: A live rule that matched a member's transaction or event. Test-mode matches are not included.

NetworkTimelineCaseLinked.description: A case opened for the network in your organization. `source_ref.ownership` says whether it belongs to the application you called.

NetworkTimelineNoteAdded.description: A note left on the network. The note text is not included.

FeatureStatusOverride.description: One override of a check (feature) status made with `PATCH /v3/session/{sessionId}/features/{nodeId}/update-status/`: what it changes, whether it applied or still waits for the person to finish the flow, who asked and why.

id.description: Identifier of the override. Pass it to the cancel endpoint.

node_id.description: The workflow node the request named (`default` for a step without a node).

feature_type.description: The `feature_type` the request passed, or an empty string when it passed none.

feature_model.description: The kind of check that was overridden, for example `KYC`, `Face`, `AML` or `GeolocationCheck`.

previous_status.description: The check's status when the override was requested.

state.description: `applied`: the check has the new status. `pending_until_flow_finishes`: the override waits and applies when the person finishes the flow. `cancelled`: it waited and never applied (see `cancel_reason`).

forced.description: `true` when the override applied at once while the person was still in the flow.

reason.description: The `comment` sent with the request, or `null`.

requested_by.description: Who requested the override, or `null` when that is not known.

email.description: Email of the console user, or `null` for API keys and the system.

name.description: Display name of the requester, or `null`.

type.description: Who made the request: a console user, an API key, or Didit itself.

applied_at.description: When the check took the new status, or `null` while it waits or once it is cancelled.

cancelled_at.description: When a waiting override was cancelled, or `null`.

cancel_reason.description: Why a waiting override never applied, or `null`. `cancelled_by_reviewer`: cancelled with the cancel endpoint. `replaced`: a newer override on the same check replaced it. `check_changed`: the person redid the check before finishing the flow. `session_closed`: the session left the flow before the person finished it (abandoned, expired, or decided mid-flow).

SandboxSimulateRequest.description: Force a sandbox session's status. Every field is optional, but at least one of `new_status`, `scenario` or `risk` is required.

new_status.description: The status to set. When you leave it out, it defaults to the default status of the risk case (`risk`, or the first risk the scenario's magic values carry), else to the scenario's default status.

comment.description: Note added to the activity entry the status change records.

scenario.description: A scenario slug from the catalog (`GET /v1/sandbox/scenarios/`). It supplies the default status and, without `risk`, the warning its magic values carry. An unknown slug returns `400`.

risk.description: A risk case from the catalog. Its warning is added to the session, with a log type that follows `new_status`. An unknown value returns `400`.

node_id.description: Workflow node the risk warning is attached to. Defaults to the session's current node.

send_webhooks.description: `true` sends exactly the webhooks a real status change sends to the sandbox application's destinations: `status.updated`, plus the `user.status.updated` / `user.data.updated` (or `business.status.updated` / `business.data.updated`) events the change causes, for destinations subscribed to them. `false` changes the status without logging or sending any webhook: the missed-webhook recovery never re-sends that decision, the console still updates live, and the next status change of the session sends webhooks as usual.

previous_status.description: The session's status before the simulation.

status.description: The status the simulation set.

scenario.description: The scenario slug you passed, or `null`.

risk.description: The risk case applied (`risk`, or the one taken from the scenario), or `null` when none.

CaseTeamSummary.description: The review team that owns the case, or null when no team owns it. Routing sets it when a routing rule places the case with one of its teams. Change or clear it with `PATCH .../cases/{case_uuid}/` (`team`).

CaseChecker.description: The member named to approve or reject the pending resolution. Set only while a four-eyes resolution waits on a named checker. Null when nothing is pending, while the pending resolution waits on the checker queue, and once the resolution is approved, rejected, or returned for a new review because the evidence changed.

member_uuid.description: The member's user uuid: the value you pass as `checker` when you resolve the case.

name.description: The member's full name, or null when it is not known.

ServiceStatusFeed.description: Public service status: the state of each Didit service, the overall state, and the incidents that are ongoing or were resolved in the last 7 days.

status.description: The worst state of any service right now, decided by the ongoing incidents only.

updated_at.description: When Didit built this response (ISO 8601, UTC). Responses are cached for 30 seconds, so it can be up to 30 seconds old.

services.description: One entry per service, every service always listed.

incidents.description: Newest `started_at` first. Every ongoing incident, plus the incidents resolved in the last 7 days (at most 50 resolved incidents). Empty when nothing happened in that time.

key.description: Stable service key.
