Match on this, never on the display name. `service_id_verification`: ID verification, `service_liveness_face_match`: Liveness and face match, `service_aml_screening`: AML screening, `service_kyb_registries`: KYB registries, `service_database_validation`: Database validation, `service_phone_delivery`: Phone verification delivery, `service_email_delivery`: Email verification delivery, `service_transaction_monitoring`: Transaction monitoring.

name.description: English display name of the service.

status.description: `operational` when no incident is ongoing for the service, otherwise the worst state of its ongoing incidents.

service_name.description: English display name of the affected service.

state.description: How the service is affected. A resolved incident keeps the last state it had.

status.description: `ongoing` until the service recovers, then `resolved`.

title.description: English headline. To translate it, build your own text from `service`, `state` and `country_name`.
title.example: Database validation is degraded in Brazil.

body.description: English detail line: since when checks may be slow or fail, or when it recovered.
body.example: Checks against Brazil (CPF) may be slow or fail since 08:55 UTC.

affected.description: Countries or registries affected, for example `Brazil (CPF)`. Empty when the incident is not tied to a country or registry.

country_name.description: Country affected, in English. Empty when the incident is not tied to a country.

resolved_at.description: When the service recovered (ISO 8601, UTC). `null` while the incident is ongoing.

duration_minutes.description: Whole minutes from `started_at` to `resolved_at`. `null` while the incident is ongoing.

TravelRuleJoinInvitation.description: What the join page shows before anything is typed.

email.description: The address the invitation went to.

source.description: Where the invitation came from, for example `pickup`.

email.description: Must be the address the invitation went to.

code.description: The 6-character code emailed after registering.

TravelRuleJoinCredentials.description: The new free organization and the credentials its application calls the API with.

api_key.description: Send as the `x-api-key` header on the workspace endpoints.

vasp_id.description: The directory entry this workspace is. Read ids from `GET /v3/travel-rule/vasps/`.

enabled.description: Only `true` is accepted: outbound billing cannot be turned back off through the API.

TravelRuleWorkspaceTxtRecord.description: The TXT record to publish for the DNS proof. Empty until a proof has been started.

TravelRuleWorkspace.description: The free Travel Rule workspace of an application that joined free.

prefill.description: Profile values taken from the directory entry: `vasp_id`, `legal_name`, `lei`, `jurisdiction`, `compliance_email`, `domains`. Nothing is written until the claim is made.

billing_enabled.description: Receiving Travel Rule data is free. Sending is billed only after billing is enabled.

didit_network.description: Whether the Didit network lists this VASP and, when not, each condition it still misses.

InvestigatorDecision.description: How the item left the Investigator queue. `decided_by`, `original_outcome` and `overrides` are returned by the accept and override endpoints and the report; the `investigator` block of a session decision carries the other fields.

outcome.description: `accepted` or `edited` took the recommendation (`edited` with a rewritten narrative), `overridden` took another action, `decided_elsewhere` is a decision taken outside the Investigator while the report was open, `automated` is a decision the Investigator took on its own.

final_status.description: The item's status after the decision.

agreed.description: Whether the decision matched the recommendation.

original_outcome.description: The decision the Investigator took on its own, unchanged by later overrides. Null for a decision the team took.

overrides.description: Every override of a decision the Investigator took on its own, oldest first.

InvestigatorBlock.description: The item's latest Investigator review, or null when it never had one. Carried by the V3 session and business session decision (and so by `status.updated` webhooks).

automated.description: The Investigator decided on its own, even if the decision was later overridden.

subject.description: The item under review: `id`, `number`, `status`, `name` and, depending on the kind, `country`, `workflow`, `vendor_data`, `txn_id`, `amount`, `currency`, `direction`, `title` or `priority`.

guardrails.description: The locked guardrails that hold this item, if any.

lookups.description: How many sections and linked records it read.

report.description: The report: reasoning, evidence points with their verdict (`ok`, `risk`, `look`, `explained`, `context`) and cited sources, screening hit verdicts (`same`, `not_same`, `unclear`) and suggested next steps.

trail.description: What I checked: the overview, sections and records it read, in order.

autonomy.description: What autonomy made of the report (`result`, `reason`, `tier`, `policy_version`, `rule`, `agreement`, `decisions`, `threshold`, `at`). Null when the queue is not automated.

narrative.description: A rewritten narrative. Sending one records the decision as edited and accepted.

send_email.description: Email the person about the decision.
Email the person about the decision.

monthly_spend_limit.description: Monthly limit in your billing currency, 0.01 to 1,000,000. Null turns it off.

reserved.description: The price of every open live report, held back because accepting it charges it.

paused.description: At the limit: no new review starts.

TravelRuleUtxoEntry.description: One input or output of a UTXO transaction, as the chain recorded it.

amount.description: Decimal string in the coin's own unit (BTC, not satoshis). Optional.

txid.description: Optional. The transaction an input spends.

vout.description: Optional. The output index an input spends.

TravelRuleUtxo.description: The inputs and outputs of a UTXO transfer (BTC, LTC, BCH, DOGE). Only accepted on those chains: on any other chain it is a `400`. From them Didit infers the originator wallet (the declared one, else the input address that contributed the most) and the beneficiary output (the declared one, else the only output that does not pay an input address back as change, else the one output paying the transfer amount). The result is on the transfer's `chain_details`.

inputs.description: Optional. Without inputs no originator is inferred and no change output is recognised.

TravelRuleChainSide.description: One side's wallet as Didit resolved it from the chain data.

address.description: The wallet. On a memo network the classic address (an XRP X-address is split into its classic address and its tag); on Lightning the payee node id or Lightning Address.

memo.description: The destination tag or memo that is part of the wallet; `""` for none.

source.description: Where the wallet came from: `declared` (your request), `x_address` (split from an XRP X-address), `largest_input` (the UTXO input address that contributed the most), `only_non_change_output` (the only UTXO output that is not change), `amount_match` (the one UTXO output paying the transfer amount), `invoice_payee` (the payee a Lightning payment request names), `updated` (set later with `action: update_originator_wallet`).

TravelRuleChainDetails.description: How the transfer's chain names its two wallets, when that is more than one address paying another. Empty (`{}`) for an account-chain transfer (EVM, Solana, Tron), where the two addresses are the wallets. Matching, routing and the address book read the wallets from here first.

chain.description: Canonical chain, e.g. `BTC`, `XRP`, or `LIGHTNING` for a Lightning transfer.

utxo.description: On a UTXO transfer: the inputs and outputs as stored (amounts as decimal strings) and which outputs Didit read as what.

change_output_indexes.description: Outputs that pay an input address back.

beneficiary_output_index.description: The output that pays the beneficiary; null when none could be told apart.

lightning.description: On a Lightning transfer: what the payment request says. Always `kind` (`bolt11`, `bolt12_offer`, `bolt12_invoice`, `bolt12_invoice_request`, `lnurl`, `lightning_address`, `node_id` or `unknown`); a BOLT11 invoice adds `network`, `payee_node_id`, `payment_hash`, `amount_msat`, `created_at` and `expires_at`; a BOLT12 string `blinded_paths` and `payee_node_id`; an LNURL or a Lightning Address its `domain`. Nothing is resolved over the network: the request is decoded only.

warnings.description: UTXO inconsistencies worth a look: the declared originator is not an input, the declared beneficiary is not an output, no single beneficiary output could be told apart, or the beneficiary output pays a different amount than the transaction states.

not_applicable_reason.description: On an outbound Lightning transfer whose payment request names no payee: why the transfer is `NOT_APPLICABLE`. `LIGHTNING_NO_PAYEE_IDENTIFIER` (the request names no payee node, or could not be decoded), `LIGHTNING_BOLT12_BLINDED_PAYEE` (the offer hides its payee behind blinded paths), `LIGHTNING_LNURL_NAMES_NO_PAYEE` (an LNURL names a service, not a payee). The same code opens the transfer's last `timeline` entry.

WalletAddressImportRow.description: One wallet to import: by its `address`, its `address_hash`, or both. The camelCase forms of these fields are accepted too, as are `walletAddress`, `walletAddressHash`, `destinationTag` and `externalUserId`.

address.description: The wallet address. Alias: `walletAddress`.

address_hash.description: SHA-256 of the lowercased address, as 64 hex characters or 44 base64 characters. Send it alone to register a wallet without disclosing its address; sent with `address`, it must be that address's hash. Alias: `walletAddressHash`.

memo.description: The destination tag or memo. XRP: a destination tag, a whole number from 0 to 4294967295 (a JSON number is accepted). XLM: a text memo of up to 28 bytes, a 64-bit id or a 32-byte hash in hex. EOS: up to 256 bytes. ATOM: up to 256 characters. HBAR: up to 100 bytes. Bitcoin, EVM, Solana, Tron, Litecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Dogecoin and Lightning wallets take no memo: one there is a `400`.

holder_vendor_data.description: Your internal identifier for the holder. Alias: `externalUserId`.

self_declared.description: Create the entry already verified through a self-declaration, when your settings allow it.

WalletAddressImportReport.description: What happened to each row of an import, in the order sent.

status.description: `created`: added to the book. `existing`: the wallet is already in the book and was left untouched. `duplicate`: repeats an earlier row of this import. `failed`: see `errors`.

entry_id.description: The address-book entry the row created or found.

errors.description: Field errors of a `failed` row; empty otherwise.

duplicate_of_row.description: On a `duplicate` row, the row it repeats.

TravelRuleCounterpartyContact.description: A compliance address the EMAIL rail writes to for one directory entry.

counterparty.description: The directory entry's `id`, as GET /v3/travel-rule/vasps/ shows it.

name.description: Optional label, for example the team name.

source.description: staff: curated by Didit. learned: an address at one of the VASP's own domains that answered a request through its response link. application: added by your application.

scope.description: platform: curated by Didit or learned from a verified answer, used for every Didit customer, read-only for you. application: private to your application.

created_by.description: Empty for platform contacts and for contacts an API key added.

verified_at.description: When this address last answered a request through its response link.

is_invalid.description: true once the address bounced or complained; the EMAIL rail skips it.

invalid_detail.description: The receiving mail server's reason, when it gave one.

name.description: Optional label.

TravelRuleNameMatch.description: The name comparison that decided the transfer, or null until one ran. While the parties are masked, and on the other customer's copy of an INTERNAL exchange, `transfer_name`, `compared_name`, `matched_names` and `mismatched_names` are hidden. `score` and `matched` can disagree: `matched` follows the strictness, `score` is the similarity of the two full names.

score.description: Similarity of the two full names, 0 to 100. 0 when either name is blank.

matched.description: Whether the names satisfy `strictness`. The transfer's outcome follows `data_match`, which compares every field, so a transfer can be COUNTERPARTY_MISMATCHED_DATA while this is true.

method.description: How `matched` was decided: none (`NONE`), exact_token (`STRICT`), token_subset (`DEFAULT`), token_containment (`CONTAINS`) or sequence_ratio (`FUZZY`).

compared_with.description: wallet_holder: the holder recorded for the wallet. counterparty_vasp: the name the counterparty answered on the email response page, or the Didit Test VASP's answer in sandbox.

compared_name.description: The name it was compared with.

mismatched_names.description: Words of `transfer_name` missing from `compared_name`, then words of `compared_name` missing from `transfer_name`.

TravelRuleTransferRow.description: One Travel Rule transfer as the transfers list shows it: VASP names, wallets and memos only, never the originator or beneficiary person data.

transaction_id.description: The Didit transaction the transfer belongs to.

txn_id.description: Your own id for the transaction. Transfers Didit books for you, such as a Didit Test VASP inbound transfer, carry a generated one.

kind.description: withdrawal: outbound. message: an inbound transfer a rail created from a counterparty's message (a TRP inquiry, the INTERNAL inbound leg, or a GTR, VerifyVASP or Sygna Bridge message). deposit: any other inbound transfer.

reason.description: Why a `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_FOUND` or `COUNTERPARTY_VASP_NOT_REACHABLE` transfer is stuck, the same value as the transfer's own `reason`, so the list tells a bounced compliance email from a counterparty with no route without opening each transfer. `""` for any other status. See [Why a transfer is stuck](/transaction-monitoring/travel-rule#why-a-transfer-is-stuck).

amount.description: The amount as a plain decimal, for example "1.25".

originator_vasp.description: Outbound: your VASP's legal name. Inbound: the counterparty's name, from its directory entry, the Didit network member, the TRP sender, the Didit Test VASP, or the name the transfer declared. Empty when none is known.

beneficiary_vasp.description: Outbound: the counterparty's name, worked out the same way. Inbound: your VASP's legal name.

originator_memo.description: Memo or destination tag, empty on chains without one.

originator_wallet_type.description: vasp, self_hosted (declared unhosted) or own (a wallet your address book records as yours). Your own side is always vasp.

matched_transaction_id.description: The other side of a deposit you matched to an announced transfer by hand.

deadline_at.description: When the transfer expires if it is still waiting on its counterparty. Set on every transfer you create with `POST /v3/transactions/` that needs an exchange, outbound or inbound. Null below the threshold, on a Lightning payment the Travel Rule does not apply to, and on inbound transfers Didit creates when a counterparty reaches you (an inbound TRP inquiry, a network message or the INTERNAL inbound leg).

BankAccountCheckHolder.description: The name the account is checked against. Send exactly one of `full_name` and `business_name`.

country.description: The account's country, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code, for example `GBR`. Lowercase is accepted.

account.description: The account the way its country writes it: an `iban`, or an `account_number` with the bank or branch code the country needs (`sort_code`, `routing_number`, `transit_institution`, `bsb`, `ifsc`, `bank_code` or `bic`). Mexico takes a `clabe` and Argentina a `cbu_cvu`, which already name the bank. A business account adds a `registration_id` where the country asks for one. Spaces, dashes and dots are ignored. Keys the country's check does not use are ignored; a key it needs and does not get is a `400` that names it.

iban.description: The IBAN, in a country that uses IBANs. It must belong to `country`.

account_number.description: The account number, in a country that writes the account with a separate bank or branch code.

routing_number.description: United States: the 9-digit ABA routing number.

transit_institution.description: Canada: the 8-digit transit and institution number.

bank_code.description: The bank's code, where the country needs one, for example in Nigeria.

bic.description: The bank's BIC, where the country's check asks for one.

clabe.description: Mexico: the 18-digit CLABE. It already names the bank.

cbu_cvu.description: Argentina: the 22-digit CBU or CVU. It already names the bank.

registration_id.description: A business account's registration number, where the country asks for one.

vendor_data.description: Your own reference for this check, returned unchanged.

request_id.description: The ID of this check.

result.description: `match`: the bank holds the account under the name you sent. `close_match`: under a close name, for example a missing middle name or a typo. `no_match`: under another name, or there is no such account. `cannot_verify`: the bank answered without comparing the name, for example for a blocked or closed account.

holder_name.description: Only on a `close_match`, and only when the bank returned it: the name on the account, as the bank holds it. `null` otherwise.

account.description: The account, masked to its last 4 characters.

vendor_data.description: Your own reference, as you sent it.

created_at.description: When the check ran, in UTC.

code.description: A stable code to branch on. Absent on `401` and `403`.

field.description: `400` only: the body field to correct, as a dotted path, for example `account.sort_code`.

reason.description: `400` only: why the field was refused. `required`, `length`, `format`, `checksum` and `country_mismatch` (an IBAN of another country) are Didit's own checks; `rejected` means the bank refused the account as sent.

BankVerificationResult.description: One Bank Verification step's result, for User and Business Verification. `method` says how the account was verified. See [Bank verification methods](/core-technology/bank-verification/verification-methods).

schema_version.description: Version of this result shape. `1` today.

node_id.description: The workflow node this result belongs to.

status.description: The step's verdict, after its actions and status rules.

original_status.description: The first verdict the step reached, before any later change such as a manual review.

method.description: How the account was verified: `open_banking` (bank sign-in: the person signed in at their bank), `account_lookup` (account check: the person typed the account details and the bank confirmed the name), `microdeposits` or `statement` (a statement upload). `null` until an account is evaluated. Workflow rules read the same value as `bank.method`.

provider.description: The key of the route that ran the connection. Read `method`, not this key, to tell how the account was verified.

credential_source.description: `native`: Didit's own route, billed to your Didit balance. `byok`: a marketplace provider you connected with your own credentials.

route.description: The route chosen before consent. It never changes afterwards.

is_fallback.description: Whether Didit's own route stood in for a marketplace provider that could not connect.

requested_scopes.description: The data the connection asked for, for example `ownership` or `balances`.

connection.description: The latest attempt's connection. `null` before the first attempt.

institution_id.description: The bank's ID. `null` for an account check, where no bank is picked.

institution_name.description: The bank's name. `null` for an account check.

oauth.description: Whether the bank sign-in ran over OAuth or app-to-app. `null` for an account check.

consent_expires_at.description: When the bank consent ends, for bank sign-in.

last_refreshed_at.description: When the financial data was last read again.

attempts.description: The attempts the person spent on this step, every method together.

reason_code.description: Why the connection is not simply `connected`, for example `USER_CANCELLED`, `INSTITUTION_DOWN`, `ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`, `REFERENCE_IDENTITY_MISSING` or `VERIFICATION_COMPLETED`.

account.description: The evaluated account. `null` until an account is evaluated.

sort_code.description: The sort code, in the United Kingdom.

ownership.description: How the account holder compared with the verified identity. `null` until an account is evaluated.

result.description: `partial_match` is a close match. `not_verifiable`: the bank answered with no holder to compare. `unknown`: the evidence could not be read, or there was no identity to compare.

reference_identity_source.description: The step whose identity the holder was compared against: `kyc`, `database_validation`, `expected_details`, `questionnaire`, `document_ai` or `kyb`.

provider_name_score.description: The bank's own holder name score, when it returned one.

address_score.description: The holder address score, when address matching ran.

email_score.description: The holder email score, when email matching ran.

phone_score.description: The holder phone score, when phone matching ran.

dob_score.description: The holder date of birth score, when the bank shared one.

close_match.description: Whether the name landed in the close-match band.

holder_confirmation.description: The person's answer when asked to confirm a close-match name. `null` when never asked.

method.description: Which name comparison produced the score. This is not the verification method: read the top-level `method` for that.

holders.description: Each holder the bank listed, with its scores.

financial_data.description: The financial data the step read. Only bank sign-in reads it.

categorization.description: Didit's categorization of the transactions read. `null` without them.

not_collected.description: The data the step asked for that the method which verified the account does not collect. Balances, transactions and income come from bank sign-in only, so an account verified by account check lists them here. Never a failure. Empty otherwise.

marketplace_fee.description: The marketplace platform fee charged, for `byok`.

usage_type.description: The usage line the charge was booked on.

reference_identity.description: The identity the holder was compared against, with its source.

signals.description: Account signals read from the transaction history, when the step read one.

connection_abandoned.description: Whether the step ended without a match after the person left at their bank.

not_covered.description: Whether the person's bank or country could not be reached on this step.

evidence_purged_at.description: When the bank evidence was deleted under `bank_evidence_retention_days`. `null` otherwise.

warnings.description: Informational codes, for example `holder_declared`. A warning never changes the status on its own.

reason_codes.description: Why the verdict came out the way it did, for example `OWNER_NAME_PARTIAL`. Several may apply.

BankAccountCheckPersonHolder.description: The person who should hold the account.

full_name.description: The full name of the person who should hold the account.

BankAccountCheckBusinessHolder.description: The company that should hold the account. Checks a business account.

business_name.description: The name of the company that should hold the account. Checks a business account.

ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Your application's API key, from Developers -> API keys in the Business Console. The primary key has full access. A named key can be scoped: none, read or write per resource, limited to some workflows or to approved sessions, to a list of IP addresses, and to an expiry date. 401 means the key is missing, wrong, revoked or expired; 403 means the key has no access to this resource or action, or the request came from an address outside its IP list; 404 on a session route means the session is outside the key's workflows or statuses. A key without media access receives image, video and PDF URLs as null, and a key without sessions write receives session links and tokens as null. See https://docs.didit.me/console/api-keys.

TransactionTokenAuth.name: X-Transaction-Token
TransactionTokenAuth.description: Short-lived scoped token minted by your backend via POST /v3/transactions/sdk-token/. Used by the Didit SDKs on the device-facing /v1/transactions/ endpoints.

SessionTokenAuth.name: Session-Token
SessionTokenAuth.description: Short-lived token returned in the `session_token` field of POST /v3/session/. Used by the hosted verification flow (and custom sandbox UIs) to call session-scoped endpoints on behalf of the verifying user, without your server-side API key.

CaseRequestToken.name: X-Case-Request-Token
CaseRequestToken.description: Request-specific credential from the secure link. Grants access only to this request.

value.detail: Invalid API Key.
You do not have permission to perform this action.

value.error: You don't have enough credits to perform this request. Please top up at https://business.didit.me

value.detail: Resource not found.

ip: Enter a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address.

country_code: Ensure this field has no more than 3 characters.

ip_address: Enter a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address.

claimed_country: Ensure this field has no more than 3 characters.

RiskPermissionDenied.description: The API key is missing or invalid, or the organization cannot cover the live lookup. This API never returns `401`.

Missing or invalid API key.summary: No `x-api-key` header, or the key is invalid or revoked

value.detail: You do not have permission to perform this action.

Not enough credits.summary: Organization balance cannot cover the lookup price

value.error: You don't have enough credits to perform this request.

RateLimitedWrite.description: The shared write limit of 300 requests per minute per API key was exceeded. Honor `Retry-After` before retrying.

example.detail: Write request rate limit exceeded. You can make up to 300 requests per minute.

WebhookSignature.name: X-Signature
WebhookSignature.description: Lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the destination's secret, of the exact raw request body.

WebhookSignatureV2.name: X-Signature-V2
WebhookSignatureV2.description: Lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the destination's secret, of the canonical JSON of the body (keys sorted, no whitespace, non-ASCII characters unescaped). Recommended, because it survives middleware that re-encodes the body.

WebhookSignatureSimple.name: X-Signature-Simple
WebhookSignatureSimple.description: Lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the destination's secret, of `{timestamp}:{session_id}:{status}:{webhook_type}` (missing fields as empty strings). Covers the envelope only, never the payload.

WebhookTimestamp.name: X-Timestamp
WebhookTimestamp.description: Unix time in seconds, equal to the body's `timestamp`. Reject deliveries older than a few minutes.

post.description: A verification session changed status. `decision` is sent only for `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review` and `Abandoned`; it has the shape of `GET /v3/session/{sessionId}/decision/` for destinations on webhook version 3 (the default), and the older reduced shape for version 1 or 2 destinations. Business sessions always receive the version 3 business decision.

2XX.description: Any 2xx response acknowledges the delivery. Other responses and timeouts are retried; see https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks.

post.description: Data of a verification session changed without a status change, for example after a manual review edit, a step override or an ongoing-monitoring rescreen. `decision` is sent only for `Approved`, `Declined`, `In Review` and `Abandoned`; it has the shape of `GET /v3/session/{sessionId}/decision/` for destinations on webhook version 3 (the default), and the older reduced shape for version 1 or 2 destinations. Business sessions always receive the version 3 business decision.

2XX.description: Any 2xx response acknowledges the delivery. Other responses and timeouts are retried; see https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks.

post.description: A user changed status. Not sent when the user is created.

2XX.description: Any 2xx response acknowledges the delivery. Other responses and timeouts are retried; see https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks.

post.description: Fields of a user changed. Not sent when the user is created. One save can produce both a status and a data event.

2XX.description: Any 2xx response acknowledges the delivery. Other responses and timeouts are retried; see https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks.

post.description: A business changed status. Not sent when the business is created.

2XX.description: Any 2xx response acknowledges the delivery. Other responses and timeouts are retried; see https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks.

post.description: Fields of a business changed. Not sent when the business is created. One save can produce both a status and a data event.

2XX.description: Any 2xx response acknowledges the delivery. Other responses and timeouts are retried; see https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks.

post.description: A transaction was created and screened. Sent for live applications only.

2XX.description: Any 2xx response acknowledges the delivery. Other responses and timeouts are retried; see https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks.

post.description: A transaction changed status, from a rule, a review or an end-user action. Sent for live applications only.

2XX.description: Any 2xx response acknowledges the delivery. Other responses and timeouts are retried; see https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks.

post.description: A Travel Rule exchange changed status. Sent on every transition up to and including `FINISHED`, `CANCELLED` or `EXPIRED`, never after. Sent for live applications only. There is no top-level `status`.

2XX.description: Any 2xx response acknowledges the delivery. Other responses and timeouts are retried; see https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks.

post.description: The compliance status of a published workflow changed after a re-evaluation. One event per workflow. There is no top-level `status`.

2XX.description: Any 2xx response acknowledges the delivery. Other responses and timeouts are retried; see https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks.

post.description: Body of the callback sent to the `webhook_url` of `POST /v3/kyb/search/` once the registry search resolves. It is not signed: the request carries `X-Didit-Unsigned-Callback: true` and none of the signature headers, so confirm it by matching `request_id` against a search you started. Uses `event_type`, not `webhook_type`.

2XX.description: Any 2xx response acknowledges the delivery. Other responses and timeouts are retried; see https://docs.didit.me/integration/webhooks.
